- Badges are agent-owned and ignorable: The agent may add, revise, or remove tangent badges as quick informational flags. Users do not edit or approve badges and may ignore them. Badges never constrain tangent selection or become canonical specification authority.

- Show every in-scope tangent in a flat frontier: The tangent selection surface lists every Proposed, Tracked, Active, and Deferred tangent in one flat collection with badges. Out-of-scope and Closed tangents are omitted from the default frontier.

- Keep the datastore renderer-neutral and resolve outcomes directly: The brainstorm datastore contains no Lavish concepts and no raw feedback collection. It stores renderer-neutral questions, proposals, review packets, decisions, and lifecycle state. The agent may present a review as ordinary Markdown or send the same packet to an optional renderer. After any response channel, the agent interprets user meaning and calls dag_brainstorm_resolve_review with semantic outcomes only.

- Review next actions may suggest optional Lavish rendering: dag_brainstorm_review may return a non-binding next suggestion to present the packet as ordinary Markdown or send it to an optional Lavish renderer. The renderer and its feedback transport never become datastore concepts.

- Let the agent choose the most useful question-context representation: The complete brainstorm-turn document may still use a consistent optional Lavish renderer whose stable shell owns Current understanding, navigation, question cards, badges, standard choices, comments, and turn-level actions. Within each question/review point, the freeform context section is flexible rather than one mandatory renderer-neutral shape: the agent may use ordinary Markdown, predefined semantic blocks, arbitrary HTML/CSS, scripts, or a linked/generated artifact such as an interactive web UI mockup. The workflow must not force every context section to be expressible in every renderer.

- Treat agent-authored brainstorm context as trusted local content: Do not require fragment sanitization, sandboxing, Shadow DOM, CSS scoping, or a security allowlist for agent-authored brainstorm context. The workflow assumes the user and agent are the local authors/readers. Renderers may still apply ordinary layout containment, diagnostics, or namespacing for usability, but not as a restriction on expressive capability.

- Allow fully interactive agent-authored context: Agent-authored context may include scripts, forms, editable controls, interactive prototypes, custom buttons, visualizations, and direct renderer integrations when they help communicate or test an idea. Renderer-provided review controls remain available for common decisions but are not the exclusive interaction mechanism. Any response delivered through custom context is still interpreted by the agent; verbatim responses and unprocessed submissions are not persisted in brainstorm state.

- Require session-level modality choice, not per-context fallback parity: A context section does not require a decision-complete Markdown fallback and rich rendering may carry modality-specific information. The workflow itself must not require Lavish: when the user or agent chooses a Markdown-only session, the agent provides suitable Markdown, a crude textual mockup, or a link to a separately opened artifact. Behavioral compatibility is chosen for the current interaction rather than imposed on every authored context section.

- Offer a small optional semantic component vocabulary: Provide markdown, callout, code, table, comparison, diagram, and freeform context helpers for common presentation. Renderer-owned review cards, understanding, options, recommendations, comments, navigation, and submission remain convenient defaults. These helpers reduce boilerplate but never limit the agent from authoring arbitrary HTML/CSS/scripts or linked artifacts when a brainstorm needs more expressive context.

- Explore the turn-to-Lavish rendering engine in a separate tangent: Do not settle the detailed renderer test contract inside production validation yet. Create a dedicated tangent for the engine that converts Current understanding, turn shell, review points, standard controls, and freeform question context into a whole-document Lavish artifact and transports submissions back to the agent. Define automated renderer validation after that engine's architecture and seams are understood.
discoveries.implications: The renderer frontier is settled for a bounded vertical implementation: a separate presentation adapter, tested optional Lavish CLI dependency, whole-turn projection/shell/lifecycle, bounded human-initiated feedback, and semantic resolution through existing model tools.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Implement and dogfood a vertical renderer prototype before refining secondary shell components or broader renderer automation.
discoveries.title: Deferred turn-to-Lavish renderer details

discoveries.body: When the launch CWD is explicitly bound as the sole conductor worktree for a session, its exact common-dir/worktree-admin identity, branch ref, HEAD/index/tree, and clean state can be fenced by the run. After proposal verification, the conductor can invoke an ordinary fast-forward from that worktree so Git updates branch, index, and files together. This avoids the raw `update-ref` stale-index hazard. Concurrent sessions sharing that worktree, branch switches, dirty state, or target drift must block; node workers remain in separate detached/private worktrees.
discoveries.title: A designated session worktree can safely replace external user handoff

discoveries.body: After the partially resolved Lavish review left one continuation point, the user selected its recommended option through a fresh direct chat question. `dag_model_record_direction` correctly accepted the exact decision and synchronized the generated spec, but the active review still contains the now-answered point. `dag_model_resolve_review` cannot clear it because the continuation itself was never presented successfully. The model question and tension can be marked answered/resolved, yet the disposable review frontier remains stale.
discoveries.implications: Exact direct directions now reconcile matching fresh active-review points transactionally, and session startup removes preexisting points whose reviewed semantic result is already receipt-valid.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Monitor field use for ambiguous non-equivalent direct responses.
discoveries.title: Direct direction does not reconcile an equivalent active review point

discoveries.body: Accepted v1 disables future-prefix speculation and adaptive F1 fanout. A zero speculative invalidation numerator therefore has no exposure denominator and cannot be presented as a successful 0% invalidation rate. Evaluation ratios need states such as measured, zero_exposure, unsupported_policy, not_observed, partial_coverage, and censored, with explicit numerator, denominator, missing, and censored counts. This applies to every absent capability or unexercised scenario.
discoveries.title: Metrics for disabled behavior must report unsupported policy rather than zero success

discoveries.body: The external `.ai` archive was 12.66 GB and dominated by complete source/dependency trees nested under run worktrees; individual run trees contained hundreds of thousands of copied files. Durable execution state should reference commits and bounded content-addressed evidence while worktrees live in disposable storage excluded from backup.
discoveries.implications: The canonical run store and widget must remain compact; artifacts are explicit bounded references, never recursive worktree archives.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Choose run/worktree paths and cleanup/quarantine policy during execution-state design.
discoveries.title: Durable run metadata must exclude disposable worktrees

discoveries.body: Primary sources strongly support its individual mechanisms and most failure transitions, but do not converge on implementation before all new tests, architecture review strictly after broad regression, or hardening strictly after review. Those are reasonable opinionated orchestration choices whose field effectiveness should be measured rather than presented as settled research fact.
discoveries.implications: Adopt the fixed loop as an explicit product decision and instrument it; cite prior art for components, not as proof of the exact sequence.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Capture phase duration, back-edges, invalidations, hardening yield, and review findings during dogfood runs.
discoveries.title: The exact proposed node loop is a composed design, not an established standard

discoveries.body: A precedence graph can be acyclic while a runtime gate requires evidence produced by a phase that the same gate blocks. Plan validation must expand work-to-gate evidence dependencies and gate-to-blocked-phase arcs, reject closed SCCs without a genuinely external release path, and keep mutexes/integration order out of causal-cycle analysis. Discovering this only as an empty runtime frontier is too late.
discoveries.title: Static cycle validation must include runtime-gate evidence producers

discoveries.body: If a detached worker writes and the manager ingests a terminal result before late supervisor PID binding completes, the prior launch path unconditionally reset attempt and worker status to running. The launch binding mutation now attaches previously absent supervisor PID/start-identity facts but updates lifecycle status only when the same attempt is still current and nonterminal; its return status reflects preserved state. A deterministic injected-supervisor fixture writes and ingests a valid terminal result before returning its process handle, then proves late identity binding leaves both launch and worker status succeeded while retaining supervisor identity.
discoveries.title: Fast worker result can be overwritten back to running

discoveries.body: Archived runs show path declarations helped reviewers detect unrelated edits and predict shared-registry conflicts; one Home Manager recovery succeeded by preserving unrelated entries and changing only the expected wiring file. But path restrictions also become stale, omit generated or architectural work, and can force poor designs. The reconciled role is predicted/observed change evidence plus review and scope-expansion triggers—not a hard write sandbox or proof of parallel independence.
discoveries.implications: Node contracts should declare semantic outcomes/effects and advisory expected paths. Unexpected paths require explanation and possibly architecture/integration review; they are not automatically forbidden. Shared predicted paths raise a risk signal but typed semantic constraints decide scheduling.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Define path-diff attestations and explicit scope-expansion escalation within the fixed lifecycle.
discoveries.title: File scope is useful evidence but dangerous authority

discoveries.body: Mutable booleans and matching attempt/receipt fields are insufficient for completion unless the run also resolves the exact predecessor prefix, plan-authorized composition/prefix/final profiles, immutable verification facts, every acceptance-oracle assertion's procedure and environment result, the sole legal post-F3 evidence-adoption transition, and the exact work-item effect-scope replay contract.
discoveries.implications: Closed by exact composition/prefix/final profile hashes and verification facts, F2 oracle assertion facts, one-generation post-F3 delta-attested adoption, item-local provider/kind/replay effect scopes, exact observed train targets, and year-zero-safe RFC 3339 arithmetic.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Implement all five repairs, add focused adversarial fixtures, obtain a bounded final rereview, and only then commit the schema slice.
discoveries.title: Completion needs exact integration profiles, oracle assertions, adoption lineage, and effect-scope closure

discoveries.body: `DEC-defer-worker-widget-until-dag-redesign` explicitly supersedes `DEC-passive-live-dag-widget-v1`, but `spec/owned-worker-runtime/spec.md` renders both as governing direction. The projector's `isSpecEligible` checks accepted state and receipt hash only; it does not exclude objects targeted by an accepted `supersedes` relationship. Projection validation also requires every accepted receipt-valid object to retain canonical placement. The same issue leaves older per-run/DAG-coupled worker wording visible beside newer session-scoped DAG-agnostic decisions.
discoveries.implications: Projection eligibility now excludes accepted objects targeted by receipt-valid accepted `supersedes` relationships; governing context and cross-spec links use the same effective set.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Monitor future supersession chains in model tests.
discoveries.title: Generated specs still render superseded accepted decisions

discoveries.body: A real fixture produced a clean composition while predecessor and candidate tests became behaviorally incompatible in the combined tree. Target movement, predecessor reorder/replacement, or any changed prefix identity must therefore invalidate combined-state evidence and rerun exact-prefix profiles; clean rebase/merge, patch ID, ancestry, or equal isolated candidate evidence is only diagnostic.
discoveries.title: Clean Git composition does not preserve behavioral evidence

discoveries.body: Risk hardening can expose different failures: sanitizer crashes, races, security flaws, performance/robustness defects, or invalid boundary behavior are product defects and return to implementation before mandatory codification; a meaningful surviving mutant may indicate only a test-sensitivity gap and return directly to codification; an architectural flaw may require review/replan; equivalent mutants or accepted limits need disposition; tool/environment failures become blocked rather than product edits.
discoveries.implications: The lifecycle diagram and transition contract must route by finding class. Hardening never skips implementation when production code is defective, and every repaired defect still passes through codification and accumulated verification.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Define the hardening finding enum and routing table in the execution schema.
discoveries.title: Hardening findings need typed routing rather than one back-edge

discoveries.body: Historical data proves recurring failure classes and supplies scenario shapes, but run survival and state quality are heterogeneous: local audit found 22 named IDs but only nine surviving directories and one coherently completed run; external audit classified 24 state-backed runs but included stale, duplicate, abandoned, unfinalized, and partially merged states. Legacy readiness, completion, retries, worker identity, validation, and integration semantics differ from v1. Retrospective rates or duration comparisons would be selection-biased and definitionally incomparable. Use the audits to pre-register failure scenarios, then establish prospective v1 baselines.
discoveries.title: Historical DAG audits cannot supply a trustworthy quantitative before/after baseline

discoveries.body: The first vertical topology prototype was readable but too tall for a persistent terminal widget. Review feedback asks whether a left-to-right slice can preserve edge visibility, statuses, and running-work detail in substantially fewer rows.
discoveries.implications: Compare horizontal and adaptive orientations at realistic 50-, 80-, and 120-column widths. Orientation may need to switch by available width and graph shape rather than be globally fixed.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Prototype a compact horizontal slice now, then compare narrow fallback and high fan-in/fan-out cases in later review turns.
discoveries.title: A horizontal topology slice may fit the Pi widget better

discoveries.body: Horizontal chains can show a small active neighborhood in fewer rows, matching earlier feedback, but high fan-in/fan-out and long annotations consume columns quickly. Git, systemd, Argo, and pstree instead keep one node per row with topology connectors in a separate gutter, making status and facts easier to align while spending more rows. Narrow adjacency rows are the safest fallback. The final contract should compare these at realistic widths and graph shapes, not select orientation from prose.
discoveries.title: Horizontal chains and one-node-per-row topology gutters have different persistent-widget strengths

discoveries.body: Human decision elapsed time is dominated by user availability, and provider-reported cost varies by model, pricing, cache semantics, retries, and missing usage fields. Record exact counts, timestamps, model/provider, tokens, reported cost, and coverage when available, but compare like-for-like and never treat latency/cost as scheduler inputs or lifecycle ceilings. Human intervention count and autonomous-span duration are more interpretable burden signals; semantic prompt quality remains a separate later corpus/rubric exercise under `COM-semantic-evaluation`.
discoveries.title: Human latency and model cost are contextual diagnostics, not success budgets

discoveries.body: Historical validators caught semantic, preservation, API/UI, path-safety, test-coverage, and architecture defects that executor self-checks missed. Multiple nodes failed review, looped through targeted recovery, and then passed. Parent-side verification also caught merged-state issues. Conversely, prose-only `Done.` output and fragile verdict parsing were unusable.
discoveries.implications: Keep evaluation/review independent from implementation where feasible, use typed evidence and findings, and codify fixed failures before a clean rerun. Do not collapse all checks into executor self-validation.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Specify which fixed phases require a fresh worker/context and how findings bind to repair attempts.
discoveries.title: Independent validation produced real recovery value

discoveries.body: Structural closure and root hashing do not prove execution invariants. The initial implementation can accept arbitrary evidence refs as stage passage, detach integration readiness from F8 and the current candidate, permit suffix integration ahead of the train head, and release sticky lanes without a terminal item disposition. Canonical JSON also loses `__proto__` when ordinary objects are used as parser/canonicalizer outputs.
discoveries.implications: Closed in the strict canonical schema implementation: dangerous keys are preserved/rejected, all stage and completion claims require exact plan/fact joins, train suffixes cannot speculate, and sticky lane identity is durable.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Repair canonical JSON, make precedence integration-only, encode the accepted merge-tree strategy, add plan/fact-aware validation, enforce exact F0–F8/current-candidate/train-head/sticky-lane invariants, and codify every adversarial probe.
discoveries.title: Initial canonical schemas need exact plan, fact, lifecycle, train, and lane joins

discoveries.body: The accepted per-repository integration lock spans authoritative composition through exact checks and receipt acceptance, but integration trains explicitly do not imply authoring precedence. Scheduler capacity must model integration as a repository-scoped resource/queue distinct from F1 authoring, F2/F5 independent evaluation, deterministic checks, and provider capacity; otherwise one long integration attempt would unnecessarily serialize all candidate creation.
discoveries.title: Long integration locks are a separate bottleneck from authoring capacity

discoveries.body: The terminal-state race fix guards only ingested or terminal attempts. If cancellation changes the current worker to `cancelling` while launch waits for supervisor identity, the later launch mutation can set it back to `running`; cancellation escalation then exits because the worker no longer appears cancelling.
discoveries.implications: Launch identity binding must enrich identity without overwriting cancellation/control intent, and a delayed-binding cancellation fixture is required.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Preserve cancelling state in late launch binding and prove escalation remains armed under the race.
discoveries.title: Late worker identity binding can overwrite a concurrent cancellation

discoveries.body: The first real open detected the visually hidden skip link as viewport-unreachable and detected exact authority payloads nested inside radio labels as clipped text. Moving details outside labels and using a standard clip-path skip-link pattern removed the findings. Fixture/string scenarios had passed before the browser audit, so production validation should retain one real-browser layout gate in addition to deterministic renderer tests.
discoveries.title: Lavish browser audit catches control failures invisible to string tests

discoveries.body: Implementation exposed and resolved several details that were too small for product-level review: standard controls must carry review, point, option, and semantic hashes; entering freeform text alongside a selected option is a modification, not acceptance; real Lavish output may encode homogeneous warnings as compact TOON tables; resume must render/open when disposable files are missing; user-ended state must survive review rerendering; exact payload disclosure belongs outside radio labels to avoid clipped interactive content; and the browser layout gate catches failures deterministic string tests miss. These are now executable prototype behavior.
discoveries.title: Prototype resolves the first concrete renderer seams

discoveries.body: When a representative second decision was added to prove multi-decision rendering, the human reasonably asked whether its feedback-cap question was fake and selected another fixture option. Although prototype documentation already said the artifact was non-authoritative, the page itself looked like an active review. The sample now carries a prominent Prototype fixture status and notice that queued choices validate interaction only and never resolve the repository model. Representative questions explain which part is illustrative and why the underlying production concern exists.
discoveries.title: Interactive renderer fixtures must be unmistakably non-authoritative

discoveries.body: The retained legacy `appendEvent` helper reads all of `.ai/runs/<run-id>/events.jsonl`, concatenates one line, and rewrites the entire file for every event. It currently has no call sites because mutating execution tools are disabled, but reusing it in the owned runtime would create quadratic I/O and reproduce the same resource class the new runtime is meant to eliminate. The owned runtime needs bounded append or compact snapshots, not read-concatenate-rewrite logging.
discoveries.title: Legacy DAG appendEvent performs quadratic whole-file rewrites

discoveries.body: Reuse graph/readiness algorithms, deterministic diagram layout, worktree/rebase mechanics, evidence-classification prompts, and semantic decomposition heuristics only behind new contracts. Do not restore prose authority, arbitrary lifecycle flows, manual worker-result relay, advisory transitions, regex verdicts, duplicate topology representations, or pre-rebase-only validation.
discoveries.implications: The redesign should adapt dormant mechanics around the owned worker runtime and a new atomic model-bound DAG snapshot rather than reactivate the old conductor.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Specify canonical planning input, graph, stage/evidence, run-state, Git integration, reconciliation, telemetry, and live-projection contracts before mutating DAG commands return.
discoveries.title: Legacy DAG mechanics are reusable but its control plane is not

discoveries.body: Historical runs reached thousands of starts/results and hundreds of attempts. Parallel orchestration repeatedly produced corrupt JSON, duplicate worktree/start errors, stale worker results, Git lock/rebase conflicts, manual state repairs, and run manifests inconsistent with node truth. One local run has 113 attempts for eight nodes; another has 93 attempts for 24 nodes.
discoveries.implications: The new DAG conductor needs one atomic revisioned run snapshot, serialized mutations, idempotent claim/start/ingest transitions, immutable attempt identity, explicit recovery/abandonment, and serialized integration. The owned worker kernel solves only the generic worker part.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Design DAG attempt binding and conductor recovery without duplicating worker-session authority.
discoveries.title: Real DAG scale exposed non-atomic shared-state failures

discoveries.body: A stable widget architecture has two pure boundaries: first join immutable plan topology, one exact atomic run snapshot, and only explicitly mapped worker/repository/fact inputs into `DagExecutionProjectionV1`; then render that projection under width, row budget, ASCII profile, and explicit observation-time bucket. This keeps layout policy from becoming execution authority and permits commands, RPC summaries, full diagrams, and the persistent widget to share one semantic projection without sharing one layout.
discoveries.title: Semantic execution projection and terminal layout need separate versioned contracts

discoveries.body: The accepted passive DAG widget and its open projection question assume a live conductor-owned `RunState`, readiness frontier, node transitions, and `/dag` mutation controls. The newer accepted boundary explicitly removes those responsibilities from the subagent runtime and defers DAG redesign. The current extension has only static legacy `DagFile` rendering and read-only legacy DAG commands. Therefore the next implementable UI frontier is a generic per-session worker activity surface; live DAG topology should wait for a future DAG adapter and canonical DAG state.
discoveries.implications: Persistent worker and DAG widgets are out of the subagent-runtime scope. The widget contract is revisited only after the canonical DAG schema and adapter are designed.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Proceed with headless worker runtime and explicit commands/tools; keep static legacy DAG diagram read-only.
discoveries.title: The live DAG widget frontier is premature after decoupling subagents from DAG orchestration

discoveries.body: Established implementations either omit the recursive tool by default or bound it with depth/cycle guards. V1 has no need for worker-owned nested queues, routing, or budgets. If field use requires nested fanout later, expose a child-safe `subagent` variant only for explicitly assigned fanout and add depth, cycle, ownership, and completion routing contracts then.
discoveries.implications: Do not initialize nested worker runtimes or expose the recursive launch tool in ordinary v1 children.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Reopen when a concrete delegated task needs child-controlled fanout that cannot be orchestrated by the top-level agent.
discoveries.title: Nested subagent fanout remains an explicit future opt-in

discoveries.body: The legacy merger rebased and fast-forwarded a node after its validator had passed, without rerunning tests against newly integrated sibling changes. The proposed lifecycle therefore needs an integration-ready state distinct from complete, followed by post-rebase or fan-in verification before merge completion.
discoveries.implications: The fixed node loop must include an integration gate or define a separate graph-level integration-verification phase; success in an isolated worktree is insufficient.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Decide where post-rebase and fan-in checks live and which failures return to node implementation versus an integration node.
discoveries.title: A node cannot complete on pre-integration verification alone

discoveries.body: The legacy flow exposed orchestration as multiple model calls: discover next action, start a node, ask a separate subagent tool to launch, wait for package notification, and record the result in another call. This creates partial states and makes completion delivery dependent on the main agent interpreting tool output correctly. An owned async conductor should atomically claim a ready step, persist worker identity, launch it, ingest one terminal result idempotently, advance/fail the DAG, and wake the main agent with the resulting transition.
discoveries.implications: The generic worker runtime still needs serialized worker-session state, but it must not own DAG transitions. DAG orchestration remains a separate future adapter.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Reuse worker state and completion APIs from the future DAG redesign without embedding DAG semantics in the subagent runtime.
discoveries.title: Owned runtime should replace agent-mediated launch/result choreography

discoveries.body: The extension now owns a process-isolated always-asynchronous Pi RPC worker runtime under `extensions/dag-workflow/worker-runtime/`. It persists one atomic session snapshot, launches detached supervisors, filters child orchestration tools, captures terminating `subagent_report` results, performs bounded report repairs, derives immutable terminal envelopes, recovers with PID/start and attempt-generation checks, transfers direct forks, drains compact completions serially, and exposes generic tools plus `/workers`. The dormant `dag_subagent` adapter and `pi-subagents` dependency are removed. Fake RPC tests cover reporting, repair exhaustion, cancellation, failure precedence, corrupt-result recovery, reload redelivery, direct-fork transfer, retry, and bounded logging; a real installed-Pi RPC worker completed with a valid structured report.
discoveries.implications: The headless owned-worker scope is implemented. Runtime field use can now evaluate prompts and operational ergonomics; persistent DAG visualization remains separately deferred.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Reload Pi to activate the new parent manager in this conversation, then dogfood `subagent` and `/workers` before designing canonical DAG execution state.
discoveries.title: Owned asynchronous worker runtime is implemented and validated

discoveries.body: Two nodes may safely investigate, implement, and review in isolated worktrees while still requiring a fixed merge or deployment order. Zuul/GitLab-style trains can test ordered future prefixes concurrently and invalidate downstream results after a predecessor changes or fails.
discoveries.implications: Do not encode integration order as an early implementation dependency unless the later node truly consumes the earlier result. The canonical run state needs separate implementation readiness and integration readiness.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Prototype prefix validation and adaptive fanout after the canonical graph/state contract is accepted.
discoveries.title: Parallel authoring and ordered integration are distinct

discoveries.body: Disjoint files can share an API, schema, invariant, unresolved architecture decision, generated source, runtime resource, or integration failure. Overlapping files can contain commutative or structurally mergeable edits. Path predictions also change during implementation. Use paths for review routing, risk scoring, targeted tests, and merge simulation—not as hard worker boundaries or proof of independence.
discoveries.implications: Remove `ownedFiles` and `forbiddenFiles` from the decision-bearing parallelism contract; retain predicted and observed paths only as advisory evidence and integration diagnostics.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Include unexpected changed paths in architecture/integration review rather than automatically failing a node.
discoveries.title: Path overlap is neither necessary nor sufficient for parallel incompatibility

discoveries.body: The exact design proposes an immutable content-addressed `SchedulerDecisionReceiptV1` for every nonempty reservation batch. Accepted artifact policy limits hashing to durable cross-boundary context and promoted phase evidence while leaving transient diagnostics unhashed by default. Atomic reservations and persisted launch/effect intents already own execution correctness, and deterministic ready/admission projections can explain the current choice. V1 should justify a durable audit/recovery need before turning every priority decision into an immutable artifact; otherwise only authority-bearing overrides, policy changes, or attention-required decisions should be promoted.
discoveries.title: Per-batch scheduler receipts may over-promote deterministic transient diagnostics

discoveries.body: Pi has no core subagent-summary guarantee. The official subagent example prompts a separate Pi process, collects completed messages, and scans backward for the last assistant text block; absent text becomes `(no output)`. `terminate: true` only makes a structured tool final if the model chooses to call it—it does not force the call. Stronger extensions add prompt contracts, validated result tools, completion guards, or repair turns. The owned runtime's `subagent_report` plus missing-report repair is therefore an intentional reliability layer beyond Pi's example.
discoveries.implications: Do not describe report invocation as Pi-enforced. Tests must cover omission, invalid arguments, report-only repair, and final report-missing fallback.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Keep one bounded repair decision in the active terminal-result review.
discoveries.title: Pi core does not guarantee that a child emits a summary

discoveries.body: `pi-subagents` collects completed child messages and `getFinalOutput()` scans backward for the last non-empty assistant text block, skipping assistant error messages. Foreground completion returns that text, a file-only output reference, an error, or `(no output)`; the background runner can also fall back to raw stdout lines. It does not require a terminating summary tool. Its separate completion guard only detects implementation-like tasks that exited successfully without an observed mutation attempt and can mark those as failed/needs-attention; it does not guarantee summary production.
discoveries.implications: The owned runtime's required `subagent_report` plus bounded repair is deliberately stronger and more deterministic than `pi-subagents` final-text extraction.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Keep fallback final text for diagnostics, but never treat it as equivalent to a valid structured report.
discoveries.title: `pi-subagents` does not force a structured summary

discoveries.body: The user's authorization concern and subsequent acceptance establish an important schema requirement: plan authorization coordinates exact reviewed semantic work, repository/effect classes, irreversible boundaries, validity, and broad budgets; it does not constrain files, directories, symbols, modules, abstractions, or internal design. The default authorization should cover all reversible local implementation/evaluation work for the reviewed plan, while separate gates are reserved for materially new semantic scope, another repository not already declared, external/live effects, integration/landing, or deployment.
discoveries.title: Plan authorization must remain broad coordination, not a code architecture sandbox

discoveries.body: The new focus seed asks for a user-transparent planning/chunking boundary: `/dag plan` should write the human-readable plan and compile the executable DAG, with a way to show the graph. This does not introduce a conflicting direction; it operationalizes accepted decisions for one canonical two-phase artifact and deterministic human-readable/static graph projections. The unresolved frontier is command lifecycle and inspection UX, not whether chunking is separately user-facing.
discoveries.title: New planning focus aligns with the accepted one-command two-phase contract

discoveries.body: `git merge-tree --write-tree <prefix> <candidate>` followed by deterministic `git commit-tree <tree> -p <prefix>` creates an exact one-parent integration candidate without mutating an index, branch, or rebase/cherry-pick sequencer. Private refs can protect inputs and outputs, and repeated fixed-metadata composition should reproduce the commit/tree. This intentionally discards worker commit topology and still requires exact-prefix behavioral verification; conflicts route to a new candidate rather than conductor resolution.
discoveries.title: Plumbing composition can remove mutable rebase and cherry-pick recovery state

discoveries.body: The production `dag_model_present_review` path previously called pinned `lavish-axi` directly with the artifact path and relied on its default browser opening, so a review could report open without appearing in the dedicated Lavish Chromium window. `LavishCliAdapter.open` now routes interactive opens and explicit reopens through configurable `lavish-open`, while `noOpen` mode and all poll/end operations continue through the pinned optional `lavish-axi` CLI. Regression coverage proves the helper receives the exact file plus `--reopen` and that no-open test/headless behavior bypasses the browser helper. The renderer also now constrains flex/grid identities to prevent the horizontal overflow observed during the same review.
discoveries.title: Review presentation bypasses the dedicated Lavish browser helper

discoveries.body: `ProjectModelStore.mutate()` and focus-session mutation load a revision and later rename a replacement without a process-shared lock or expected-revision comparison. Two ordinary Pi processes can both read revision N and each publish N+1, silently losing one update. Existing before/after model hashes do not prevent this. The practical fix is shared locking or a database transaction plus expected integer revision and durable temp-fsync/rename/parent-fsync.
discoveries.title: Project-model and focus stores can lose concurrent updates

discoveries.body: Archived attempts failed deterministically because an explicitly requested Anthropic model lacked credentials, worktrees were stale or missing dependencies, test commands resolved the wrong environment, and negative searches were misclassified as shell failures. These are not implementation defects and should not consume the same retry budget.
discoveries.implications: P0/P2 and scheduler launch need provider/tool/environment capability preflight, typed infrastructure failure, fallback policy, and separate retry counters.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Define global model/capability resolution and environment hydration in the execution contract.
discoveries.title: Provider and environment failures need preflight rather than product retries

discoveries.body: Per-node infrastructure or replacement retry ceilings do not prevent a fanout wave from amplifying one provider, credential, capability, endpoint, or region outage into correlated launches. A deterministic circuit keyed by the normalized failure domain should open immediately for hard auth/capability failure or after matching transient failures, suppress new dispatch, allow one explicit half-open probe, and close only from an accepted success/health observation rather than elapsed time.
discoveries.title: Provider outages require a shared failure-domain circuit

discoveries.body: Installed-runtime dogfooding held a cancelled attempt-1 completion behind another in-flight completion, retried the same worker, and then received the attempt-1 completion ID with attempt-2 success content. `WorkerManager.inspect(completionId)` found the owning worker but always selected its current attempt. It now resolves the exact attempt carrying that completion ID, while worker-ID inspection continues to select the current attempt. Regression coverage verifies historical completion inspection remains bound after retry.
discoveries.implications: Serial queue identity and payload now refer to the same immutable attempt result even when a worker is retried before an older queued completion is delivered.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Run the focused worker tests and repeat installed cancellation/retry dogfooding after the correction is installed.
discoveries.title: Queued historical completion initially rendered the latest retry attempt

discoveries.body: Because the user selected the conductor agent as the only control plane, persistent widget hints should not look like clickable controls or teach direct mutation commands. A bounded footer can say `ask conductor: explain N07` or `ask conductor for full graph`; the conductor chooses exact read or guarded mutation tools. Agent tools remain explicit and typed internally, but the widget is status, not a command menu.
discoveries.title: Read-only widget hints should tell the user what to ask the conductor

discoveries.body: The workflow needs enough stable identity to resume after crashes, reject stale writes, avoid duplicated effects, and explain what plan, run, or result is being discussed. But the trusted agent can fabricate or misuse any in-process receipt, so byte-exact interaction proofs and cryptographic-style chains do not create a meaningful security boundary. Every hash or receipt must be justified by a concrete preventable reliability failure rather than generic tamper-resistance language, and simpler revisions, IDs, CAS, or direct joins should replace hashes where sufficient.
discoveries.title: Reliability identity must not be presented as a security boundary

discoveries.body: During iterative lifecycle review, a candidate decision changed after presentation. `refreshReviewPoint` refreshed reference/option hashes but retained the option's old materialized authority payload, so the revised visible choice could not resolve correctly. The kernel now preserves each existing-target direction's original explicit value patch as private focus-session metadata, rematerializes the public exact direction from the current model target plus that patch on every unresolved-review refresh, strips private metadata from review projections and hashes, and preserves it across partial resolution. Legacy directions without metadata safely rematerialize from the current target. Deterministic tests cover no-patch refresh, explicit-patch refresh, repeated refresh, private/public separation, and successful acceptance of the current payload.
discoveries.implications: Iterative reviews of mutable candidates can now refresh exact authority payloads safely. New-object directions remain immutable, existing-target explicit overrides remain intentional, and every rematerialized payload still requires fresh presentation before acceptance.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Continue field use and retain stale-point visibility; no additional kernel repair is currently required.
discoveries.title: Review refresh updates hashes but not an existing object's direction payload

discoveries.body: `dag_model_review` returns the exact review Markdown as a visible tool result, but the Pi adapter marks presentation only when a later assistant text message contains the entire Markdown verbatim. The user responded to the visible review, yet `dag_model_resolve_review` rejected it as unpresented. The manual recovery used the domain presentation marker. Production should recognize the exact tool result/turn delivery itself, or store a tool-result-bound presentation receipt, rather than require a large verbatim assistant echo.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Intentionally ignored by direct user request; do not pursue unless explicitly reopened.
sourceRefs: Live focus review-lavish-renderer-architecture failure and recovery
discoveries.title: Visible review tool output is not recognized as presentation

discoveries.body: A global revision change may be unrelated, while a newly added governing object can invalidate a plan without changing any previously referenced object. Useful fail-closed revalidation therefore needs both full snapshot identity and a versioned, reproducible semantic selector/closure hash that includes effective authority and transitive governing relationships; unknown impact blocks.
discoveries.title: Model revision alone cannot prove plan staleness

discoveries.body: A process-shared directory lock, pure reducer, atomic rename, and passing happy-path tests are insufficient unless the store confines run namespaces, binds every owner transition to immutable process/lineage evidence, makes takeover resumable after every crash point, verifies predecessor and immutable-fact references, and prevents any new non-recovery effect after a cancellation fence. Cancellation must preserve sticky lanes and uncertain resources while coherently fencing reservations, effects, train entries, and per-work-item generations.
discoveries.implications: Task 109's foundational reducer/store boundary is now implemented and verified. Ownership is bound to the executing PID/start identity, explicit current-owner transfer, deterministic lineage, durable process observations, owner epochs, and crash-resumable recovery. Cancellation now fences generations/effects first, rejects overlap and post-fence work, quarantines non-cancel terminal races without semantic pointers, and releases lanes/leases only after exact worker and effect reconciliation. Snapshot/archive/fact publication and liveness fail closed with resumable initialization, atomic lock retirement, stable read retry, and raw corruption retention.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Proceed to task 110 worker-runtime hardening; keep concrete worker ingestion, Git integration, and scheduler command families in their accepted downstream tasks.
discoveries.title: Run-state kernel needs crash-resumable proof-bound ownership and coherent cancellation

discoveries.body: The immutable plan and atomic run state already distinguish precedence, gates, mutexes, resources, leases, stages, authorization, freshness, effects, and integration. A node/stage can therefore be semantically ready yet not admitted because capacity or policy slots are unavailable. Conflating these states—as the legacy pending-plus-merged check does—would make heuristics look like correctness blockers and make widget explanations unstable. V1 needs a pure correctness frontier followed by deterministic reservation/admission ordering.
discoveries.title: Correctness readiness and capacity admission must be separate deterministic layers

discoveries.body: A run-local overlay may only narrow operations through holds, reduced capacity, quarantine, or phase-scoped exclusion. Discovering a missing producer dependency, semantic effect, architecture/contract gate, acceptance criterion, repository write, or migration phase reveals changed decomposition. Affected work must pause and a successor plan hash with fresh authorization must be produced; silently mutating the running graph exceeds authorization.
discoveries.title: Semantic dynamic edges require a new authorized plan

discoveries.body: Historical plan, chunk, and run commands were usually paired in the same conductor sessions. Their durable prose and graph files made complex work inspectable, but ignored `.ai` context was often absent from worktrees, root DAG files drifted after runs, and no typed binding prevented translation loss or stale execution. The evidence does not compare a unified alternative experimentally.
discoveries.implications: Preserve separate architecture-first and decomposition views while storing them in one versioned model-bound planning artifact and review transaction.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Ask the user to choose the one-artifact/two-phase workflow versus two independently reviewed artifacts.
discoveries.title: Separate plan and chunk artifacts added review value but not reliable authority

discoveries.body: A count-only worker ceiling does not bound invalidation cascades: branching descendants can create superlinear wasted work. Speculative exact-prefix work should classify green/amber/red, prohibit red, limit amber concurrently per run/repository, limit predecessor/causal distance, and fence the full affected generation closure before signaling cancellation. Ordinary authorized independent authoring is parallel work, not speculation.
discoveries.title: Speculation requires both concurrent credit and causal-distance bounds

discoveries.body: The earlier 4-total/2-F1/downstream-reserve profile assumed that a node leaving F1 released capacity that could admit another node while the first moved through F2–F8. The accepted sticky-lane model forbids that: every admitted node retains its lane through validation, repair, waits, and integration. Physical phase workers and resource demands still require exact leases, but they cannot increase the active-node set. Concurrency configuration can therefore be reduced to `maxActiveNodes` plus actual shared-resource/mutex capacities.
discoveries.title: Sticky node lanes remove the need for phase-level validation reserves

discoveries.body: Execution cannot depend on evaluation telemetry. A detached bounded evaluation envelope should bind plan/run/policy/source hashes, report coverage and missingness, and derive from the final/current snapshot plus immutable receipts and exact worker results. Telemetry write failure must not mutate or block an otherwise valid run; it creates an evaluation-coverage warning. Metrics never release gates, authorize retries, change scheduling, prove evidence, or become implicit time/token/cost budgets. Time-series measures not recoverable from retained natural-slot facts require either explicit bounded interval records in the canonical schema for operational correctness or a separate lossy diagnostic accumulator—not an event log.
discoveries.title: Telemetry must be non-authoritative, loss-tolerant, and regenerable from exact facts

discoveries.body: Independent adversarial review found that an instance-local fault latch would be lost on conductor service or process replacement, allowing session_start/timer activation to retry without explicit diagnosis. It also found that dirty wakes must preserve their own occurredAt rather than inherit the first pump timestamp. The follow-up patch now publishes a hash-validated durable per-run fault marker before rejecting callers, suppresses background resume across service replacement, removes the marker only through explicit retry, and tracks the latest dirty wake timestamp for successor passes.
discoveries.title: Terminal conductor faults require durable restart fencing

discoveries.body: Pi's structured-output pattern makes the tool call the final action in that Pi agent run and exposes its typed result to the caller/client. In the owned async architecture, the caller is the detached RPC supervisor—not the already-settled top-level agent. Therefore `subagent_report` itself supplies the worker summary and eliminates any extra child assistant response, but it does not replace durable result writing, parent watcher ingestion, serial queueing, or a later `pi.sendMessage(..., { deliverAs: "followUp", triggerTurn: true })` to wake the top-level agent. The supervisor should still wait for `agent_settled`, persist the immutable result, and close the child RPC process.
discoveries.implications: Describe `terminate: true` only as the child finalization boundary. Keep parent delivery as a separate durable pipeline because launches return immediately and the parent may be closed.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Clarify the active review so it does not imply Pi automatically bridges a terminating child tool result to the parent session.
discoveries.title: `terminate: true` ends the child turn but does not deliver across processes

discoveries.body: Field implementation demonstrated that one small focus-linked plan record plus a compatibility adapter is sufficient to expose plan/show/run without replacing the canonical scheduler, lifecycle, worker, Git, and run-state machinery. The necessary extra durability is limited to ordinary plan revisions, process-shared CAS, and one recoverable start intent; mandatory interaction receipt stacks or compilation manifests were not needed.
discoveries.title: The thin product workflow can reuse the shipped canonical runtime

discoveries.body: Review feedback identified that representing each static failure as a new top-level worker transition would repeatedly serialize child startup, context reconstruction, and completion delivery. The edit/static loop is high-frequency local feedback and should remain inside one implementation worker run.
discoveries.implications: The DAG state records the implementation bundle and its final/static evidence, while detailed internal iterations remain bounded worker diagnostics/evidence rather than separate scheduled nodes or worker launches.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Define which other adjacent checks can be internal without sacrificing independent evaluation or review.
discoveries.title: A top-level implementation/static back-edge would waste time and context

discoveries.body: `git update-ref <branch> <new> <old>` enforces ref identity but bypasses checked-worktree safety. A concurrent checkout/worktree-add scan races the CAS, and moving a checked branch leaves its index/files stale; a later ordinary commit can silently delete integrated content. Automated normal-branch landing therefore cannot be justified by a preflight checkout scan alone. Safe v1 options are explicit user handoff for normal repositories or CAS only for a declared bare/conductor-exclusive target.
discoveries.title: Expected-old ref CAS cannot protect uncontrolled checked-out worktrees

discoveries.body: Raw worker count, launches, active lanes, or elapsed-time reduction do not prove useful parallelism. A defensible measure combines exact overlap of independent active-node or operation intervals with whether candidates survive F2/F5/F7, avoid successor-plan correction for missing causality, integrate against exact prefixes, and retain accepted behavior. Conflict fencing, invalidated suffixes, rework, and waits by typed blocker explain lost parallel benefit. Higher concurrency is neither intrinsically good nor a scheduler input.
discoveries.title: Useful parallelism is overlap that survives evidence and integration

discoveries.body: After v0.1.2 was published/applied, the original Operant Pi hot reload did not re-register `/dag`; the session was cleanly stopped and old PID 3392234 proven dead. A fresh exact session called guarded `dag_run_reattach` once, advancing canonical authority from r17/epoch1 to r18/epoch2 without direct file edits. The same long response continued investigating, and queued reload/run inputs prevented a clean agent-settled boundary; F0 remained unsealed and F1 undispatched. SIGTERM then could not complete because async conductor detach drains the in-flight/queued pump, so the process required SIGKILL and epoch2 is now proven dead. This is operational evidence that recovery verification must isolate reattachment from long/queued agent work and that shutdown drain needs a bounded or cancellable path if a pump cannot settle.
discoveries.title: Operant proven-dead reattachment advanced ownership but the first recovery turn did not pump

discoveries.body: Scheduler terminology overloaded “downstream.” The protected capacity serves later F2/F4/F5/F6/F7/F8 and integration operations for nodes that already produced candidates. It does not make a separate causally dependent work item ready. Under the accepted rule, a true consumer B remains blocked from F0 onward until producer A has a current accepted integration receipt and reconciled conductor-branch landing. Future-prefix speculation likewise cannot start B early.
discoveries.title: Validation/drain capacity is not causal consumer release

discoveries.body: The Pi widget factory receives a public TUI with `terminal.rows`, while `render(width)` receives exact columns. A passive component can therefore cap itself to a deterministic share of visible rows and switch graph representations by width, without capturing keyboard focus or replacing the editor. This supports a compact persistent slice and keeps full inspection/control in explicit commands/tools.
discoveries.title: The persistent widget can adapt to terminal height without becoming an interactive panel

discoveries.body: Each service.status call already invokes workerManager.readBoundAttempts, which scans worker stores and returns processDisposition for the exact bound attempt. The current projection joins that fact but drops processDisposition from the node-facing worker tuple. A versioned projection can retain exact process disposition, while the widget controller records when it received the successful fresh status. Motion then requires both processDisposition=live and a recent successful controller observation; stale cached projections freeze without mutating canonical DAG state.
discoveries.implications: No renderer-local claim of process liveness and no new durable heartbeat field are required for the first implementation.
discoveries.title: Spinner authority can come from the existing exact worker scan without persisting UI heartbeat state

discoveries.body: Review feedback rejected a card-oriented research-worker surface as the design example. The Pi widget must be monospaced and show a useful slice of DAG edges with character/dot status marks for running, pending or blocked, and complete nodes, alongside a compact list of currently running work.
discoveries.implications: Prototype topology-first ASCII layouts at realistic Pi widths before accepting the final widget contract. Worker details are secondary annotations linked to nodes.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Present at least one concrete graph/list prototype and iterate through multiple review turns before implementation.
discoveries.title: The live widget's primary value is a topology slice, not worker cards

discoveries.body: The active review framed worker lifetime as session-scoped cancellation versus a durable daemon. Repository inspection of `pi-subagents` shows a real third architecture: detached per-run supervisors survive Pi reload/exit and reconnect through durable files without a daemon. This materially changes the lifetime decision and means the active review should not resolve that point unchanged.
discoveries.implications: The lifetime review was replaced; detached per-run worker supervisors are now accepted governing direction.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Carry detached process identity, reconnect, orphan reconciliation, and DAG/widget restoration into future implementation planning.
discoveries.title: The worker-lifetime review omitted detached per-run supervision

discoveries.body: Current recovery can synthesize lost from missing or corrupt mailbox/result artifacts without proving both detached supervisor and child/process group are dead. A stale heartbeat, corrupt mailbox, missing supervisor, or PID mismatch may leave an old child alive in the same cwd. Runtime terminal classification must remain distinct from a `retrySafe` ownership disposition; ambiguous process ownership must retain/quarantine the cwd and block replacement.
discoveries.title: Generic lost status does not yet prove retry safety

discoveries.body: Implementation confirms that a valid or synthesized terminal result cannot itself authorize retry: the detached supervisor may still be live, a child identity may be absent or reused, or the process group may remain present. Retry authorization therefore needs a separately published immutable disposition fact joining the exact attempt, supervisor and child PID/start identities, process-group observation, owner, and observation time; missing or corrupt proof must block retry even when terminal status is already durable.
discoveries.title: Worker retry safety needs immutable process proof rather than terminal inference

discoveries.body: `WorkerSessionStore.queue` serializes mutations inside one JavaScript manager instance but does not exclude a second Pi process from loading the same revision and winning an atomic-rename last-writer race. Initialization, ownership claim/transfer, launch reservation, ingest, and future DAG conductor takeover need process-shared locking plus expected revision/state-hash CAS; PID identity and atomic rename alone are insufficient.
discoveries.title: Worker session mutation serialization is process-local only

discoveries.body: Git worktrees protect working directories, indexes, and branch state, but agents can still conflict through contracts, schemas, generated sources, external services, ports, databases, caches, credentials, staging environments, or combined behavior. Runtime resources need namespacing or capacity constraints, and future merged states need direct validation.
discoveries.implications: The DAG scheduler should pair per-node worktrees with resource declarations/pools and integration validation rather than treating isolated branches as sufficient safety.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Define resource access modes and namespacing evidence in node contracts.
discoveries.title: Worktree isolation does not prove semantic independence

discoveries.body: Structured Markdown is already preserved by both chat and Lavish review renderers, while model delta is rendered separately. The next design frontier is deciding which semantic facts a Current understanding must make easy to verify and which headings may adapt to the focus.
discoveries.title: Current understanding needs a content contract rather than new rendering capability

discoveries.body: No further product choice is required to identify the implementation surface. The compact mode-guidance block should state the semantic core and adaptive synthesis rules, while deterministic tests should assert guidance delivery and safe structured Markdown rendering. Runtime validators remain limited to nonempty/current provenance checks, and semantic transcript scoring remains deferred.
discoveries.title: The prompt and deterministic regression impact follows from accepted direction

discoveries.body: Question briefs and Current understanding now have adaptive semantic contracts, and existing authority already distinguishes causal synthesis from documentation recitation. The unresolved implementation-policy choice is whether meaningful Markdown should be prompt-guided and smoke-tested or mechanically rejected by runtime shape validation.
discoveries.title: The remaining structure risk is enforcement, not information architecture

discoveries.body: The user experiences dense question briefs and Current understanding prose as a loss of visibility into the underlying project model. The issue is not formatting alone: visible brainstorming artifacts need to carry enough relevant context to demonstrate why a decision exists, how the affected behavior works today, what would change, and whether the agent's understanding matches the user's intent.
discoveries.title: Brainstorm surfaces need to serve as project-model projections

discoveries.body: Current understanding is now defined as the persistent present-state proof, while the resolver already emits a low-level transaction receipt. The missing acknowledgement layer should translate the user's input and resulting model mutation into a short human-readable semantic delta, then identify what remains open or where exploration continues. It should not repeat the full question brief or Current understanding.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Superseded by direct user feedback that no separate acknowledgement surface should be required.
discoveries.title: A brainstorm acknowledgement is a semantic-delta handoff

discoveries.body: The desired proof is an agent-authored explanation that selects and connects the relevant project facts, analogous to asking someone to describe the problem back in their own words. Forcing an acknowledgement surface or documentation-like exhaustive template can prove access to project information without proving comprehension, and can suppress the judgment the user wants to inspect.
discoveries.title: Template compliance can conceal whether the agent understands the project

evidence.body: The renderer owns the stable whole-turn shell; freeform question context may be Markdown, helpers, arbitrary HTML/CSS/scripts, or linked artifacts. Lavish is optional, review state remains renderer-neutral, review presentation blocks/waits through dag_brainstorm_review, submissions return to the agent for interpretation, failures leave review active, and detailed automated renderer tests follow the engine architecture.
evidence.title: workflow.md, tools.md, pi-integration.md, and production-validation.md

evidence.body: The implementation adds one dirty-generation coalesced `activate` pump per run, exact session-bound activation from the existing canonical session/timer/agent wake points, and a direct worker-terminal ingestion listener that wakes active runs. Pump settlement removes the old pump and synchronously hands dirty generations to a successor, including a wake injected after the final quiescence comparison. `detach()` first fences new activation, drains in-flight pumps while retaining the process-global registry claim, and only then releases the exact service lock so an awaited external lifecycle adapter cannot overlap a successor generation. Raw `advance` no longer reconstructs ownership from run-state PID alone. Each service generation registers its exact run/lock identity process-locally; concurrent live generations cannot steal an epoch. After the prior service detaches, a fresh service in the same exact session/process publishes a chained same_manager ownership fact, CAS-transfers to the next owner epoch, replayably repairs the session binding and active start identity across failpoints after owner, binding, or intent publication, and only then reconciles/schedules. Explicit proven-dead reattachment has the same replay coverage across distinct source and successor sessions: a lineage-less pre-transfer placeholder cannot rewrite start identity, while the durable successor binding and intent are published only after owner CAS. Different-process ownership remains fenced behind exact proven-dead reattachment. Current thin-plan runs fail closed if their required start intent disappears, while historical low-level canonical runs without one remain resumable. Ownership hydration remains finite at 4096 epochs and regression coverage executes more than 64 service generations. Tests reproduce an interrupted post-F0 applied_exact effect with an unsealed running attempt, prove concurrent service theft is blocked, detach the old service, then prove owner epoch advancement, F0 sealing, and exact F1 worker dispatch. One adopted terminal ingestion emits one wake. Focused model, planning, command, prepared-start, runtime, worker, and real-Git integration suites plus source and packed-artifact smoke pass.
evidence.title: Canonical conductor liveness and service-generation regression fix

evidence.body: Read-only analysis of the legacy diagram, canonical plan projection contract, live execution projection, widget, Pi command/TUI constraints, and authority boundaries recommends `/dag show` as one canonical read-only inspection namespace. Planning should automatically preview architecture and static graph before authorization; exact static plan selectors and session-bound live overlays remain distinct, deterministic, hash-labeled projections. Optional Lavish and exports present the same projection without authority. Legacy `dag_diagram` remains explicitly legacy.
evidence.title: Canonical DAG inspection UX research

evidence.body: Stress testing against model/code drift, cross-repository work, ignored context, capabilities, shared decisions, migrations, mutexes, capacity, dynamic discovery, worker retries, re-decomposition, partial authorization, user edits, secrets, large artifacts, and widget projection found five necessary contracts: immutable plan, separate authorization receipt, atomic mutable run snapshot, immutable bounded evidence, and generic worker result. It recommends selector-versioned semantic closure, commit/tree baselines, separate work items and gates, phase-scoped constraints, per-entity hashes, typed artifact references, and fail-closed replan for newly discovered semantic graph changes.
evidence.title: Adversarial canonical plan boundary review

evidence.body: A repository-grounded design exercise produced a closed content-hashed model-aware plan shape with architecture/outcome and decomposition phases, exact model/spec/code bindings, independent oracles, semantic effects, separate precedence/gate/mutex/resource/integration structures, fixed lifecycle binding, advisory paths, canonical hashing, deterministic projections, and a parallel API/server/client example. Its strongest result is the concrete vocabulary; adversarial review found that embedded review/authorization, dirty file hashes, singular repository binding, static capacity, whole-node mutexes, and ambiguous dynamic constraints must be corrected before adoption.
evidence.title: Concrete schemaVersion 1 design exercise

evidence.body: A bounded independent retry on the final stable schema verified that borrowed scoped effects are rejected, detached train expected targets are rejected, active integration attempts bind the exact train target, post-F3 F2 adoption is satisfiable only across the exact F3 input/output generation, and historical F1 evidence remains legal only through its exact indexed produced candidate. The canonical runtime test suite also passed.
evidence.title: Final canonical schema closure probe found no remaining task-108 blocker

evidence.body: A final independent read-only review verified the prior activation, catalog, receipt, authorization, lane, model-ref, dangerous-key, path, and most timestamp repairs, then found five remaining gaps: completion did not resolve exact predecessor prefix or required prefix/final profile evidence; oracle passage named oracle IDs without assertion-scoped procedure/environment evidence; F2 adoption was not limited to the sole post-F3 evidence-only-delta transition; external effects could borrow another work item's globally authorized scope or replay class; and RFC 3339 year-zero leap-day validation used JavaScript's 1900 remapping.
evidence.title: Final schema rereview isolated five last completion and evidence gaps

evidence.body: An independent no-edit review of the new TypeBox plan/run schemas found one canonical-JSON prototype-key collision and multiple semantic false acceptances: forged indexed stage evidence, integration readiness without exact F8/candidate closure, wrong detached-fact kinds, early causal release, later train-entry speculation, sticky-lane release/state mismatches, and legacy integration strategies. Existing positive tests passed, showing that closed structural schemas alone are insufficient without exact cross-record and plan/fact joins.
evidence.title: Initial canonical runtime schemas remain fail-open under adversarial probes

evidence.body: A second independent no-edit adversarial rereview found that the first repair still allowed active stages to bypass predecessor stages, fixed producers, or causal readiness; stage evidence hashes were not resolved through plan-bound procedure, environment, and check catalogs; later train entries could trust forged predecessor receipt strings; authorization validity, train-prefix closure, and effect authorization joins were incomplete; blocked admitted work could shed sticky lanes; merge-tree lineage and F2 evidence adoption were underrepresented; model refs erased collection/category semantics; and portable path plus RFC 3339 edge handling remained incomplete.
evidence.title: Second canonical schema rereview found residual activation, catalog, receipt, authorization, lane, lineage, and model-ref gaps

evidence.body: extensions/dag-workflow/dag-runtime/integration.ts installs canonical-dag-run above the editor, refreshes projection state every second, calls requestRender, and computes animation time inside render. widget.ts emits 4–12 independently cropped text lines, spends most rows on one-edge-per-line topology, and always appends an instructional footer. The component invalidate method is empty.
evidence.title: Current DAG widget is a one-second passive text renderer

evidence.body: Repository inspection of extensions/dag-workflow/dag-runtime/integration.ts shows both conductor advancement and widget status refresh use independent 1000 ms intervals. The current refresh is not serialized, and render(width) is widened with Math.max(20, width). A replacement controller can preserve the accepted one-second safety observation cadence while separating it from animation frames and honoring exact width.
evidence.title: Current DAG widget polls semantic status every second

evidence.body: `package.json` pins `pi-subagents` 0.25.0 and `extensions/dag-workflow/dag-subagent.ts` imports package-private `src/**` modules for discovery, execution, watchers, notifications, settings, schemas, and state. The current extension entry point does not import or register `registerDagSubagentTool`; dependency analysis finds no importer. The post-cutover runtime therefore does not currently launch workers, but still installs the dependency and retains tightly coupled dead integration code.
evidence.title: Current pi-subagents integration is packaged but dormant

evidence.body: An independent evidence review compared the accepted DAG contracts with DORA, SPACE, DevEx, controlled software-engineering experiments, SWE-bench/agent-evaluation guidance, queueing, and Amdahl-style serial constraints. Applicable lessons are to balance throughput with instability/recovery, use multiple objective and perceptual dimensions, measure feedback/cognitive-load/flow burden, predeclare units and hypotheses, pair/counterbalance comparable runs, retain hidden independent oracles, report cost with outcome, and avoid one metric, cross-context comparisons, p-value claims from tiny samples, or maximizing utilization. It recommends exact integrated outcomes and safety first, then operator active time, elapsed time, and cost; four pairs are formative and six valid pairs support only a directional local claim.
evidence.title: DORA, SPACE, DevEx, empirical methods, and agent evaluation support a paired multidimensional dogfood framework

evidence.body: A baseline review classified historical evidence into exact corpus/artifact facts, conditionally reconstructable facts, qualitative cases, unavailable/incomparable metrics, and prospective paired evidence. Legacy `maxConcurrency`, arbitrary flow, attempts, retries, merged/completed state, validation, and architecture semantics do not match sticky lanes, fixed F0–F8, exact worker identity, or integration receipts. It recommends fresh same-baseline pairs with `maxActiveNodes=1` versus parallel policy, counterbalanced order, fixed model/profile/oracle, separate fault drills, all pair traces, and immediate stops for integrity/duplicate/stale/effect/architecture escapes. The report is valid but source verification was limited because three referenced `/tmp` audit memos were no longer present; authoritative model evidence summaries were used.
evidence.title: Historical runs support incident classes while prospective pairs are required for comparative claims

evidence.body: Read-only design research recommends `/dag plan` as a separate run-grade CAS transaction whose mutable snapshot points to immutable scope, grounding, architecture, decomposition, candidate, validation, projection, review, authorization, publication, and handoff facts. Architecture and decomposition seal into one exact candidate; deterministic views are reviewed together; detached review and authorization receipts remain separate; identical candidate bytes publish immutably through lineage CAS; explicit `/dag run` builds a just-in-time hash-bound start bundle for the shipped runtime. Focus sessions and Markdown remain routing/presentation rather than planning authority.
evidence.title: DAG planning transaction lifecycle research

evidence.body: An independent contract design separates metrics derivable from the plan, terminal/current atomic snapshot, immutable receipts, and exact worker results from metrics that require observation. Terminal outcomes, attempts, retries, findings, conflicts, integration receipts, and usage are mostly derivable. Exact readiness queues, time-weighted useful concurrency, recovery intervals, and actual human response require a separate bounded atomic accumulator containing current open intervals, fixed counters/sums/histograms, source revision/hash, clock coverage, and no transition list. The observer runs post-commit, never backpressures execution, drops/gaps on overload, and produces a strict content-addressed `RunEvaluationEnvelopeV1` with explicit measured/zero-exposure/unsupported/not-observed/partial/censored status and denominators.
evidence.title: A bounded envelope plus non-authoritative accumulator can measure telemetry without event sourcing

evidence.body: Crash and concurrency analysis supports one closed atomic run snapshot with conductor epoch/CAS, persisted intents before external effects, exact launch/result/evidence identities, candidate/worktree generation fencing, dynamic gate/resource epochs, explicit quarantine, and exact integration transaction state. It identifies release blockers: process-shared conductor exclusion, idempotent generic launch reservation, result enumeration independent of completion auto-ack, retry-safe process ownership distinct from terminal status, immutable evidence reducer advancement, fail-closed corruption, bounded runtime retention, durable writes, and target-worktree-safe Git CAS landing. Twenty-five reducer invariants and adversarial worker/reducer/Git fixture matrices are specified.
evidence.title: Adversarial DagRunStateV1 and owned-runtime boundary review

evidence.body: An independently inspected 1,208-line design specifies a strict non-event-sourced atomic run snapshot, closed enums and subrecords, immutable fact indexes, natural idempotency slots, revision/hash CAS, conductor ownership, desired/current projections, work-item candidate generations, F0–F8 attempts, exact generic worker bindings, gates/precedence/resources/mutexes/leases, retry ledgers, blockers/effects/cancellation/quarantine, freshness, integration trains, exhaustive reducer inputs, transition guards, recovery matrices, 36 invariants, and adversarial fixtures. It preserves retry-only limits and separates integration-ready from combined-state completion. Material choices remain around run ownership transfer, generic-runtime idempotent launch and result enumeration, pause/cancel races, authorization composition, remaining retry defaults, process-shared locks and durability, successor-plan adoption, environment equivalence, and Git landing policy. The worker terminal status is failed because of an observed WebSocket model error, so the report claim is not treated as successful execution; the artifact itself remains independently inspectable evidence and materially agrees with the successful adversarial review.
evidence.title: Closed DagRunStateV1 schema and guarded reducer design

evidence.body: Independent source review found the exact-width violation definite and judged the reported repeated active row below the editor separator consistent with either an over-width physical wrap or stale content after a variable-height transition. It also identified un-serialized one-second refreshes, teardown races, and insufficient projection fields for authoritative spinners and stage progress. The recommended repair is a small versioned projection extension plus a serialized disposable widget controller around the pure renderer.
