evidence.title: Independent failure analysis confirms width violation and stale-row mechanisms

evidence.body: The third terminal-styled review presented exact run binding, visibility across every run condition, event/rescan/stable-join refresh, reload/fork/ownership behavior, nine conductor-internal tools, and non-TUI degradation. User feedback selected one exact session-bound run with direct-fork-only transfer; visibility through every nonterminal condition and clearing only after durable terminal reconciliation; transition signals plus one-second safety rescan and a three-attempt stable join; five separate read tools and four separate mutation tools; and persistent widget installation only in interactive TUI mode.
evidence.title: Final review accepts session binding, lifecycle, recovery, tool, and mode boundaries

evidence.body: Independent comparison rejected orchard9/tui-diagrams as a Go-only traversal renderer without true DAG edge routing, viewport bounds, canonical sorting, or terminal-cell-safe width. beautiful-mermaid and lovely-mermaid produce useful full diagrams but representative activity DAGs still exceeded the widget's 4–12-row budget; Dagre and d3-dag provide coordinates but leave terminal rasterization, clipping, omission semantics, and row budgeting custom. The review recommends a custom selected-neighborhood renderer and reserves generic libraries for benchmarks or explicit full-DAG views.
evidence.title: Generic graph renderers do not fit the persistent widget viewport contract

evidence.body: DagExecutionNodeV1 exposes activeLane and a worker tuple containing workerId, attemptNumber, terminalStatus, and retrySafe, but not processDisposition or an explicit live/running bit. A sticky active lane can also wait between operations. Therefore neither activeLane nor worker presence alone is sufficient authority for an animated spinner.
evidence.title: Current projection cannot prove a live worker process

evidence.body: A disposable Pi-terminal-styled Lavish artifact showed the same sticky-lane run at 48, 80, and 120 columns, runtime conflict containment, integrity degradation, ten ASCII marks, focus anchors, row budgeting, and interaction boundaries. User feedback selected the full ten-mark set, horizontal normal/wide topology with narrow adjacency fallback, one-third terminal height capped at twelve rows, and an entirely read-only widget whose users control the run only by communicating with the conductor agent.
evidence.title: Prototype review 1 accepts the core persistent widget grammar

evidence.body: A second disposable terminal-styled artifact stress-tested high fan-in/fan-out, disconnected active lanes, more active nodes than the row budget, long IDs, retry and worker-evidence distinctions, remote typed constraints, and stale/corrupt projection states. User feedback selected attention-before-active-before-context overflow, stable canonical `Nxx` aliases, a strongly marked hash-validated last-good graph during transient churn with suppression on corruption/no baseline, and one-minute elapsed-time buckets.
evidence.title: Prototype review 2 accepts deterministic overflow, identity, stale, and time policies

evidence.body: The active-focus seed preserves a concrete TUI incident where a dense multi-line DAG topology, an active summary, the read-only footer, a separator, repeated active text, and a tool/evidence line appear concatenated or overwritten around the editor/footer boundary. The incident establishes visible corruption but not its transient trigger.
evidence.title: DAG widget output visibly collided with the chat surface

evidence.body: Counterexamples and simulations confirm five distinct layers—static validity, correctness readiness, speculative safety, capacity admission, and dispatch safety—and recommend a minimal deterministic vector-resource list scheduler rather than RCPSP or per-run DRF. The review demonstrates expanded gate-production cycles, phase-scoped mutex requirements, greedy fragmentation, critical-path starvation, duplicate architecture authority, exponential speculative invalidation, correlated provider retry storms, evaluator/reviewer bottlenecks, long integration-lock separation, multi-repository preverification, generation-first cancellation, lease leakage, fairness head-of-line blocking, fanout oscillation, and large-frontier indexing needs. It proposes bounded bypass reservations, provider circuits, green/amber/red speculation, conservative hysteresis, closed narrowing observations, twenty reducer invariants, and property/crash/metamorphic release gates.

evidence.body: An independent design specifies a pure event-driven deterministic list scheduler over immutable plan and atomic run state. It separates correctness readiness from mutex/capacity admission; defines phase slots, exact readiness/admissibility, atomic batch reservations, resource/provider/role/worktree capacities, critical-path and dominant-resource priority, bypass-count starvation, exact-prefix-only speculation, implementation-only adaptive fanout, dynamic narrowing and successor-plan routing, pause/cancel/replan behavior, structural deadlock classification, crash reconciliation, reducer inputs/invariants, and deterministic projections. evidence.body: The official Pi subagent example extracts final assistant output and caps parallel model-visible output at 50 KiB. `pi-subagents` supports file-only output references and bounded parent results but does not require a generic structured report. `pi-agent-router` injects only bounded final responses or validated `submit_result` payloads, not full transcripts/tool history. `pi-subagent-lite` uses explicit output-file contracts. These converge on a compact terminal handoff with artifact references while leaving runtime observations and detailed diagnostics outside the parent prompt.
evidence.title: Pi subagent ecosystems favor bounded final results over transcript injection

evidence.body: The official Pi subagent example launches a child with optional per-agent `--tools`; omitted tools inherit normal defaults and there is no dedicated recursion guard. Mature `pi-subagents` is more explicit: it sets `PI_SUBAGENT_CHILD=1`, its normal extension entrypoint immediately returns in children so parent watchers/UI/orchestration never initialize, strips parent-only orchestration skill/history, and does not register `subagent` by default. Only agents whose resolved tools explicitly include `subagent` receive a child-safe fanout extension, bounded by `maxSubagentDepth`. Other normal builtins and extensions remain available unless an agent declares allowlists. `pi-subagent-lite` defaults child extensions to none and supports per-agent tool allowlists. `@mjakl/pi-subagent` inherits parent/default tools and extensions while bounding recursion with depth and cycle guards. `pi-agent-router` uses `--no-extensions` plus explicit delegated extensions as a stronger sandbox-oriented design.
evidence.title: Established Pi subagent implementations separate child role, tools, and recursion policy

evidence.body: Dogfood artifacts demonstrate useful whole-turn sections and controls, but their shell, CSS, JavaScript, option forms, navigation, and queuePrompt wiring were repeatedly handwritten by the agent. evidence.body: A read-only audit inventoried 9,845 USB files totaling 27.995 GB; streamed all 4,312 direct Pi JSONLs totaling 3.425 GB and 936,292 valid records; parsed the full 823,245-file `.ai` archive manifest; streamed its 12.66 GB tar while selecting 386 bounded DAG artifacts; and metadata-listed all 190,725 on-call archive entries. evidence.body: Adversarial review found that generic worker success cannot imply stage pass; evidence must bind exact plan, work item, candidate generation, worker attempt, commit/tree, oracle, procedure, environment, authorization, findings, and side effects. evidence.body: An independent adversarial review of the initial task-109 reducer/store slice found release-blocking gaps in run-store path confinement, cancellation execution fencing, crash-resumable dead-owner takeover, hash-bound ownership proof, immutable-fact liveness, partial-completion cancellation, parent-directory durability, and exact natural-slot coverage. evidence.body: Thirty-five primary-source references across Terraform/OpenTofu, Bazel, Ninja, Nix, Kubernetes, Argo, Tekton, GitHub/GitLab merge queues, Flyway, Liquibase, Sqitch, and BuildKit converge on immutable reviewed plan identity, detached approval, mutable observed run state, explicit input/environment digests, exact-combination revalidation, declaration checksums, typed staleness, and secret references rather than values. evidence.body: A no-edit review of commits `a366e87`, `0e779ab`, and `f0d14b6` found that interactive Lavish opening depends on an ambient unshipped `lavish-open` helper despite the pinned optional CLI contract, and that late supervisor identity binding can overwrite a concurrently recorded `cancelling` worker state. evidence.body: Lavish 0.1.43 exposes file-oriented open, poll, end, export, and share CLI commands. Open canonicalizes the HTML path and derives a stable session key from it; saving the same file live-reloads the artifact. Poll waits for normalized prompts, user/agent end state, or browser-proven severe layout warnings. Interrupted polls can safely resume because queued feedback persists. User-ended sessions refuse ordinary reopen and require an explicit `--reopen`.
evidence.title: lavish-axi 0.1.43 help and installed implementation

evidence.body: In Lavish 0.1.43, `window.lavish.queuePrompt` posts a prompt from the artifact iframe and `sendQueuedPrompts` submits the queue. Poll normalizes uid, prompt, selector, tag, text, and optional target, but carries no origin or trusted-user-gesture field. Agent-authored scripts share the page and can call the same functions or imitate standard tags. Therefore a poll prompt proves browser-channel feedback was queued, but cannot mechanically prove a human initiated it.
sourceRefs: lavish-axi 0.1.43 injected SDK queuePrompt and normalizePrompt implementation
evidence.title: Lavish poll does not distinguish human-triggered from artifact-script prompts

evidence.body: The artifact receives `window.lavish.queuePrompt`, `sendQueuedPrompts`, and `endSession`. `queuePrompt` emits prompt text plus normalized tag/text/selector/target context; `options.data` is appended as JSON inside prompt text rather than returned as a distinct field. Poll may also return whiteboard references, session-ended metadata, a DOM snapshot, and severe layout warnings. Standard controls should queue one final response per question. A project adapter must cap prompts/bytes and omit the DOM snapshot by default before model context.

evidence.title: lavish-axi queuePrompt/poll implementation and T8 dogfood

evidence.body: Lavish 0.1.43 ships only a `dist/cli.mjs` executable: package metadata declares no main or exports and documents no JavaScript or JSON API. Results are AXI/TOON. evidence.body: The renderer maps every review point into its own card and form, uses point IDs as independent queue keys, and the updated fixture visibly renders two decisions in one turn. evidence.body: The user-requested prototype under `spec/prototypes/lavish-turn-renderer/` renders a versioned fixture into a deterministic self-contained whole-turn shell; supports Current understanding, delta, frontier, awareness, decisions, exact payloads, and trusted interactive HTML; bounds expanded and compact-table CLI feedback; and exercises fake open/poll/end, missing-artifact open, abort/resume, user-ended preservation, and cleanup. evidence.body: A read-only audit compared current dormant legacy assets, the last active conductor at git revision 220f206, current worker-runtime contracts, and the candidate node lifecycle. The legacy system had typed graph/run records, dependency readiness, isolated worktrees, rebase/fast-forward integration, evidence-oriented executor/validator prompts, and deterministic ASCII layout. But planning/chunking were free-form prose, readiness and failure policy were advisory, worker completion required manual relay, result recording was not bound atomically to immutable worker identity, configuration allowed arbitrary flows, file scope was decorative or architecture-distorting, validation happened before rebase without post-rebase verification, and run state lacked crash-safe canonical ownership.
evidence.title: Legacy DAG design and control-plane audit

evidence.body: The retained legacy run state has useful DAG/node/step/worktree fields, but `saveRunState` directly writes `manifest.json` and `nodes.json` as two separate non-atomic files; worker records are also direct overwrites. The old launch flow marks an attempt `running` and saves before a separate model-mediated subagent launch, while result ingestion is a later model call that mutates nodes and writes a worker record. There is no run revision, ownership token, process identity, launch receipt, terminal result ID/hash, ingestion receipt, completion queue, or mutation serialization. A crash can leave manifest/nodes inconsistent, a `running` attempt with no process, a live process with no persisted PID, or a duplicated result transition.
evidence.title: Legacy DAG state cannot safely recover detached workers

evidence.body: The current legacy `getReadyNodeIds` selects nodes whose status is `pending` and whose `dependsOn` nodes are all `merged`; the legacy DAG exposes one `maxConcurrency`. It has no distinct gate, phase-scoped mutex, resource demand/capacity, lease, risk, critical-path, speculative invalidation, integration capacity, ownership epoch, or persisted launch reservation semantics. This code is useful only as a regression fixture for simple topological readiness, not as authority for the redesigned scheduler.
evidence.title: Legacy scheduler reduces readiness to merged dependencies

evidence.body: A prior PsychoPack incident proposal correctly identified unrecorded retries, stale commit pointers, incomplete merge/finalization telemetry, missing context paths, and worker-count-only metrics. It proposed append-only `events.jsonl` and deterministic metrics files for legacy `nodes.json`. The current accepted architecture instead forbids an execution event log: one atomic `DagRunStateV1` retains natural-slot attempts, blockers, leases, retries, effects, findings, and receipt pointers, while transition notices are disposable. The incident and desired measures remain evidence; its event-log storage design must not be carried forward.
evidence.title: The legacy telemetry proposal identifies missing recovery facts but conflicts with current snapshot authority

evidence.body: Node branches and worktree paths are deterministic by run and node, and refresh verifies branch identity plus cleanliness before work starts. This is reusable. However, a node worktree has no active-attempt lease, owner token, or generation. After a crash, automatic relaunch could place two supervisors in the same worktree, and refresh/rebase must never run while an ambiguous or live detached attempt owns it.
evidence.title: Legacy worktree topology is reusable but lacks attempt ownership

evidence.body: An independent worker reviewed authoritative model decisions, the canonical run-state design, scheduler projections, legacy diagram code, owned-worker boundaries, and Pi TUI APIs. It recommends a pure semantic `DagExecutionProjectionV1` followed by a separate viewport renderer; validates plan/run hashes and only exact worker bindings through a torn-read-resistant join; preserves orthogonal work-item, phase, blocker, retry, worker, and integration facts; uses deterministic focus ordering and explicit omission counts; fails closed on corrupt or ambiguous authority; and routes every mutation through closed reducer commands. The report also identifies unresolved session binding, placement, glyph, height, RPC, terminal visibility, and overflow policies.
evidence.title: Adversarial review defines a two-layer live DAG projection boundary

evidence.body: A reproducible read-only parser scanned 731 JSONL files, 618 unique session IDs, and 966,632 lines with three documented malformed lines. It classified 466 relevant unique sessions: 38 active invocation sessions, 163 DAG child sessions, and 265 mention/inherited-context sessions. Thirty-one unique sessions made structured DAG calls; 26 contained high-confidence Pi-expanded DAG command prompts; 5,662 unique DAG tool calls and 81 command invocations were found. The audit correlated 22 named run IDs and nine surviving run directories. Structured errors repeatedly showed existing-worktree collisions, corrupt shared JSON, model invariant rejection, ambiguous active-run lookup, rebase/dirty merge conflicts, oversized transport, and stale running manifests. Only one surviving run is coherently completed; the others remain running, blocked, or partially merged.
evidence.title: Exhaustive local Pi DAG session audit

evidence.body: A first-principles read-only audit finds that separate durable planning/run/release authorities are sound, but the proposed receipt/hash stack is overbuilt. Use UUIDs for occurrence identity; integer revisions checked under a real process-shared lock for mutable JSON CAS; file fsync, same-directory atomic rename, and parent fsync for durability; canonical content hashes only for exact immutable plan bytes, independently stored artifacts/facts, targeted model closure, and a reviewed packet when equality matters; native Git OIDs without wrapper hashes; persisted natural operation keys for duplicate-effect prevention; and intent/observe/reconcile only around external effects. Exact human-entry attestation, blanket self-hashed receipts, blanket nested-entity hashes, per-phase immutable fact chains, and a mandatory permanently hashed run-start bundle do not prevent additional ordinary crash/race/retry failures and should be removed or made optional. Concrete retained fixes are process-shared planning/publication CAS, exact reviewed-candidate equality, internally derived `/dag run` inputs, recoverable starting-to-active session binding, atomic plan-affecting whole-run fence, idempotent discovery upsert, private Git refs for candidate retention, and remote push reconciliation using expected-old/desired-new Git OIDs.
evidence.title: Pragmatic durability audit for a trusted local workflow

evidence.body: No single paper, standard, or mature system prescribes the requested exact phase order. A defensible fixed lifecycle composes: NASA/FDA implementation, static analysis, intended-use validation, defect disposition, regression, review, and delivery evidence; Cucumber discovery/formulation/automation; LLVM regression tests, review, and revert-to-green; architecture fitness functions; changed-code mutation testing and OSS-Fuzz bug corpora; fixed agent/repair pipelines with original-revision witnesses, regression filtering, finite budgets, and explicit non-success outcomes. Test passing is plausibility rather than proof, and exact retry counts or mandatory hardening techniques are local risk policy.

evidence.body: orchard9/tui-diagrams provides Unicode flowchart rendering and Mermaid parsing, but it is implemented in Go and targets orchard9/tui. Direct use in this TypeScript Pi extension would require a subprocess or port and does not inherently solve strict widget width/row budgets or activity-neighborhood selection.

evidence.body: Each immutable generic worker result records exact worker/attempt/config identity, `startedAt`, `endedAt`, model, provider, stop reason, aggregate input/output/cache/total tokens, reported monetary cost when available, report-repair count, runtime/model/protocol errors, bounded diagnostic metadata, and artifacts. evidence.body: Task 110 closed the generic owned-worker consumer boundary after four independent read-only closure rounds. The final tree serializes process-shared session mutation with exact PID/start identity and revision/hash CAS; reserves launches by launchKey plus normalized request hash; binds supervisor authority only to the actual spawn result; separates terminal status from immutable retry-safety proof; fences disposable roots by canonical repository containment and dev/inode identity; arbitrates cancellation, recovery publication, and result adoption under store-locked authority; preserves durable results, launch replay, quarantine, and archived inspection under bounded mutable retention; and queues explicit and coalesced timer scans without stale-return or starvation behavior. Focused fixtures cover crash windows, copied/PID-reused locks, concurrent retry replay, detached cwd/nonce/uninspectable descendants, root replacement/retirement races, forged pre-binding artifacts, timestamp/report conflicts, completion-less retention, cancellation/result races, scan backlogs, dispatch-in-progress recovery, and stale unbound scan snapshots. evidence.body: Primary and mature-system sources converge on typed dependencies, resource pools, isolation, speculative validation, and ordered integration rather than hard file ownership. Ninja distinguishes dependency kinds, dynamic dependencies, and pools; PostgreSQL SSI provides an evidence-bearing conflict-serializability analogy with abort/retry; Crystal demonstrates higher-order conflicts after clean textual merges; Git worktrees and merge-tree isolate and simulate without proving semantics; schema systems require staged expand/adopt/contract protocols; Airflow and Dask separate readiness from capacity/priority; Zuul and GitLab merge trains speculatively test ordered future integration prefixes and invalidate successors after failures. Structured merge reduces textual false positives but still requires review and behavioral validation.
evidence.title: Prior art for safe parallel software-engineering work

evidence.body: An extension can return from a launch tool while work continues, then call `pi.sendMessage` with `triggerTurn: true` and `deliverAs: "followUp"` to wake the main agent after it settles. `pi.appendEntry` stores compact non-context state pointers and custom entries can have TUI renderers. `ctx.ui.setWidget` supports persistent string lines in TUI and RPC, or a width-aware component factory in TUI; updates can be event-driven and request render. `setStatus`, notifications, tool renderers, and commands provide secondary inspection/control. Long-lived processes, watchers, and timers must start after `session_start` or on demand and receive idempotent `session_shutdown` cleanup.
evidence.title: Pi exposes the completion and live UI primitives the DAG runtime needs

evidence.body: Pi 0.82.1 intentionally has no built-in subagent workflow. Its official example implements a foreground `subagent` tool by spawning separate `pi --mode json -p --no-session` processes, parsing selected `message_end` and `tool_result_end` events, propagating abort, limiting parallel work to eight tasks/four concurrent, capping model-visible output, aggregating nested usage, and rendering rich collapsed/expanded progress. Pi's public SDK alternatively exposes `createAgentSession` with in-memory sessions, direct lifecycle subscriptions, tool/model control, abort, and dispose. RPC mode offers strict LF-framed JSONL commands/events, prompt acceptance separate from completion, `agent_settled`, abort/steer/follow-up, session state, and extension UI transport.
evidence.title: Pi intentionally leaves subagents to extensions

evidence.body: `pi.sendMessage` injects a custom message that participates in session/LLM context. With `deliverAs: "followUp"` it waits until the agent has no more tools, and `triggerTurn: true` starts a turn when idle. Custom message details can carry a stable completion and delivery ID. Pi session entries survive restart and are inspectable through `ctx.sessionManager`, while `agent_settled`, `ctx.isIdle()`, and `ctx.hasPendingMessages()` provide drain scheduling signals. These primitives can reconcile a crash after message append by finding the delivery ID in the session branch instead of blindly sending another copy.
sourceRefs: Pi docs/extensions.md: pi.sendMessage, pi.appendEntry, ctx.sessionManager, agent_settled
evidence.title: Pi can deliver one completion turn and persist its message identity

evidence.body: Pi custom tools execute after runtime initialization with an AbortSignal, incremental `onUpdate`, and extension context. A presentation adapter tool can spawn Lavish open/poll, report that the browser is waiting, remain attached to the current agent turn, kill only the poll subprocess on abort, and later resume the same file-keyed Lavish session. Session start/reload hooks can restore focus presentation metadata without starting background resources during extension loading.
sourceRefs: Pi extensions.md custom-tool and lifecycle contracts
evidence.title: Pi tools can host an interruptible Lavish review wait

evidence.body: The official extension resolves the running Pi invocation by preferring `process.execPath + process.argv[1]` when the current script exists, handling Bun virtual scripts, then falling back to a non-generic executable or `pi` on PATH. It launches with `shell: false`, an explicit cwd, model, tools, prompt file, and cancellation escalation. For an owned RPC worker, Pi's `--no-extensions`, `--no-skills`, `--no-prompt-templates`, `--tools`, `--extension`, `--model`, `--thinking`, `--no-session`/`--session-dir`, and context/trust flags can make inheritance explicit rather than ambient.
evidence.title: Pi's official subagent example provides robust CLI resolution and explicit tool selection

evidence.body: Pi extension documentation and installed type declarations confirm that `ctx.ui.setWidget(key, factory, { placement: "belowEditor" })` installs a persistent component; clearing the key removes it. The component receives `render(width)` and every rendered line must fit that width. The factory receives the live `TUI`, whose public `terminal.columns` and `terminal.rows` permit deterministic height-aware rendering; state updates call `tui.requestRender()`. Widgets are no-ops outside supported UI modes, so the adapter must guard TUI behavior and preserve command/tool projections for headless modes. Components may implement `dispose()` for watcher/timer cleanup.
evidence.title: Pi supports passive width- and terminal-height-aware persistent widgets

evidence.body: Pi 0.82.1 RPC uses strict LF-delimited JSON commands/responses/events. Prompt success means accepted, not completed; `agent_settled` is the reliable semantic terminal event after retries, compaction retries, and queued continuations. Public commands include prompt, abort, state/model/thinking controls, and session inspection. `message_update` contains cumulative partial message data and must be ignored. `message_end`, tool lifecycle events, `extension_error`, and `agent_settled` are sufficient for bounded progress and terminal synthesis. Pi ships a typed `RpcClient`, but only its declaration/build file exists under an unexported internal subpath, so the extension should implement a small protocol client rather than import private runtime code.
evidence.title: Pi RPC exposes the complete worker lifecycle but its client is not publicly exported

evidence.body: Representative extensions expose complementary patterns: `nano-team` uses three spawn/kill/status tools and a debounced animated above-editor chip widget; `pi-subagents-lite` uses async-by-default file output and one batch completion callback but still writes multiple raw diagnostics streams and has no concurrency limit; `@bacnh85/pi-subagent` uses isolated in-process SDK sessions, closed tool allowlists, idle plus hard timeouts, parent cancellation, no recursive subagents, inspectable in-memory threads, and no disk I/O, but accesses private model-registry internals for shared runtime compatibility; `@mjakl/pi-subagent` uses subprocess RPC, bounded rolling capture, settlement events, persistent logical child sessions, depth/cycle guards, and strict output caps; `pi-dynamic-workflow` uses concurrency/budget limits, O(1) append journals, bounded background completion messages, cancellation, and deterministic resume hashes; `pi-agent-router` adds durable task registries, hidden follow-up status turns, fail-closed delegated extensions, retry classification, and compact session attachment; `pi-subagents-lite/FleetView` demonstrates live conversation, steering, stopping, queueing, and below-editor status.
evidence.title: Pi subagent ecosystem converges on bounded lifecycle and compact UI patterns

evidence.body: Independent review of Pi's bundled subagent example and pi-subagents 0.25.0 found a durable pattern: keep lifecycle separate from activity freshness, render one compact status row plus at most one activity row per selected item, show structural fractions instead of invented percentages, animate from changing snapshots or fresh heartbeats, enforce display-width and terminal-height budgets, explicitly summarize omissions, and tear down timers/widgets idempotently across session transitions.
evidence.title: Subagent widget review favors snapshot-driven bounded activity rows

evidence.body: A field investigation found that Pi `message_update` records carried a tiny incremental `delta` plus `partial` and `message`, where the latter two were duplicate cumulative copies of the complete response so far. `pi-subagents@0.25.0` synchronously serialized and appended every complete update, writing the growing response twice per token update. The resulting sum is approximately quadratic in response length. One measured run had a 388 KiB session transcript but a 188.6 MiB event log: 187.2 MiB from `message_update`, about 486× amplification. A two-character delta produced a 60,542-byte line because it contained the current 30 KiB response twice. Long-running failed agents produced 6–9 GiB logs. A deployed hotfix drops `message_update`, retains final `message_end`, tool, lifecycle, and control events, and caps child diagnostics at 50 MiB per run; active runs then contained zero message updates and only a few MiB of diagnostics.
evidence.title: Cumulative message_update logging caused quadratic write amplification

evidence.body: `pi-subagents` does not run a long-lived scheduling daemon. For each async invocation it writes a JSON config, spawns a separate Node process running `subagent-runner.ts` with `detached: true`, `stdio: "ignore"`, and `proc.unref()`, and records the runner PID plus status/result artifacts. On Unix this creates an independent process group that can continue after the owning Pi process exits. The detached runner launches and supervises the actual Pi child, writes durable status/results, and exits when that run finishes.
evidence.title: pi-subagents survives reload with detached per-run processes, not a daemon

evidence.body: The focus seed reports that `pi-subagents` can explode `events.jsonl` writes and consume substantial resources. Treat this as a high-impact field observation to reproduce and trace against the installed package before attributing the exact cause.
evidence.title: User reports runaway pi-subagents events.jsonl growth

evidence.body: Local `pi-subagents` 0.25.0 launches child Pi in JSON mode and writes every nonblank stdout line to JSONL while also parsing the same events for progress; async execution targets one `<asyncDir>/events.jsonl` across steps and model attempts. `createJsonlWriter` limits each writer instance to 50 MiB but opens in append mode and starts `bytesWritten` at zero, so each step/attempt/process can append another cap to an existing file. The async tracker can allocate and read the entire unread suffix into memory. The package changelog says earlier default JSONL artifacts duplicated Pi sessions and caused 10+ GiB directories; those sync artifacts were disabled by default, while async `events.jsonl` remains part of observability. Current local `.ai/runs/**/events.jsonl` samples are small, so the user's exact incident is architecturally plausible but not reproduced from surviving files.
evidence.title: pi-subagents streams duplicate raw child events into append-only JSONL

evidence.body: The extension starts a filesystem watcher on its global results directory and scans existing result files at load and again after `session_start` establishes the current session ID. Results are filtered by stable session ID (or cwd fallback), deduplicated in memory for a short TTL, emitted through its intercom/completion event path, and then deleted. `session_shutdown` stops watchers/timers and clears in-memory jobs but deliberately does not kill detached runners. Thus a runner can finish during reload and its result is picked up afterward. The in-memory live-job widget map is cleared and does not appear to be reconstructed from running status directories, so status remains disk-inspectable but live UI continuity is weaker than completion continuity.
evidence.title: pi-subagents recovers completion through durable files and a restarted watcher

evidence.body: Pi's official `structured-output.ts` extension defines a typed tool whose result contains bounded machine-readable `details` and `terminate: true`. Pi instructs the model to use it as the final action; termination avoids an extra assistant turn after the tool call. In RPC mode, `tool_execution_end` carries the complete tool result and details, while `agent_settled` independently proves the session-level run has no retries, compaction retries, or queued continuations left. Therefore a supervisor can capture a valid report at tool completion but must still wait for `agent_settled` or process termination before finalizing runtime status.
evidence.title: Pi supports a terminating structured-output tool captured through RPC

evidence.body: Pi's TUI component contract requires every rendered line to stay within the provided display width. Persistent widgets can render themed custom components, and timer-driven motion is implemented by changing a version/frame and calling tui.requestRender(). The bundled Snake and Space Invaders examples demonstrate this pattern; plan-mode demonstrates compact persistent progress.
evidence.title: Pi supports animated widgets but requires strict width-safe rendering

evidence.body: `SessionManager.getSessionId()` exposes a durable session UUID, `getSessionFile()` exposes its persisted JSONL path, and descendant headers record `parentSession`. `ExtensionContext.mode` distinguishes `tui`, `rpc`, `json`, and `print`. In TUI mode, `ctx.ui.setWidget` accepts a component factory whose `render(width)` can remain resize-aware and request rerenders. In RPC mode, `setWidget` supports fire-and-forget string arrays but ignores component factories. `setWidget(key, undefined)` clears either form. Session replacement tears down the old extension runtime before the replacement receives `session_start`, so manager subscriptions, timers, watchers, and widget state must rebind per session and captured old contexts are invalid.
evidence.title: Pi exposes enough stable primitives for a session-scoped worker activity surface

evidence.body: Read-only inspection confirms a self-attestation gap across the current authority chain. Project-model acceptance validates semantic content but trusts an ambient caller-generated interactionRef rather than an exact durable user entry; Lavish binds bounded parsed prompts rather than raw feedback; review presentation has no immutable presentation receipt; run state validates only nominal receipt HashRefs; and conductor start accepts caller-built plan, genesis, context, concurrency, and time before robust session-binding preflight. The recommended closure introduces strict canonical HumanInteractionReceiptV1 with independent decision slots; PlanReviewReceiptV1 binding exact plan plus architecture/decomposition/static-graph hashes and post-response freshness; PlanAuthorizationReceiptV1 and deterministic AuthorizationSetV1; boundary-specific PlanFreshnessReceiptV1; byte-identical PlanPublicationReceiptV1 plus lineage-head CAS; and compiler-owned DagRunStartBundleV1 with explicit run-request receipt and starting-to-active session-binding CAS. Validation is a dependency DAG from strict bytes and source observations through freshness, projections, interaction, review, authorization/publication, run preflight, bundle, genesis, and binding. Existing run-store hard-link/fsync/locking patterns are reusable. Positive authority cannot come from arbitrary tool args, ambient refs, truncated feedback, or generic prose; approve-only remains valid, same-turn approval/authorization require independent explicit slots, and `/dag run` becomes the sole start intent.
evidence.title: Exact interaction, planning receipt, publication, and run-start contract design

evidence.body: Implemented the accepted product-facing vertical slice over the shipped canonical runtime. The planning core provides strict typed source joins, static semantic plan hashing, immutable retained revisions, decision CAS, deterministic Markdown/static graph/node/lineage projections, and PID/start-identity lock recovery. `/dag plan` preserves the active focus, performs architecture-first planning through one save tool, and keeps approval, authorization, and explicit run start separate. V1 authorization is exact whole-plan scope and cannot expand a subset. `/dag show` resolves exact static or current-session live views without inferred latest selection. `/dag run` revalidates clean Git model/spec baselines, exact common-dir/object-format identity, and the checked-out target branch; it compiles internally to CanonicalDagPlanV1/genesis/context, persists a recoverable prepared-start intent, blocks cross-plan concurrent starts, and advances only the exact session-bound runtime/source plan. Prefix/final integration validation executes plan-bound shell-free argv in a detached combined-state worktree and binds both Node and helper bytes; failed commands remain FAIL. Owned evaluator completion is treated as trusted external observation, while needs-attention/failure and F6 candidate edits fail closed. Whole-run needs_replan blocks new dispatch/integration while allowing current work to settle. Project-model/focus stores prevent cross-process lost updates, monotonic rollback ABA, and symlink-mediated roots. Focused planning, runtime-adapter, command, prepared-start, model, full canonical runtime, Git integration, package, and smoke tests pass; the command suite includes a real plan→show→prepared canonical run reaching F1. The complete real-Git dogfood matrix passed with manifest sha256:776c7a2107805219083c5c00c9edecb8f28c722f72df1d53f04df335aac59aca. The six-pair/twelve-execution counterbalanced portfolio and three recovery drills passed with unchanged semantic manifest sha256:057de6716bed1bd822dcfa66edeb3c057de2ad4cd01b743e0d8e99d3abcd797f and runtime-bound manifest sha256:ea224045f3babe8a0230ee09d10e30d49c65b0f04928d7438525f275aaad3d4a.
evidence.title: Plan/show/run vertical slice implementation and verification

evidence.body: Read-only source inspection recommends three linked but separately authoritative transactions under one active focus: planning publishes immutable lineage-CAS plans; DagRunStateV1 owns execution; a distinct release-closure transaction owns post-run verification and exact remote push. Pre-publication candidate ordinals do not consume plan revisions; publication requires same planId, exact predecessor head, revision +1, identical reviewed bytes, and atomic lineage-head CAS. A plan-affecting finding must atomically fence new dispatch and integration before a deterministic non-authoritative execution discovery is handed to the project model. V1 should use a whole-run barrier and require human reconciliation plus a distinct reviewed successor even when dismissed. Sealed predecessor candidates remain content-addressed and private-ref preserved; only mechanically exact-equivalent candidates may be explicitly authorized for successor adoption, and all F0–F8 evidence/status reruns. `/dag run` resolves exact published plans, compiles fresh start bundles internally, and never accepts caller paths. `/dag show` exposes exact plan/node/run/finding/lineage views. Release requires an explicit durable intent-before-effect transaction and exact remote OID reconciliation. A non-circular rollout uses a human-reviewed bootstrap plan for the minimum self-hosting compiler, then uses the new planner for finding/successor/adoption/release slices and deliberately dogfoods one successor event before release.
evidence.title: Successor-plan, execution-discovery, and release-closure contract design

evidence.body: Read-only source inspection confirms the runtime validates closed internal coherence but has no authoritative source-joined compiler: conductor start trusts caller-authored paths/hashes, plan validation does not recompute model/spec/repository authority, and lifecycle task packets omit the complete transitive referenced plan slice. The recommended compiler is a CAS-backed immutable phase-fact pipeline for scope, grounding, architecture, decomposition, validation/seal, review, authorization, publication, and start. It deterministically recomputes governing selector closure and receipt validity; binds exact model/spec/artifact/repository/profile facts; derives a semantic access matrix and only justified precedence, mutex, resource, migration, gate, and integration-train constraints; emits complete closed node packets and deterministic architecture/decomposition/graph projections; routes diagnostics to the earliest correctable phase; and seals only exact validated candidate bytes. Authority and freshness are revalidated at compile, review, authorization, publication, and start. Required representational additions include acceptance-receipt identity, entity-level grounding/traceability, explicit semantic-read source basis, work-item architecture relevance, strict transaction/receipt/node-packet/start-bundle schemas, and a plan-bound compilation-manifest ref if traceability remains detached.
evidence.title: Planning compiler core contract and schema-gap analysis

evidence.body: A holistic read-only audit finds that the accepted product direction is coherent but implementation priorities inverted: roughly 12.4k lines of canonical DAG runtime exist while `/dag plan` and `/dag show` are absent and `/dag run` remains an informational stub requiring caller-built low-level inputs. The shortest useful release path is a thin vertical slice over the shipped worker/Git/run substrate: one revisioned `plan.json` with whole-plan hash, readable Markdown and graph projections, internal architecture then decomposition, direct `/dag show`, internally assembled `/dag run`, a whole-run `needs_replan` pause for blocking plan discoveries, one end-to-end recovery fixture, accurate docs, package audit, and a release-readiness check. Mandatory compilation manifests, receipt chains, automatic cross-plan adoption, remote release transactions, and bootstrap authority ceremony should be deleted or deferred absent field evidence. The five prior review points are mostly implementation details rather than product choices. Release-ready means locally verified, documented, packaged, and clean; remote push/tag/npm publication remains an ordinary explicit user action unless separately requested.
evidence.title: Planning product requirements and release-path simplicity audit

evidence.body: After successive adversarial findings were repaired, final read-only closure worker `worker-msfq1drj-e08efac880` reported no release blockers. evidence.body: A repository-wide first-principles audit classifies hashes by practical role. Retain hashes for canonical plan equality across stores, independently hydrated artifact/fact bytes, project-model semantic object and selected governing-closure equality, generated-spec/projection checksums when persisted, worker config/result checksums, executable/config/environment fingerprints, large diagnostic/patch/no-progress fingerprints, deterministic evaluation envelopes and privacy-safe cohort keys, plus native Git OIDs. Retain compare-and-swap semantics but implement mutable concurrency with process-shared locks and expected integer revisions, not parallel snapshot hashes. Use stable UUIDs and generations for transactions, reviews, authorizations, runs, attempts, effects, findings, ownership, and release records. Remove or simplify whole-model mutation hashes, review/presentation hashes, batch/interaction hashes, schema hashes, blanket nested plan hashes, self-hashed receipt chains, run nonce/hash chains, repeated attempt/effect tuple hashes, duplicate ownership/Git receipt chains, evaluation closure hashes, and wrappers around Git OIDs or inode identities. The most urgent concrete reliability gap is project-model/focus lost updates: current load-mutate-rename has no process-shared lock or expected-revision check. Persisted V1 artifacts must remain readable; simplifications require versioned writers rather than reinterpretation.

proposals.body: The tool supplies state references, and the agent authors the full shell, styles, scripts, controls, and context.
proposals.rationale: This maximizes page freedom but retains repeated shell/control tokens and inconsistent review behavior.
proposals.title: Let the agent provide complete HTML

proposals.body: Every worker launched by this extension runs asynchronously relative to the main agent. Completion, failure, cancellation, and relevant result summaries are delivered back to the main agent without requiring it to block on a worker tool call.
proposals.rationale: This is explicit user direction in the focus seed and a core compatibility requirement for the desired DAG-centered experience; authority remains pending because the command seed was not receipt-eligible.
proposals.title: Always run extension workers asynchronously and report completion
tradeoffs: The main agent needs reliable wake-up and deduplicated completion delivery.
Worker results need bounded storage and replay after reload.
Background lifecycle introduces cancellation and orphan recovery requirements.

proposals.body: Spawn `npx -y lavish-axi` from the adapter and rely on the npm registry/cache for installation and version selection. Parse the current TOON output and fall back to chat on command failure.
proposals.rationale: Keeps Lavish out of package dependencies and mirrors the current skill workflow.
proposals.title: Invoke ambient npx Lavish on demand
tradeoffs: May access the network during a review.
Version drift can break output recognition without a project change.
npm/npx availability becomes an undeclared runtime requirement.

proposals.body: V1 may create a plan baseline from dirty tracked plus explicitly selected untracked/ignored source using a temporary index initialized from an immutable parent. Require direct user approval of the exact path/sensitivity manifest, pre/post file stability, closed symlink/filter/submodule rules, deterministic `write-tree`/`commit-tree`, an immutable private ref and snapshot receipt, and proof that user HEAD/index/files/stash/refs were unchanged. Missing or changing files block; broad `git add -A` and implicit secret/cache capture are forbidden.
proposals.title: Support explicit path-manifest snapshots without touching user state

proposals.body: Change launch guidance from a soft choice into a decision rule: continue only work that does not depend on the worker; at the first point where remaining work depends on it, end and settle the turn immediately. Do not poll, sleep, call status, or inspect to cross that barrier. Keep the parent task in progress and tell the user that no action is required because the completion follow-up will automatically start the next turn. Label status/inspect as diagnostic and recovery tools, not completion-waiting tools.
proposals.rationale: The current wording says the agent may continue or end the turn but does not identify the later dependency barrier. This permits one-turn completion bias to reappear after independent work is exhausted. An imperative transition rule explains that settling is normal continuation rather than abandonment.
proposals.title: State an imperative dependency-barrier rule for async workers
tradeoffs: A brief interim assistant response may be visible before the automatic completion turn.
The rule relies on the agent correctly recognizing when its remaining work is blocked.
Diagnostic inspection remains available for actual recovery without serving as a waiting primitive.

proposals.body: The conductor owns the worker state machine `pending → claimed → queued → running → terminal`, enforces dependency and capacity checks, persists the claim before launch, binds one worker/attempt ID to one process, ingests terminal results idempotently, advances or fails the node, schedules newly ready work, and exposes all transitions through one subscription. The main agent requests run-level actions but does not manually relay launch parameters or worker results.
proposals.rationale: This removes the partial-state windows and agent-mediated choreography in the legacy tools.
proposals.title: Use one atomic DAG worker conductor
tradeoffs: The conductor becomes a critical stateful component requiring transaction and crash tests.
Git worktree/merge transitions must remain separate from process completion.
Concurrent callbacks need one mutation queue per run.

proposals.body: Deliver one custom completion follow-up and treat the following `agent_settled` event as acknowledgement, then immediately schedule the next queue item without requiring an explicit tool disposition.
proposals.rationale: This has lower model/tool overhead and cannot stall because the agent omitted an acknowledgement call.
proposals.title: Auto-ack the in-flight completion when the top-level agent settles
tradeoffs: An aborted, failed, or irrelevant turn may be misclassified as handled.
There is no durable statement of what the agent did with the completion.
Reload/session replacement ambiguity can cause lost handling or duplicate side effects.

proposals.body: When a new Pi session header names the launching session file as `parentSession`, atomically rebind that source worker-session and its pending queue to the new session UUID after proving no attached source owner remains. Redirect later result ingestion and completion delivery to the descendant. New unrelated sessions and ordinary switches do not adopt workers.
proposals.rationale: Workers follow the user's active conversational branch with no manual resume step.
proposals.title: Automatically transfer live workers to a direct fork or clone
tradeoffs: A fork becomes a hidden side effect on worker ownership.
Returning to the parent can no longer receive its original completions.
Transfer needs durable source/target receipts and recovery across a crash midway.
Concurrent or chained forks require arbitration.

proposals.body: Track valid `subagent_report` capture as supervisor state. On the first `agent_settled` without a report, issue a deterministic report-only RPC follow-up that repeats the exact report schema and forbids additional task work. Wait for another settled state; use a small finite configurable retry count and emit report-missing/needs-attention when exhausted.
proposals.rationale: This implements the user's hybrid requirement without scraping prose or allowing an unbounded self-repair loop.
proposals.title: Prompt settled workers automatically when their report call is missing
tradeoffs: Adds another model turn when workers forget reporting.
The bounded retry count still needs a default.
A worker may report stale facts after partial failure.

proposals.body: Retain accepted product repair=3, infrastructure=1, and worker replacement=2. Add test-evidence rework=3 because codification may need iterative witnesses; review rework=2 and hardening rework=2 because each back-edge replays substantial lifecycle evidence; integration retry=1 because repeated drift/conflict should become an integration decision rather than blind churn. Counters remain per canonical failure fingerprint/dimension, no-progress/oscillation stops apply earlier, and explicit authorization profiles may narrow or raise exact retry ceilings without introducing time/cost/launch budgets.
proposals.title: Complete retry-only defaults with balanced evidence and integration ceilings

proposals.body: Standard controls queue prompts naming review ID, point ID, proposed action, option ID, and the displayed semantic hash/payload. The adapter returns only normalized prompts, tags, text/targets, user-ended state, and severe layout warnings; it drops the DOM snapshot unless explicitly requested, caps prompt count and total bytes, and uses Pi truncation metadata when needed. Within the trusted local agent/harness threat model, feedback returned through the active Lavish poll is assumed human-initiated and may create a review-scoped interaction receipt. The agent still interprets all feedback and calls `dag_model_resolve_review`; matching active review IDs and semantic hashes prevents stale or misrouted outcomes.
proposals.rationale: This preserves correction and ambiguity handling while preventing arbitrary DOM state from flooding model context or bypassing semantic review.
sourceRefs: Authority receipt and sparse resolution contracts
proposals.title: Return bounded Lavish feedback for agent interpretation
tradeoffs: Agent interpretation adds a model turn and can ask clarification.
Annotations and custom controls remain less mechanically structured than standard options.
Truncation must never silently turn partial feedback into authority.

proposals.body: Ordinary authorized independent authoring is not speculation. Future-prefix composition/verification classifies the strictest applicable green/amber/red risk. Green may look ahead at most three unaccepted predecessors. Amber may look ahead one, with two concurrent credits run-wide and one per repository. Red has zero. No class bypasses precedence, gates, authority, migration, irreversible/production effects, or integration order. Exact identity is required for adoption; predecessor change fences and invalidates the full affected suffix before cancellation.
proposals.title: Bound exact-prefix speculation by risk, credit, and causal distance

proposals.body: Return session/artifact references, session-ended status, normalized prompts with prompt/tag/text/selector/target and whiteboard summary/file references, plus severe layout warnings. Omit the DOM snapshot and server chatter from routine model content; save diagnostics by reference only when needed. Standard shell controls queue stable review-point/proposal IDs and human-readable labels. The agent interprets the packet and calls resolve_review; no transport field is persisted automatically.
proposals.rationale: The packet preserves user intent and precise annotation targets while excluding large page snapshots and operational prose that provide no routine reasoning value.
proposals.title: Return a bounded intent-transport packet, not raw poll output

proposals.body: If explicitly requested, create `spec/prototypes/lavish-turn-renderer/` with a fixture-driven `ModelReviewTurnProjection`, package-owned self-contained shell, standard sparse decision controls, trusted rich-context examples, deterministic focus/review artifact path, bounded feedback normalization, and fake Lavish open/poll/end scenarios. Include one opt-in live Lavish exercise. Do not register a production tool or mutate project-model authority from the prototype. Use the concrete result to refine projection fields, lifecycle states, limits, accessibility, and failure recovery before implementing the production adapter.
proposals.rationale: The broad product direction is settled; remaining uncertainty concerns concrete seams best exposed by a runnable artifact rather than more abstract review.
proposals.title: Build a bounded vertical Lavish turn-renderer prototype
tradeoffs: Adds a short prototype step before production implementation.
Avoids prematurely coupling production code to an untested projection/shell contract.
Must remain bounded and not become a second authority implementation.

proposals.body: Implement a strict LF parser with request IDs and one bounded in-memory record buffer. Discard `message_update` records without JSON object retention or persistence. Normalize only prompt response, `message_end` assistant final text/usage/model/stop reason, tool start/end names plus small path/progress summaries, retry/compaction state, `extension_error`, and `agent_settled`. Replace the worker mailbox at semantic progress transitions; do not write per-event history. Treat process exit before `agent_settled` as failure unless cancellation was requested. After settled, close RPC stdin and wait briefly for exit before verified TERM/KILL escalation.
proposals.rationale: This supplies live status and terminal evidence while obeying the accepted logging hotfix and avoiding the cumulative streaming object allocation/persistence path.
proposals.title: Project selected RPC events into bounded worker state
tradeoffs: Discarded event detail is unavailable for forensic replay.
Tool result normalization must avoid accidentally copying large accumulated payloads.
Protocol corruption needs a bounded diagnostic excerpt and terminal failure classification.

proposals.body: Render each queue item into a bounded follow-up containing completion ID, worker ID/label and attempt, canonical terminal status, report status, worker summary, artifact references, and a concise hint for `subagent_inspect`/`subagent_tail`. Include next steps only when present. Do not inject report details, raw transcript, tool history, diagnostic logs, or artifact contents. Cap the entire follow-up at 16 KiB with explicit truncation metadata; the immutable terminal result remains available to inspection. The first top-level `agent_settled` after this follow-up auto-acknowledges it under the accepted queue policy.
proposals.rationale: The top-level agent gets enough context to react without recreating the resource amplification or context pollution the owned runtime replaces.
proposals.title: Deliver a compact completion message with stable identity and inspect references
tradeoffs: The agent may need an inspection call for substantive details.
A long summary may be truncated below its report limit.
Artifacts can disappear or change after completion unless copied or hashed separately.

proposals.body: Store one atomic worker snapshot per attempt plus bounded result/artifact files. Keep recent progress as a small in-memory ring or fixed-size rotating diagnostic tail only when enabled. Do not copy child message deltas, reasoning, full tool results, or Pi session events into repository or global JSONL. Track timestamps, status, PID, current tool/path, usage, output references, and terminal error as explicit fields.
proposals.rationale: The conductor needs current state and terminal evidence, not a duplicate event ledger. Snapshot replacement makes disk use proportional to active workers rather than event volume.
proposals.title: Persist compact worker snapshots and bounded results, never raw event streams
tradeoffs: Less forensic detail than a full transcript.
Debug mode needs deliberate bounded capture and redaction.
Atomic snapshots require idempotent transition validation.

proposals.body: Use one shared pure renderer over `worker-session.json`. In TUI mode, install a below-editor component factory whose `render(width)` produces at most eight lines and whose cached state is invalidated with `tui.requestRender()` after canonical state or heartbeat ingestion. In RPC mode, send the same projection as conservative 80-column string arrays after semantic transitions. Use ASCII-safe states: `[ ]` queued, `[>]` starting, `[*]` running, `[R]` report repair, `[+]` succeeded pending delivery, `[!]` failed, `[-]` cancelled, `[L]` lost, and `[?]` needs attention. The header reports active, pending completion, and attention counts. At wide widths show up to five task rows with worker ID, attempt, status, age, and bounded label; compact widths reduce fields/rows; very narrow widths show summary plus the highest-priority row. Clear the widget once no active attempt, undrained completion, or attention item remains. Historical acknowledged workers remain available through explicit inspection, not the persistent widget.
proposals.rationale: A single bounded projection is testable, resize-aware in the TUI, usable through RPC, and updates naturally from already-required mailbox/state events without adding a high-frequency timer.
proposals.title: Render a bounded event-driven worker widget from canonical state
tradeoffs: RPC clients receive a conservative fixed-width projection rather than live terminal width.
Acknowledged successful workers disappear from the persistent widget.
Heartbeat frequency controls the coarseness of displayed ages.

proposals.body: The default detached authorization receipt binds exact plan/review projection hashes and authorizes all work items plus dependency/integration closure in every declared repository; all F0–F8 local/isolated activity; unrestricted architecture-preserving edits anywhere in each work item's repository; worktree/commit operations; per-repository rebase, exact-prefix verification, and fast-forward landing into declared targets; and reviewed reversible non-production external evaluation scopes, within bound budgets/retry policy. It has no path, directory, symbol, module, or internal-design limits and requires no repeated confirmation for normal retries/back-edges. Separate fresh authorization is required only for materially new semantic work, an undeclared repository/target, production deployment, irreversible/destructive external effects, credentials/effect scope beyond the plan, or budget escalation. Optional partial authorization must be mechanically dependency/effect/integration closed, remains visibly blocked elsewhere, and can only narrow the plan's maximum envelope. This is coordination under a trusted-agent threat model, not a security sandbox.
proposals.title: Default to broad whole-plan coordination authorization

proposals.body: Build the turn document as a hydrated framework application with packaged JavaScript and CSS assets.
proposals.rationale: This supports sophisticated components but adds a browser build pipeline, hydration/runtime complexity, and less transparent artifacts.
proposals.title: Ship a compiled client-side application bundle

proposals.body: Generate one self-contained HTML document from package-owned template, CSS, and standard control JavaScript; do not require Tailwind, DaisyUI, or remote assets at runtime. The shell owns navigation, Current understanding, awareness and decision cards, exact authority payload disclosure, recommendations, comments, queue/send actions, and responsive layout. Agent-authored presentation blocks may use Markdown, predefined components, trusted HTML/CSS/scripts, or links to sibling artifacts without a restrictive sandbox.
proposals.rationale: Bundling removes network/version drift and repeated shell boilerplate while preserving the accepted trusted-local expressiveness boundary.
proposals.title: Bundle a stable offline shell and allow trusted rich context
tradeoffs: Arbitrary context can still disturb shell usability, so layout diagnostics and conventions remain useful.
A bespoke shell needs accessibility and responsive tests.
Linked artifacts require relative-path and size safety.

proposals.body: Standardize the current artifact approach around browser-loaded Tailwind and DaisyUI versions.
proposals.rationale: This provides a broad component library quickly but requires network availability and a browser CSS compiler for the standard shell.
proposals.title: Generate a DaisyUI/Tailwind CDN shell

proposals.body: Explicitly expose only `subagent_report` from the worker-runtime extension inside ordinary children. The terminating tool validates and returns a bounded worker-authored report in tool details. The supervisor captures it from `tool_execution_end`, then waits for `agent_settled` or process failure and combines it with independently observed runtime metadata. If the worker settles without a valid report, run the bounded report-repair policy and preserve bounded final text rather than scraping authority or silently declaring success.
proposals.rationale: A structured terminal boundary supports deterministic DAG transitions and completion messages without granting the child DAG or project-model mutation authority.
proposals.title: Use one child-safe report tool with a bounded fallback
tradeoffs: Prompt compliance is not guaranteed, so fallback remains necessary.
The report schema must accommodate non-code research workers.
This makes structured results a future runtime decision even though the accepted incident baseline did not require them.

proposals.body: `DagRunStateV1` is the sole mutable DAG authority: a strict canonical snapshot containing immutable plan/receipt identity, owner/desired/current projections, repositories/work items/gates/precedence/resources/mutexes/leases, stage attempts/launch intents/worker bindings, immutable fact indexes, finding/retry/blocker/effect/cancellation/quarantine projections, freshness, integration trains, and completion. It stores references and current projections, never evidence bodies, transcripts, secrets, or plan copies. One pure reducer accepts a closed command/observation union with run nonce, owner epoch, expected revision, idempotency key, and payload hash; exact duplicates are no-ops, conflicts/stale inputs reject, readiness is derived, and revision/hash advance atomically. External work occurs only from persisted effect intents; notices are disposable projections, not event sourcing.
proposals.title: Use one closed atomic snapshot and pure guarded reducer

proposals.body: Define `CanonicalDagPlanV1` as a strict JSON object with exactly: `schemaVersion`, `kind`, `canonicalization`, `planId`, `revision`, optional `supersedesPlanHash`, `createdAt`, `generator`, `modelBinding`, `repositories`, `architecture`, `semanticSubjects`, `acceptanceOracles`, `workItems`, `gates`, `constraints`, `lifecycleBinding`, `artifactPolicy`, `projectionContract`, and `planHash`. `planHash` is SHA-256 over canonical JSON of every field except itself. Object keys sort recursively; schema-declared sets sort and deduplicate by stable key; semantically ordered arrays preserve order; duplicate keys, unknown fields, non-finite numbers, absolute paths, and malformed hashes fail. Every contract, oracle, work item, gate, and constraint has its own content hash. `planId` is stable across successor revisions; `revision` increases; `supersedesPlanHash` is mandatory after revision 1. Entity IDs never prove equivalence: evidence adoption after re-decomposition requires a detached receipt binding old/new plan, entity, oracle, input-closure, repository-tree, and content hashes. Creation/store provenance outside the closed envelope cannot alter plan meaning.
proposals.title: Use one closed content-hashed plan envelope with per-entity lineage

proposals.body: Bind Git/object/filesystem/config identity and explicitly declare required filters, submodules, LFS, generators, and hydration procedures. Prohibit custom/union merge drivers in v1; reject replace refs and unsupported shallow/partial/alternate object state unless a declared materialization procedure proves a closed local object set. Missing tools/objects/credentials, nondeterministic generators, unknown filters, unsupported filesystems, or untested object formats block rather than becoming not applicable.
proposals.title: Use a closed fail-closed Git capability profile

proposals.body: Define strict canonical schemas and source-join validators for review, authorization, deterministic authorization sets, boundary freshness, publication, lineage heads, explicit run request, and run-start bundles. Review binds exact candidate bytes and jointly recomputed architecture/decomposition/static-graph projections. Publication stores the same reviewed bytes and atomically advances exact lineage-head CAS without requiring authorization. Authorization remains independently composable within plan maximum. `/dag run` recomputes all sources and session preflight, derives scheduler/genesis/context internally, and starts only by immutable bundle hash through a starting-to-active session binding CAS. Remove public caller paths, max concurrency, nonce, timestamps, and self-attested receipt hashes from authoritative start.
proposals.title: Require a closed source-joined receipt stack from review through run start

proposals.body: On each terminal worker transition, atomically ingest the result and advance the DAG, append a compact non-context session pointer, and schedule a short coalescing window. Deliver one `followUp` custom message with `triggerTurn: true` containing all newly terminal workers, DAG transitions, newly ready work, failures, and decision needs. Deduplicate by worker-attempt completion ID so reloads or duplicate process events cannot wake the main agent twice.
proposals.rationale: This satisfies completion reporting without creating one expensive main-agent turn per worker in a fan-out burst.
proposals.title: Persist every completion and coalesce main-agent wakeups
tradeoffs: Completion reporting may be delayed briefly by the coalescing window.
The message must remain bounded and link to artifacts for details.
Exactly-once delivery requires persisted receipt IDs.

proposals.body: Terminal result ingestion advances the node/step and computes newly ready DAG work immediately, but the conductor does not auto-launch work unlocked by that completion until its queue item is acknowledged with a continue disposition. Already-running independent workers continue. Failure, report-missing, conflict, or needs-decision dispositions keep affected dependents blocked.
proposals.rationale: The top-level agent is expected to react to each completion before downstream work consumes it; otherwise serial message delivery would not provide meaningful control over DAG advancement.
proposals.title: Gate newly ready dependent launches until completion acknowledgement
tradeoffs: Burst completions can reduce throughput while the queue drains.
Independent newly-ready nodes may wait even when safe unless provenance is tracked per completion.
The ack tool needs an explicit disposition contract.

proposals.body: Bind an explicit capacity profile with four active non-integration external dispatches, initial/max implementation admission of two unless a lower observed/authorized cap applies, and at least one compatible shared slot reserved for ready F2/F5/F7/head integration before new F1. F2 and F5 each require one logical fresh-lineage service capacity; deterministic checks may use two subject to environments. Integration is one per Git common directory and never consumes implementation capacity. Missing required capacity observations mean zero; users may configure different validated capacities within semantic maxima.
proposals.title: Start with four external slots, two implementation slots, and one downstream reserve

proposals.body: Every plan context/evidence reference uses `ArtifactRefV1`: SHA-256 digest, byte size, media type, optional schema ID, sensitivity public/internal/restricted, retention ephemeral/run/project, and optional validated root-relative locator. Locator is never identity. Hydration verifies digest/size/type before launch; missing/mismatched content blocks; restricted content and even sensitive locators are omitted from general projections/completions and never auto-read/injected. Plans, receipts, run snapshots, widgets, reports, diagnostics, and durable artifacts contain no secret values. Symbolic credential requirements declare provider, scope, purpose, phases, environment, and semantic class auth-only/semantic-versioned/non-replayable; delivery is just-in-time outside durable records. A hash-bound artifact-policy profile supplies inline/count/byte limits, accepted roots/types, retention, and redaction; worktrees, dependency trees, and arbitrary directories are forbidden durable artifacts, while source identity uses repository commits/trees.
proposals.title: Use one bounded content-addressed artifact and sensitivity contract

proposals.body: Record operator blockers, decisions, authorization changes, waivers, cancellations, replans, active operator minutes when explicitly observed, authority-wait versus unattended time, and a three-item optional post-run pulse for confidence, cognitive effort, and interruption burden. Preserve raw items rather than a composite. Attribute exact model/provider/token/cache/reported-cost facts through exact worker bindings with coverage; report per started run, completed item, and accepted outcome without estimating missing fields or normalizing unlike profiles. Store no prompt/transcript bodies and perform no LLM-judge or semantic prompt scoring; later prompt evaluation requires its separately approved corpus/rubric.
proposals.title: Measure human attention and exact usage contextually while deferring prompt scoring

proposals.body: After mandatory reconciliation, order triggered fairness reservations first, then head integration/downstream evidence, repair work, initial authoring, and exact-prefix speculation. Within class prefer green over amber, greater unit-weight remaining milestone height, later lifecycle progress, genuine admission debt, train position, and stable IDs. Scan the full stream and admit every fitting item. After eight genuine competing bypasses, reserve the candidate's missing resource/mutex classes until it fits. Defer RCPSP optimization and DRF to dogfood evidence or a future shared multi-run pool.
proposals.title: Use deterministic vector first-fit with critical rank and bounded bypass fairness

proposals.body: Version the execution projection rather than silently widening V1. For each node, retain the exact joined worker process disposition and expose the ordered F0–F8 stage states plus candidate generation. Keep observation freshness outside the semantic projection. Preserve the existing exact plan/run/scheduler/worker join and omission behavior; V1 remains available for historical compatibility if needed.
proposals.rationale: The accepted spinner and progress semantics need fields already present in canonical inputs but omitted by V1; a narrow version bump keeps the contract explicit.
proposals.title: Add a narrow DagExecutionProjectionV2 for liveness and stage progress

proposals.body: Render a compact header plus an activity-centered topology lane for each currently active or attention node, preserving edges rather than replacing the graph with worker cards. Each lane shows alias/title, exact stage, a stage progress bar, elapsed time, and a spinner only when the joined worker projection proves a live process. Use remaining horizontal width for immediate downstream dependents, grouped by active parent, and collapse all other DAG state into small aggregate counts.
proposals.rationale: This directly prioritizes current activity, scales independently of total DAG size, and uses horizontal space for parallel lanes instead of one edge per row.
proposals.title: Replace the flat topology list with an activity spotlight

proposals.body: Treat an exact successful live-worker observation as fresh for 2.5 seconds. Advance spinner frames every 120 ms only while at least one selected node remains freshly live; otherwise stop the animation timer. A new non-live observation freezes immediately, and failed refreshes never extend freshness.
proposals.rationale: This tolerates one delayed one-second safety scan without allowing a cached live claim to persist for many seconds, while matching the reviewed prototype motion.
proposals.title: Use a 2.5-second liveness window and 120 ms active-only animation

proposals.body: First build a TUI reproduction harness, capture PI_TUI_WRITE_LOG and terminal dimensions, and identify the exact differential-render transition before changing production code.
proposals.rationale: This maximizes causal certainty but delays removal of a known render-width contract violation and may fail to reproduce an intermittent historical transition.
proposals.title: Block replacement implementation until the exact incident reproduces

proposals.body: Keep the persistent widget's deterministic bounded layout purpose-built around a selected activity neighborhood. Treat general diagram libraries as inspiration or as an implementation option for the separate full diagram tool, not as the primary widget renderer. Define narrow, medium, and wide breakpoints with a fixed row budget and ANSI-aware truncation.
proposals.rationale: The persistent widget has stricter activity selection, semantic truth, row stability, and resize behavior than a general graph renderer provides.
proposals.title: Prefer a purpose-built responsive renderer for the persistent widget

proposals.body: Proceed with Projection V2, the serialized disposable controller, exact-width rendering, stable breakpoint heights, and the regression harness. Keep PI_TUI_WRITE_LOG reproduction as an explicit diagnostic follow-up; if captured, add the exact transition as another regression without weakening the safety contract.
proposals.rationale: The known width-contract violation is independently actionable, and the accepted replacement architecture directly prevents all currently plausible corruption classes.
proposals.title: Implement now and keep exact incident reproduction nonblocking

proposals.body: Honor the exact render(width), including a minimal fallback below 20 columns; separate slow semantic refresh from lightweight animation; serialize refreshes so only one projection fetch is in flight; make every output line ANSI/Unicode visible-width safe; keep height stable for a given terminal breakpoint; clear timers and widget state atomically; guard render failures; and test resize, projection churn, teardown, diagnostics, Unicode width, and animation frames.
proposals.rationale: The preserved incident crosses the widget/editor boundary, so visual redesign should not proceed without explicit terminal rendering invariants.
proposals.title: Give the widget a render-safety contract and regression harness

proposals.body: Allow a five-second freshness window and use a slower 160 ms spinner while at least one selected node remains fresh.
proposals.rationale: This reduces flicker during temporary refresh failures but can imply current work for too long after an unobserved worker exit.
proposals.title: Use a 5-second liveness window and 160 ms active-only animation

proposals.body: Extend the semantic execution projection with an explicit worker process/activity disposition derived only from the exact joined worker binding. Animate a node while that disposition proves the bound process is live and the observation remains fresh; freeze to a static active mark when freshness expires without a terminal fact. Keep canonical node lifecycle and activity freshness as separate fields.
proposals.rationale: A local timer tied only to activeLane or worker presence can imply work is happening while a sticky lane is waiting or a process is dead.
proposals.title: Drive motion from exact fresh worker observations

proposals.body: Expire motion 1.25 seconds after the exact observation and animate at 120 ms only while fresh.
proposals.rationale: This minimizes stale claims but can visibly freeze during ordinary timer or status-scan jitter.
proposals.title: Use a 1.25-second liveness window and 120 ms active-only animation
