proposals.body: Ship `maxActiveNodes=2`. At run authorization the user may choose another positive integer up to validated worker/provider/resource and semantic safety maxima. The count controls admitted work items, not physical phase workers. Each active node retains its lane until integrated/complete, terminally cancelled, or moved to successor-plan/replan; blocked nodes are never parked automatically.
proposals.title: Default to two sticky active nodes with explicit validated override

proposals.body: Keep the static legacy `dag_diagram` diagnostic read-only. Do not adapt it to worker-session state or add DAG status/control semantics now. When planning/chunk/run is redesigned, define a separate canonical DAG execution projection and adapter that may combine DAG topology with generic worker references without allowing the worker runtime to own DAG transitions.
proposals.rationale: A live DAG requires authoritative topology and execution state that the generic subagent runtime intentionally does not own.
proposals.title: Defer live ASCII DAG topology to the future DAG adapter
tradeoffs: The original DAG-centered visual goal arrives later.
The generic worker widget cannot show dependency relationships.
Future integration must compose two state sources carefully.

proposals.body: Launch one detached, process-group-isolated supervisor per worker or bounded worker group. Persist its ownership token, PID/start identity, state snapshot, heartbeat, result envelope, and completion receipt. The Pi extension may unload or exit; on reload it scans active snapshots, verifies process identity, restores the DAG/widget projection, and ingests completed results. No always-running daemon or IPC service is introduced.
proposals.rationale: This is the missing middle ground demonstrated by `pi-subagents`: workers can survive Pi reload/exit without a durable daemon. An owned implementation can retain that useful lifecycle while replacing raw event logs and strengthening identity, reconciliation, and UI restoration.
proposals.title: Use detached per-run worker supervisors without a daemon
tradeoffs: Detached processes can become orphans and require explicit retention/reaping policy.
PID alone is unsafe because of reuse; ownership tokens and process start identity are required.
Completion cannot wake a nonexistent Pi process; it must be queued durably and delivered on reconnect.
It survives Pi exit but not necessarily machine reboot unless separately recovered.

proposals.body: Move worker processes and scheduling to a repository/user daemon so runs survive Pi reload and exit; Pi sessions attach through IPC and receive completion notifications after reconnect.
proposals.rationale: This maximizes durability for long runs and decouples worker lifetime from the interactive client.
proposals.title: Run workers in a detached durable daemon
tradeoffs: Requires authenticated IPC, daemon discovery, ownership leases, version compatibility, shutdown policy, log retention, and multi-session coordination.
Completion delivery after the owner disappears is substantially harder.
Expands v1 scope beyond the observed need.

proposals.body: Use a schema-versioned atomic `worker-session.json` as the canonical projection, written only through one in-process mutation queue owned by the attached top-level worker manager. It contains a monotonic revision, top-level session identity, owner epoch/process identity, worker attempts, ingested result hashes, and one completion queue. Attempt lifecycle is `queued → claimed → starting → running → terminal`, with terminal outcomes `succeeded | failed | cancelled | lost`, plus fail-closed needs-attention reasons for launch-ambiguous, identity-mismatch, stale-live, corrupt-artifact, or cwd-conflict. Detached supervisors write only nonce-correlated atomic mailboxes and one immutable terminal result; they never mutate workflow or DAG state. Reconnect scans terminal results first, then mailboxes, validates schema/identity/hash, ingests each result and enqueues completion in one atomic worker-session mutation, restores matching live attempts, marks proven-dead attempts lost, and routes uncertainty to needs-attention.
proposals.rationale: This creates one authoritative runtime projection without cross-process file locking, guarantees idempotent result ingestion, and fails safely across the irreducible process-spawn persistence gap.
proposals.title: Adopt a single-writer detached worker-session recovery contract
tradeoffs: The attached conductor remains a single-writer availability point for DAG advancement.
Ambiguous launches require human action instead of speculative retry.
The snapshot rewrites bounded structured state on each semantic transition, though not on streaming events.
Schema migration and corrupt-artifact quarantine need explicit tests.

proposals.body: `projectionContract` binds versioned pure projections for architecture/outcome review Markdown, decomposition review, static typed graph, bounded node execution packet, normalized scheduler indexes, optional explicitly non-executable legacy inspection, and `DagExecutionProjectionV1`. Every projection identifies plan hash, projection kind/version, and joined run/worker input hashes; set ordering and focus tie-breaks are deterministic. Node packets contain only the work item and referenced outcomes/contracts/oracles/context/policy facts and cannot broaden authority. The execution projection joins immutable plan topology with atomic run status and only worker attempts explicitly mapped by run state; it never infers DAG status from generic workers. Human Markdown remains a first-class generated view, not authority. Exact terminal glyphs, widths, topology slicing, and controls remain under the separate widget review contract.
proposals.title: Derive all plan and execution views from versioned projection contracts

proposals.body: Write the renderer-owned HTML to `.ai/model-sessions/<focus-id>/lavish/<review-id>.html`. The canonical path gives Lavish stable session identity and live reload. Store only presentation metadata in the ignored focus session: review ID, relative artifact path, status, last presentation hash, and whether the user ended the browser session. Preserve it while the review is unresolved; end and remove it after resolution. An interrupted poll resumes. A user-ended session falls back to chat unless the user explicitly requests reopen.
proposals.rationale: The artifact is disposable presentation state while unresolved meaning stays in the repository model and active review packet.
proposals.title: Use one deterministic ignored artifact per focus review
tradeoffs: Removing a resolved artifact loses the local visual record, which is intentionally non-authoritative.
User-ended state must be tracked to honor Lavish reopen etiquette.
Focus cleanup needs best-effort CLI end plus file removal.

proposals.body: A newly evidenced unordered incompatibility preserves the earliest committed reservation and generation-fences the later one before cancellation. Capacity reduction marks overcommit and blocks new leases; existing work continues unless evidence says overlap remains unsafe, then highest reservation sequence is fenced first. Build an indexed wait-for graph and classify deadlock only when an SCC has no internal/external/authorized release path. Hold the affected closure, allowing provably independent work; ambiguous scope blocks the run. Never break mutexes, reclaim by timeout, or invent precedence; plan-affecting discoveries require successor plan.
proposals.title: Fence later reservations and hold only the structurally affected scope

proposals.body: Replace ambient caller-supplied interactionRef authority with strict content-addressed HumanInteractionReceiptV1 facts created by trusted adapters from durable Pi entries, exact command custom entries, or raw untruncated Lavish feedback. Bind session header, repository, branch/leaf, full source content, exact presentation, independent typed decision slots, source timestamp, and receipt hash. Arbitrary agent tool arguments, generic prose inference, stale/off-branch entries, preselected controls, truncated feedback, and layout-only feedback cannot mint positive authority. Direct free text may request revisions or supply non-authoritative guidance; positive acceptance requires an exact hash-bearing command or structured control. Preserve independent plan-review and run-authorization slots even in one turn.
proposals.title: Require exact durable receipts for positive human authority

proposals.body: For every train entry, run its prefix profiles and all repository final profiles on the exact synthetic future commit before landing. Bind speculative evidence to the ordered predecessor/candidate/receipt set and exact environment tuple. Hold the per-common-dir integration lock from authoritative composition through landing reconciliation and receipt acceptance. Any external target movement invalidates current F8 integration readiness and all affected combined-prefix evidence, creates a new train generation, and reruns exact composition and checks.
proposals.title: Verify every future prefix fully and hold one repository lock through receipt acceptance

proposals.body: Compose exact Git identities with `git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=<sourceBase> <prefix> <candidate>` under one fixed isolated profile, then create one deterministic `commit-tree` commit with sole parent prefix. Fixed Pi-DAG attribution and immutable receipts/trailers preserve source candidate and authorship identity; source commit topology is not replayed. Stable patch/range diagnostics are non-authoritative. Any conflicted, custom-driver, or ambiguous composition fences the attempt and routes a new candidate through F1/fresh evidence; the conductor never edits, resolves, rebases, or cherry-picks integration content.
proposals.title: Use explicit-base merge-tree, synthetic first-parent commits, and no conductor conflict edits

proposals.body: Each DAG step resolves a worker profile containing model preference/fallback, thinking, idle/hard timeout, token/cost/turn budgets, built-in tool allowlist, optional extension allowlist, system prompt, context inputs, cwd/worktree, and output schema. Default to fresh context containing the relevant generated spec slice, plan/chunk, DAG step, acceptance criteria, owned/forbidden files, and prior-step artifact references. Do not expose project-model authority mutation tools or recursive worker launch tools to workers.
proposals.rationale: Explicit profiles make worker capability reviewable and prevent ambient parent configuration from silently expanding authority or context.
proposals.title: Launch workers from explicit role, context, and tool profiles
tradeoffs: Profiles add schema and migration work.
Some project-specific tools need deliberate child compatibility adapters.
Fresh context requires careful task construction.

proposals.body: Leave launch-session ownership unchanged by default, but expose an explicit adopt action from a direct descendant session. Adoption verifies parent linkage, repository/cwd, no attached source manager, and immutable worker identities, then records a durable transfer receipt and changes only completion delivery ownership; running attempt origin IDs remain unchanged.
proposals.rationale: This balances safe defaults with continuity when the user intentionally moves work to a new session.
proposals.title: Allow explicit worker-session adoption by a replacement session
tradeoffs: Adds a transfer state machine and recovery contract.
Partial adoption would be unsafe, so the whole source queue must move together.
The distinction between attempt origin and completion owner complicates inspection.

proposals.body: Use the next focused research/design burst to specify the durable worker state machine, reconciliation algorithm, serial completion queue, and RPC child contract together. Then derive the live ASCII widget from that single state projection and only afterward restore model-aware planning/chunk/run integration.
proposals.rationale: The UI and DAG scheduler both consume the same state transitions. Settling recovery and queue semantics first avoids building a display around transient in-memory state or reviving the legacy multi-call choreography.
proposals.title: Explore detached recovery and conductor semantics before UI polish
tradeoffs: Delays visible UI iteration.
Combines several tightly coupled lifecycle questions in one frontier.
Planning/execution integration remains deferred for one more burst.

proposals.body: Implement the worker runtime inside this extension rather than relying on `pi-subagents`, so resource bounds, async lifecycle, completion reporting, DAG relationships, and UI state share one explicit contract.
proposals.rationale: This reflects the user's explicit seed direction, but the command-seed transport did not provide an eligible direct-authority receipt; preserve it as recommended pending the next authority-capable turn.
proposals.title: Replace pi-subagents with an extension-owned runtime
tradeoffs: Owning process/session orchestration increases implementation and maintenance scope.
Pi-native primitives and ecosystem code may still be reused as evidence or low-level mechanisms.
The migration must avoid silently changing worker prompts, tool access, or isolation.

proposals.body: Persist repository/run/node/step/attempt IDs, an unguessable ownership token, supervisor PID, OS process start identity, config path/hash, heartbeat, and worktree path/branch in the worker mailbox. On reconnect classify each active attempt as terminal-result-present, live-and-matching, missing, stale-heartbeat, PID-reused/identity-mismatch, corrupt, or launch-ambiguous. Ingest terminal results idempotently; attach only to matching live workers; never signal an identity mismatch; and never auto-relaunch into an ambiguous or possibly owned worktree. Route ambiguity, stale live workers, corruption, and dirty worktrees to `needs_decision`.
proposals.rationale: OS process creation and durable claim persistence cannot be made one atomic transaction. Failing closed in the small crash window is safer than duplicate agents editing one worktree or killing an unrelated reused PID.
proposals.title: Fail closed on ambiguous detached-worker ownership
tradeoffs: Some recoverable crashes require human retry decisions.
Process start identity is platform-specific; unsupported platforms must degrade to conservative behavior.
Heartbeat thresholds affect how quickly missing workers are recognized.

proposals.body: Make a compiler-owned atomic planning transaction the only producer of executable canonical plans. Join every governing claim to the exact accepted project-model object and acceptance receipt; bind exact architecture/decomposition projection hashes in a detached review receipt and closed plan authorization receipt; rerun selector, generated-spec, artifact, capability, repository source, and target observations at compile, review, authorize, and start. Derive complete content-hashed node packets from the transitive referenced slice. Treat unknown semantic overlap, missing oracle coverage, prototype ambiguity, partial compilation, and plan-affecting execution discoveries as fail-closed gates requiring review or a successor plan.
proposals.title: Compile plans through source-joined authority and freshness closure

proposals.body: Atomically record each plan-affecting finding with a whole-run no-new-dispatch-or-integration fence, candidate-generation fencing, durable cancellation/reconciliation intents, and late-result quarantine. After that CAS, idempotently create one non-authoritative execution discovery keyed by finding hash; only human review may change governing authority. Integrate or dismiss outcomes both require a distinct lineage-CAS successor plan and run; unresolved findings leave the old run fenced. Preserve sealed predecessor candidate facts and private refs. Permit only explicit, independently authorized, mechanically exact-equivalent candidate adoption into the successor, then rerun F0–F8 and all evidence; non-equivalent candidates are bounded F1 seed context only.
proposals.title: Fence plan-affecting findings and require reviewed successor plans

proposals.body: Atomically reserve separate product-repair, evidence/review/hardening rework, infrastructure, worker replacement, stage-entry, worker-start, wall-time, artifact, compute, and external-effect ceilings; consumed work remains charged after cancellation/loss. Normalize failure fingerprints and define progress as a relevant candidate delta, closed finding, strictly smaller failing set, or new route-changing evidence. Stop on the same fingerprint after two materially different failed repairs, two consecutive no-progress iterations, any repeated candidate tree, repeated A→B→A oscillation, or exhausted ceiling. Recommend `standard-v1`: three product repairs per fingerprint/class, one infrastructure retry, two worker replacements per stage, 30 stage entries, 12 worker launches, 120 minutes wall time, and 64 MiB retained evidence; metered token/cost ceilings are explicit when enforceable rather than guessed. Budget increases beyond authorization require a fresh receipt.
proposals.title: Use finite hierarchical budgets and mechanical no-progress stops

proposals.body: Validate immutable topology—including precedence plus gate-evidence producer SCCs—before authorization. Derive correctness-ready slots without capacity; classify speculative safety; admit a mutex/vector-capacity-compatible subset; then dispatch only from atomic leases and persisted effect intents. Run overlays may add holds/exclusions, reserve more declared units, reduce capacity, fence generations, or restore operational narrowing within accepted maxima. Missing dependency/effect/gate/repository/oracle/migration semantics always require a successor plan. Paths remain advisory.
proposals.title: Use five explicit scheduler layers and monotone runtime narrowing

proposals.body: Every node uses the same guarded evidence lifecycle, but states do not imply one worker launch each. F0 frame/preflight binds the independent acceptance oracle, risk, baseline, capabilities, and applicable checks. F1 build candidate runs one long-lived implementation worker with an internal edit → parse/build/typecheck/lint/static/security/architecture-fitness loop until clean or honestly blocked. F2 a fresh evaluator exercises behavior against the oracle. F3 codifies required behavior and repaired failures as targeted tests/corpora, with defective-revision witnesses where feasible. F4 runs focused, affected, and broader accumulated verification. F5 a fresh implementation/architecture reviewer records typed findings. F6 hardens risk-selected surfaces: production defects return to F1 and then must pass F3/F4; test-sensitivity gaps such as meaningful surviving mutants may go directly to F3; material architecture issues return to F5/replan; equivalent findings and tool limits require explicit disposition. F7 performs a clean final rerun. F8 emits an integration-ready evidence bundle. The DAG integration train rebases/composes and verifies exact future combined states before completion. Failures follow typed back-edges with finite budgets. Node-specific input may add bounded context, acceptance scenarios, risk, and check applicability, but cannot replace or reorder the fixed evidence checkpoints.
proposals.rationale: This preserves the user's opinionated evidence loop while keeping high-frequency edit/static feedback in one context, retaining independent evaluators/reviewers where they add real evidence, and adding bounded autonomy and post-integration correctness.
proposals.title: Adopt a fixed evidence-producing node state machine
tradeoffs: The exact composite ordering has medium rather than universal empirical support.
Internal worker loops need bounded diagnostics and no-progress detection.
Independent evaluation and review still add latency and model cost.
Risk-selected hardening and applicability require global policy while checkpoints remain fixed.

proposals.body: Make the active focus the user-facing routing and review context for `/dag plan`, and link it to one exact run-grade planning transaction. The transaction store owns revision/snapshot CAS, process ownership, idempotency, immutable phase facts, publication, and recovery. The user remains in one focus and can complete planning, implementation, release verification, commit, and push in this workstream without managing a second workflow or waiting for a future release slice.
proposals.title: Keep `/dag plan` seamless in the focus while storing run-grade state separately

proposals.body: Expose an always-async `subagent` launch tool plus narrow `subagent_status`, `subagent_inspect`, `subagent_tail`, `subagent_cancel`, and `subagent_retry` tools for the top-level agent. Expose `subagent_report` as the structured child-report tool. Provide equivalent `/workers` user commands for list, inspect, tail, cancel, and retry. Remove the dormant `dag_subagent` adapter and do not reuse `/dag` for generic worker control.
proposals.rationale: Names should reflect the accepted DAG-agnostic runtime and replace the existing pi-subagents workflow without preserving its private API shape.
proposals.title: Replace DAG-prefixed worker controls with a generic subagent namespace
tradeoffs: Renames the previously proposed `dag_worker_report` tool.
A broad `subagent` name can collide if another extension is loaded.
Separate narrow management tools enlarge the active tool list.

proposals.body: Project the attached top-level session's canonical worker state into a passive string-line widget below the editor. Show a summary header and bounded rows for active, report-repair, pending-completion, failed/lost, and needs-attention workers; clear it when no active, queued, in-flight, or attention state remains. Use event-driven snapshot/mailbox updates rather than a high-frequency UI timer. Provide separate user commands and narrow top-level tools for list, inspect, bounded diagnostic tail, cancel, and retry. Do not display DAG nodes, edges, readiness, worktrees, or merge state.
proposals.rationale: This preserves immediate async-worker visibility without coupling the generic runtime to the deferred DAG redesign, and Pi supports the same bounded string projection in TUI and RPC.
proposals.title: Ship a bounded generic worker activity widget plus explicit controls
tradeoffs: A worker list is less visually distinctive than the desired DAG.
Stable width tiers and recent-terminal retention still need exact values.
Cancel and retry semantics need to follow the canonical attempt state machine.

proposals.body: Extend the DAG-agnostic owned runtime with process-shared worker-session CAS, opaque caller launch key plus normalized request hash, reserve-or-return-existing exact attempts, conflicting-request rejection, exact storage/session/worker/attempt/nonce/config/process identity, durable result enumeration independent of completion auto-ack, retry-safe process disposition separate from terminal status, owner-managed retries, and verified approved disposable working roots. The DAG adapter supplies opaque IDs and interprets results, while the generic runtime remains unaware of plans, stages, gates, worktrees, or integration.
proposals.title: Harden generic worker primitives instead of duplicating them in the DAG adapter

proposals.body: Search PATH for lavish-axi and otherwise invoke npx -y lavish-axi at presentation time.
proposals.rationale: This avoids package dependency weight but creates version drift, network behavior, and less reproducible integration.
proposals.title: Require a global command or run npx latest

proposals.body: Define `CanonicalDagPlanV1` as the sole immutable architecture/decomposition authority. A separate `PlanReviewReceipt` binds the rendered review projection and plan hash; a separate `PlanAuthorizationReceipt` binds exact plan hash plus authorized work-item/phase/effect/repository closure and budget ceilings. `DagRunStateV1` is one atomic mutable conductor snapshot referencing those hashes; evidence envelopes and generic worker results remain immutable bounded external records. Plan lineage uses `supersedesPlanHash` and per-entity hashes; no status, attempts, leases, approval fields, or evidence bodies enter the plan.
proposals.title: Keep immutable planning separate from operational authorization and execution

proposals.body: Promote the validated seams into production modules: a domain-owned `ModelReviewTurnProjection` generated from the actual active focus, model revision/hash, Current understanding, selected frontier/delta, and exact active review; optional focus presentation metadata; package shell renderer; pinned optional Lavish CLI adapter; active `dag_model_present_review` tool with present/resume/end; bounded feedback details; exact tool-result presentation receipts; resolution cleanup; fake-CLI tests; and one opt-in real-browser gate. Reuse contracts deliberately rather than importing prototype modules. Production dogfood is complete when one real multi-point model review is generated, presented, responded to, semantically resolved through existing tools, and cleaned up without manual presentation-marker recovery.
proposals.rationale: The broad decisions and first concrete seams are settled; another abstract pass is unlikely to reduce more risk than production dogfood.
proposals.title: Implement the production Lavish presentation adapter from prototype findings
tradeoffs: Production integration will expose additional Pi lifecycle details.
The prototype remains evidence and should not become a runtime dependency.
A user visual pass may still request shell iteration before or during production work.

proposals.body: Derive serialization edges from explicit non-parallelism evidence: producer/consumer dependencies, shared unresolved architecture decisions, incompatible contracts or migrations, overlapping semantic ownership, shared mutable runtime resources, required feedback from one node into another, or integration order constraints. Do not use file allowlists as a proxy for independence.
proposals.title: Assume nodes are parallel until an incompatibility is proven

proposals.body: Snapshot the parent's active tool names at launch and pass a child allowlist containing all unrelated active tools plus `subagent_report`, but excluding `subagent`, `subagent_status`, `subagent_inspect`, `subagent_tail`, `subagent_cancel`, `subagent_retry`, all `dag_*`, and all `dag_model_*`. Load normal extensions, providers, skills, templates, and project context. Worker-role metadata causes this extension's normal entrypoint to return before attaching parent writer/watcher/dispatcher/UI services; only the child-report registration remains. The worker prompt says not to delegate. Do not maintain a brittle list of arbitrary third-party delegation tools; after removing `pi-subagents`, any separately installed orchestrator is governed by instructions. Interactive UI requests are answered with cancellation by the RPC supervisor so they cannot hang the child.
proposals.rationale: This is the narrow established Pi pattern: preserve useful child capabilities, remove only parent orchestration/authority surfaces owned here, and keep nested fanout as an explicit future opt-in.
proposals.title: Inherit normal tools while omitting parent orchestration surfaces
tradeoffs: The launch command uses an explicit tool list even though the policy is ambient inheritance minus a narrow set.
A separately installed third-party delegation tool remains visible unless configured elsewhere.
Future nested fanout requires a child-safe subagent variant and depth contract.

proposals.body: Create one isolated `AgentSession` per worker with an in-memory `SessionManager`, minimal `ResourceLoader`, explicit built-in tools, direct event subscriptions, cancellation, timeout, and disposal. Share or reconstruct model/auth services and keep all worker state in the extension process.
proposals.rationale: This avoids subprocess startup, JSON transport, and disk sessions while providing direct typed events and low-latency progress.
proposals.title: Run workers as in-process Pi SDK sessions
tradeoffs: Worker resource leaks and crashes share the main Pi process.
ExtensionContext does not publicly expose the canonical `ModelRuntime`; ecosystem implementations reach private model-registry fields or reconstruct services, which may miss custom provider behavior.
No OS-level containment and harder orphan diagnosis.

proposals.body: Extend `dag_model_review` with a presentation mode. In Lavish mode the semantic tool creates the review, renders and opens the artifact, waits for feedback, and returns it to the agent; resume/end actions are also folded into that tool.
proposals.rationale: One agent call creates and presents a review and keeps the active tool list at six.
proposals.title: Integrate Lavish presentation into dag_model_review
tradeoffs: Conflates semantic packet creation with an optional long-running presentation transport.
Resume and layout-repair actions complicate the existing review schema.
A CLI failure becomes a failure of the semantic review tool.

proposals.body: F8 is a deterministic no-edit conductor seal. It requires current plan/review/authorization and entity hashes; clean exact candidate commit/tree and lineage; one current legal F0–F7 evidence chain; valid F2/F5 freshness; F7 exact-final replay; no unresolved blocking/material finding; valid applicability/waivers; hydrated bounded artifacts; reconciled side effects; released enqueue gates; and declared integration obligations. Its immutable receipt means integration_ready only. Completion requires a separate integration receipt proving composition/rebase onto exact accepted prefix, no unreviewed semantic conflict edits, exact prefix/final profile success on resulting tree, compare-and-swap/fast-forward landing, and downstream invalidation. Conflict edits return to the earliest affected lifecycle stage.
proposals.title: Derive F8 integration readiness and completion from exact evidence closure

proposals.body: Provide a focusable custom TUI surface for selecting DAG nodes/workers, opening live bounded transcripts, steering, cancelling, retrying, and navigating dependency context directly from the graph.
proposals.rationale: This offers the richest operator experience and follows FleetView/thread-viewer ecosystem patterns.
proposals.title: Build an interactive DAG FleetView
tradeoffs: Custom focus, keyboard, resize, scrolling, and lifecycle behavior substantially expand the first slice.
RPC and non-TUI modes need a separate representation.
Live transcript storage conflicts with the goal of minimal bounded event retention unless carefully designed.

proposals.body: Resolve the exact running Pi invocation using the official example's algorithm and launch with `shell:false`, the node worktree cwd, `--mode rpc`, `--no-extensions`, `--no-skills`, `--no-prompt-templates`, and an explicit tool allowlist. Select the parent `ctx.model` provider/id and `ctx.thinkingLevel` unless the DAG step overrides them. Inherit the process environment and normal Pi authentication/config; pass only reviewed extra environment. Explicitly load a tiny child-safe report extension and any profile-approved provider/tool extensions. Default to `--no-session`; allow a token-bound per-attempt `--session-dir` only for roles that need continuation evidence. Project context-file inheritance is an explicit profile switch, defaulting on for trusted implementation worktrees. Never load DAG/model-authority or worker-launch tools in a child.
proposals.rationale: This preserves exact installed Pi/auth compatibility while preventing recursive workers and ambient extension/tool authority.
proposals.title: Launch Pi RPC through explicit isolated worker profiles
tradeoffs: Custom providers need explicit extension mapping.
Some project workflows depend on global skills/MCP extensions that must be deliberately added to a profile.
Ephemeral sessions reduce post-run transcript inspection unless a role opts in.

proposals.body: Bind each worker-session snapshot and completion queue permanently to `SessionManager.getSessionId()` of the launching top-level Pi session. Reload or resume of that UUID reattaches and drains it. Fork, clone, new-session, and switch do not transfer live workers or queue ownership. A descendant may discover and show a bounded read-only notice that its parent session has live or pending workers, but cannot deliver or control them through its own manager. The user resumes the launch session to handle them. Explicit transfer/adoption is deferred unless field use proves it necessary.
proposals.rationale: This directly preserves one queue per top-level session, avoids hidden cross-session side effects and dual dispatchers, and requires no distributed transfer protocol.
proposals.title: Keep workers and completions with their launch-session UUID
tradeoffs: Forking away can leave completions waiting in the original session.
The user may need to resume the launch session.
Read-only parent discovery must remain bounded and cannot expose child transcripts.

proposals.body: Treat Lavish poll results as non-authoritative user feedback and presentation evidence. The agent interprets and summarizes selected reviewed outcomes in Pi chat, then asks the user for one explicit confirmation. Only that Pi input creates the interaction receipt used by `dag_model_resolve_review`. Lavish can still drive awareness, annotations, corrections, navigation, and proposed sparse outcomes without authority. A later trusted-action protocol could remove the confirmation step.
proposals.rationale: This preserves unrestricted rich context and the current mechanical authority boundary without relying on provenance Lavish does not provide.
proposals.title: Require Pi confirmation before Lavish feedback grants authority
tradeoffs: Adds one short Pi confirmation after browser review.
The browser cannot be the sole decision channel in V1.
Safe to ship against current Lavish without upstream changes.

proposals.body: Each catalog check is required, conditional with a deterministic predicate, or plan-declared not applicable; F0 confirms the result. Missing tools, credentials, time, or failed observations are BLOCKED/FAIL, never N/A. Waivers are detached exact-scope human/policy receipts, never self-issued, apply only to checks, expose residual risk, and expire on relevant plan/oracle/candidate/environment/rebase change. Plan/authorization identity, immutable baseline, evidence integrity, independent F2/F5, clean F7, F8 integrity, and authorization for undeclared/production/irreversible scope are non-waivable. External procedures declare pure/idempotent/compensatable/non_repeatable/unknown replay classes; durable effect intent and reconciliation precede retry, and unknown/non-repeatable effects never auto-retry.
proposals.title: Keep applicability, waivers, and side-effect replay fail-closed

proposals.body: Use separate finite retry counters for product repair, evidence/review/hardening rework, infrastructure failure, worker replacement, and integration retries. Default to three product repairs per normalized fingerprint/class, one controlled infrastructure retry per procedure/fingerprint, and two replacement workers per stage. Stop earlier after the same fingerprint survives two materially different repair commits, two consecutive no-progress attempts, a repeated candidate tree, or repeated A→B→A oscillation. Infrastructure retries never consume product-repair counts, cancellation/loss does not reset counts, and effect retries remain constrained by replay class and reconciliation. Do not impose lifecycle-wide wall-time, token, cost, stage-entry, worker-launch, compute, or artifact ceilings; bounded artifacts remain governed by the separately accepted artifact policy. Increasing retry ceilings beyond authorization requires fresh authorization.
proposals.title: Limit lifecycle retries without global time, cost, or launch budgets

proposals.body: F0/F8 are conductor computations; F1 is one logical long-lived implementation/static thread across repair back-edges; F2 is a fresh read-only evaluator for every behavior-bearing candidate; F3 normally reuses F1; F4 is a deterministic no-edit runner; F5 is a fresh read-only reviewer distinct from F1/F2; F6 uses deterministic tools and a fresh adversarial evaluator only where judgment/generation matters; F7 uses a newly materialized clean no-edit environment. F3 preserves F2 only when a hash-bound repository profile mechanically attests an evidence-only delta; unknown or behavior-bearing edits route through F1 and fresh F2. Any candidate change after F5 invalidates F5 onward. F7 replays mandatory automatable behavior on the exact final tree. Freshness packets exclude hidden predecessor reasoning and bind allowed inputs and read/write mode.
proposals.title: Bind worker continuity, fresh evaluation, and conservative evidence invalidation

proposals.body: Adapt the existing width-aware ASCII graph renderer to accept `RunState` and decorate each node with stable compact status glyphs for blocked, ready, queued, running, passed, merge-ready, merged, failed, cancelled, and needs-decision. Show the diagram below the editor while a run is active, rerender on state transitions, and use a low-frequency timer only for elapsed-time text. Provide commands/tools for full diagram, node/worker detail, output tail, cancel, and retry rather than making the widget itself a dense control panel.
proposals.rationale: Pi's widget API can present a persistent live DAG without polluting model context, while the existing renderer already handles width, fan-out/fan-in, ordering, and warnings.
proposals.title: Render a live status-aware ASCII DAG widget
tradeoffs: Large DAGs need viewport/summary behavior.
RPC mode receives string lines rather than interactive components.
Interactive cancellation still needs commands or a separate custom surface.

proposals.body: Generate one strict content-addressed `RunEvaluationEnvelopeV1` for each terminal run or explicit censored checkpoint, binding evaluation profile, plan/run/source hashes, coverage, censoring, invariants, outcomes, attempts, retries, findings, integration, timing, parallelism, human, and usage aggregates. Add a separate non-authoritative atomic `RunObservationAccumulatorV1` for open readiness/active/human/recovery intervals plus fixed counters/sums/histograms; it stores no transition list and folds closed intervals. Observer failure drops telemetry and marks gaps without backpressure or execution effect. V1 is local-only with no export. Delete sidecars after a validated final envelope plus seven days; retain at most the latest 50 bounded final envelopes per project, with manually promoted project-model evidence preserving selected durable conclusions.
proposals.title: Use local bounded evaluation envelopes plus a lossy atomic observation accumulator

proposals.body: V1 never uploads or exports telemetry. Delete a run accumulator after a validated terminal envelope has existed for seven days, allowing bounded correction/recovery. Retain at most the latest fifty bounded final/censored envelopes per project using deterministic terminal/cutoff order and expected-hash cleanup. Before cleanup, durable conclusions may be explicitly promoted as project-model evidence. Cross-run reports are disposable projections over an explicit compatible envelope cohort; no mutable metrics database or indefinite raw artifact retention.
proposals.title: Keep telemetry local and retain seven-day sidecars plus the latest fifty envelopes

proposals.body: Define `subagent_report` as a terminating tool with required `outcome: completed | needs_attention` and `summary`, plus optional bounded `details`, artifact references, and next steps. It does not require changed files, tests, model/spec IDs, validator verdicts, retryability, or DAG fields. Use schema-level item/string caps and reject a serialized payload over 64 KiB. Suggested bounds: summary 8 KiB, details 32 KiB, at most 32 artifact references, and at most 16 next-step strings. Artifact paths are opaque references and are not automatically read or injected. The latest valid call is captured, though `terminate: true` normally makes the first valid call final.
proposals.rationale: A small common core works for coding, review, and research workers and avoids making every child fabricate irrelevant structured fields.
proposals.title: Use a minimal generic terminating subagent report
tradeoffs: The top-level agent must interpret code changes, checks, and findings from prose when needed.
Task-specific automation gets fewer typed fields.
Optional details may still contain heterogeneous content.

proposals.body: For V1, limit mutable authority to three inspectable JSON snapshots: planning transaction, existing run state, and release closure. Give transactions, reviews, authorizations, runs, attempts, findings, and releases stable UUIDs; use integer revision plus process-shared lock for mutation; durably replace snapshots with fsync/rename/fsync. Keep hashes only when exact content equality or content-addressed hydration is the practical requirement: canonical plan bytes, independently stored artifacts, targeted model closure, and one reviewed packet digest. Use native Git OIDs directly. Bind stale review responses through transaction revision, candidate plan hash, review ID, and packet digest. Publish exact reviewed plan bytes under a lineage lock and recover lagging transaction state from the head. Derive run inputs internally and use a persisted start ID with recoverable starting-to-active binding; hash the start bundle only if byte-for-byte restart reproduction proves necessary. Persist natural operation keys and request payloads before external effects, then reconcile observations. Remove security-attestation language and redundant self-hash chains.
proposals.title: Use minimal local durability primitives instead of receipt chains

proposals.body: Drop `message_update`, retain final message, tool, lifecycle, and control diagnostics, and cap each child diagnostic log at 50 MiB. Do not make atomic conductor behavior, structured results, idempotent recovery, explicit worker profiles, or other lifecycle constraints part of this baseline decision.
proposals.rationale: This is the smallest direct response to the measured incident and avoids expanding one logging bug into a broad runtime-hardening project.
proposals.title: Apply only the observed logging hotfix
tradeoffs: Other correctness and recovery requirements would need separate decisions.
Detached ownership, duplicate completions, and partial DAG transitions could remain unsafe.
A log cap treats symptoms if another cumulative event type appears.

proposals.body: Render a width-aware ASCII slice centered on running nodes and their immediate predecessors, successors, blockers, and ready frontier. Use stable character status marks for running, ready, pending/blocked, complete, failed, and needs-decision. Pair the graph with a compact running list showing node, fixed phase, elapsed time, worker attempt, and short status. Large graphs collapse remote completed/pending regions into counts. Iterate examples through several review turns before implementation.
proposals.rationale: This directly serves the user's need to understand DAG edges and active work inside Pi instead of presenting generic worker cards.
proposals.title: Prototype a monospaced topology-slice DAG widget
tradeoffs: A focused slice can hide distant critical-path context.
Unicode glyph width varies; an ASCII fallback is required.
Status and edge density need narrow-terminal rules.
The projection contract must define which neighbors remain visible.

proposals.body: Schema v1 uses `repositories[]` with stable root-independent IDs, canonical identities, immutable commit/tree baselines, roles, and per-repository integration trains. Each executable work item writes at most one repository; verification may consume exact commits from several. The initiating repository model remains primary semantic authority; other repository models/contracts are separately bound inputs. Planning may inspect dirty user state, but execution starts only from a user-approved immutable snapshot commit/tree created without cleaning, resetting, stashing, or overwriting the user worktree. Unsupported cross-repository execution fails validation rather than becoming an undeclared absolute-path edit.
proposals.title: Represent repositories explicitly and authorize immutable tree baselines

proposals.body: Generate one strict content-addressed `RunEvaluationEnvelopeV1` per terminal run or explicit censored checkpoint, with exact profile/source hashes, coverage/censoring/clock status, invariants, outcomes, attempts, findings, integration, timing, parallelism, human, and usage aggregates. Add a separate non-authoritative atomic accumulator for open readiness/active/human/recovery intervals and fixed counters/sums/histograms. It keeps no transition list, folds closed intervals, observes only after authoritative commits, may drop and mark gaps, never backpressures execution, and is never imported by reducer/scheduler/evidence/Git/widget authority.
proposals.title: Separate a reproducible evaluation envelope from a lossy interval accumulator

proposals.body: Use one explicitly human-reviewed bootstrap plan and authorization under the existing runtime for the minimum self-hosting slice: planning transaction/lineage store, source-joined compiler and receipts, deterministic `/dag show`, focus-linked `/dag plan`, and fresh start-bundle `/dag run`. Record that authority as transitional human-reviewed bytes rather than compiler output. From that committed baseline, use the new planner for finding fences, model discovery handoff, successor candidate adoption, complete run UX, release closure, and end-to-end tests. Deliberately inject one fixture plan-affecting finding, compile a successor, adopt one exact-equivalent candidate, reject one non-equivalent candidate, and finish through the successor before the final release matrix and explicit release closure.
proposals.title: Bootstrap the compiler once, then self-host successor and release behavior

proposals.body: After exact verification, create an immutable proposal ref. For a normal non-bare repository, stop at `awaiting_user_handoff` and let the user perform a normal Git fast-forward in a selected worktree; observe and accept only the exact proposed OID/tree. Automated expected-old `update-ref` is allowed only for a declared bare or conductor-exclusive target. Any missing or third OID—including a same-tree commit—blocks; no equivalence inference or automatic backward ref movement is allowed. Later defects use a new forward repair/revert work item.
proposals.title: Use user handoff for normal branches and automate only exclusive targets

proposals.body: Each selected active or attention anchor owns one bounded lane row: activity cell, stable primary mark and alias, stage/progress, truncated title, then directed immediate dependents and an explicit overflow count. Optional second rows are reserved for blocker/attention detail rather than repeating topology. Shared dependents may appear by alias in multiple anchor lanes while node omission counts remain global and deterministic.
proposals.rationale: One lane per anchor uses horizontal space, preserves causal direction, and avoids both one-edge-per-row explosion and tall boxed cards.
proposals.title: Render one compact horizontal lane per activity anchor

proposals.body: When the first `agent_settled` arrives without a valid report, send one deterministic report-only RPC prompt restating the schema and requiring `subagent_report` as the only action. If the second run settles without a valid report, finalize as report-missing/needs-attention with bounded final text. Expose `reportRepairAttempts` as an integer from 0 through 2, default 1; never retry task work automatically.
proposals.rationale: One repair turn usually corrects omission while guaranteeing termination and avoiding a report-compliance loop.
proposals.title: Default to one automatic report-repair turn
tradeoffs: A zero setting sacrifices structured completion.
A second configurable repair may spend another model turn.
No repair retries the underlying task itself.

proposals.body: Each node follows a fixed state machine: implement using static analysis where available; evaluate with manual or behavioral testing; loop failures back to implementation; codify observed successes and fixed failures as integration or unit tests; verify the accumulated codified suite; perform implementation and architecture review; harden architectural defects; rerun codified tests; then mark the node complete. Node-specific configuration supplies bounded extra prompt context and acceptance evidence, not arbitrary lifecycle steps.
proposals.title: Use one opinionated lifecycle for every DAG node

proposals.body: Declare lavish-axi as an optional compatible dependency and isolate open/poll/end subprocess calls in one adapter. Invoke through Pi's abort-aware execution, parse official AXI/TOON output with an explicit parser dependency, and never call private HTTP endpoints. If absent or incompatible, report a renderer error and preserve the active review. Replace this seam if Lavish later exports a stable JavaScript or JSON API.
proposals.rationale: This uses the supported public interface without requiring a user-global install, npx latest/network behavior, or coupling production code to private server routes.
proposals.title: Use an optional pinned Lavish CLI behind a replaceable protocol adapter

proposals.body: Build the initial plan/show/run vertical slice through ordinary reviewed coding, tests, and Git using a compact implementation checklist. Once it works, use it on remaining release work or the next feature. Do not create transitional bootstrap authority bytes, self-hosting lineage, or require the compiler to authorize its own origin. Dogfood realistic resume, duplicate invocation, stale baseline, worker failure, plan-affecting pause, and target-drift cases before release.
proposals.title: Implement the first vertical slice normally, then dogfood it

proposals.body: Reserve a leading activity cell before each selected node's stable primary glyph. A fresh exact live-worker observation animates that cell; a stale or non-live observation renders a frozen/static mark or blank according to available width. The accepted `*`, `:`, `!`, and other primary marks never change meaning or phase merely to animate.
proposals.rationale: Process liveness and canonical node state are separate facts and should remain visually separable.
proposals.title: Keep spinner motion orthogonal to the primary state glyph

proposals.body: Workers continue asynchronously while their owning Pi session is alive. On extension reload or `session_shutdown`, stop accepting launches, gracefully abort children, escalate process-group termination after a deadline, persist interrupted terminal state, flush completion receipts, and leave the DAG resumable through explicit retry. Do not introduce a daemon in v1.
proposals.rationale: Pi explicitly requires session-scoped resource cleanup, and a daemon would add IPC, authentication, ownership, versioning, and orphan-recovery complexity before the core conductor is validated.
proposals.title: Scope v1 workers to the owning Pi session
tradeoffs: Workers do not survive Pi exit.
A reload can interrupt useful work.
Users need clear interrupted/retry status.

proposals.body: Keep a compact status-aware ASCII DAG below the editor and update it from conductor transitions. Use `/dag workers`, `/dag inspect <node|worker>`, `/dag tail`, `/dag cancel`, `/dag retry`, and corresponding narrow tools for details/actions. Hide the widget when no run is active and summarize large graphs around running/blocked/frontier nodes.
proposals.rationale: This keeps the always-visible surface legible and works in both TUI and RPC while preserving explicit auditable actions.
proposals.title: Use a passive live DAG widget plus explicit controls
tradeoffs: Navigation and control require commands rather than direct clicking.
Deep inspection takes another action.
Large-graph focus heuristics need tuning.

proposals.body: Write atomically to .ai/brainstorm/render/<brainstorm-id>/<review-id>.html. Re-rendering the same review updates that file for Lavish live reload. dag_brainstorm_review supports presenting/resuming the existing active review after interruption without creating a new packet. Poll runs in the foreground with the Pi abort signal; interruption leaves review/session resumable. Resolution best-effort ends the Lavish session and deletes the artifact; archive removes leftovers. User-ended sessions are not reopened unless explicitly requested.
proposals.rationale: Path-derived identity avoids Lavish metadata in the datastore, supports one live session per review, and prevents stale ended sessions or historical artifacts from becoming another state/history layer.
proposals.title: Use one derived ephemeral artifact per active review

proposals.body: Treat Lavish as an optional runtime capability. Resolve a package-installed `lavish-axi` executable pinned to a tested version, spawn it through the current Node executable, and isolate open/poll/end plus TOON status recognition in one adapter module. If unavailable or incompatible, report a clear chat-fallback result. Do not call private HTTP endpoints or read Lavish state files. Tests use a fake executable and recorded bounded outputs.
proposals.rationale: Lavish currently offers no public JavaScript or JSON API; one subprocess seam minimizes coupling and prevents ambient `npx` network/version drift.
proposals.title: Use a pinned optional Lavish CLI dependency behind one adapter
tradeoffs: Pinning requires deliberate upgrades when Lavish evolves.
An optional dependency increases install size when present.
Minimal TOON recognition is still a protocol dependency until an upstream machine API exists.

proposals.body: Bind `schedulerPolicyVersion` and canonical policy hash through the lifecycle/projection catalog and every reservation/intent. The atomic run snapshot stores exact decision sequence, reservations, leases, priority inputs needed for current guards, and launch/effect intents. Pure projections explain ready/admitted/rejected reasons. Do not create an immutable artifact for every ordinary batch; promote only human/authority overrides, policy/capacity changes that cross sessions, deadlock/starvation/replan attention, or evidence used by another boundary. Existing attempt/launch facts remain durable enough for recovery.
proposals.title: Bind one scheduler policy hash but keep routine batch explanations disposable

proposals.body: Permit multi-repository execution only when every repository proposal and exact cross-repository tuple profile is green before the first target moves, the plan declares landing order and compatibility of every partial prefix, and authorization acknowledges non-atomic effects plus forward completion/compensation. Persist per-repository intents/receipts and a coordinator projection. On later drift/failure, keep prior repositories landed, stop, and require forward completion or separately authorized compensation; never claim atomicity or auto-rollback.
proposals.title: Preverify all repositories before visible non-atomic landing

proposals.body: Start/locate the server and use its internal sessions, poll, reply, and end endpoints from the extension.
proposals.rationale: This avoids parsing CLI output but couples production behavior to undocumented routes and server-state details.
proposals.title: Call Lavish server HTTP routes directly

proposals.body: Use immutable expected-absent refs for baselines, candidates, prefixes, composed commits, proposals, and quarantined attempts. Retain baseline/candidate/accepted/proposal anchors through project retention or explicit archival; temporary attempt refs expire only after durable receipts and no active remediation/audit dependency. Cleanup persists intent, deletes refs by expected OID, normally removes only exact clean dead-owned disposable worktrees, never prunes globally, and quarantines dirty/conflicted/live/ambiguous identities. Cleanup failure never changes integration truth.
proposals.title: Protect durable Git objects with private refs and exact cleanup

proposals.body: Guard every run mutation with a process-shared OS/filesystem exclusive lock plus expected snapshot revision/hash, owner epoch/token, PID/start identity, and immutable ownership receipt. Writes fsync temporary content, atomically rename, and fsync parent directories. Run ownership remains distinct from generic worker delivery ownership. Exact direct Pi forks may transfer automatically only when lineage is proven and the source owner is absent/dead; all other attach/takeover requires proven-dead prior ownership. Live, mismatched, or ambiguous ownership blocks mutation and leaves other sessions read-only.
proposals.title: Fence one durable DAG conductor across processes

proposals.body: Key circuits by exact provider/model/capability/credential/endpoint failure domain. Open immediately on hard auth/capability failure or after two matching transient infrastructure failures; admit no new dispatch while open and exactly one explicit half-open probe; close only on accepted success/health observation. Start implementation ceiling two; halve it on a plan-affecting invalidation cascade, opened circuit, or sustained downstream backlog, at most once per trigger fact; increase by one after four clean accepted current-generation milestones with no circuit, ambiguity, or downstream watermark. Clamp to validated maxima; never use elapsed time or forbidden global budgets.
proposals.title: Use observed provider circuits and conservative hysteretic implementation fanout

proposals.body: Use bounded readiness and operation intervals. Credit an attempt only when it contributes to current accepted evidence/integration lineage or produces a unique actionable finding that receives a current disposition. Report useful average concurrency, useful overlap area, parallel opportunity area, opportunity capture, work efficiency, false-independence incidents/waste, typed queue wait, critical-path efficiency, and per-pair serial/parallel elapsed and active-human deltas. Runs with no eligible pair, serial policy, unsupported clocks, missing coverage, or censored terminal state report not-comparable rather than zero. Sticky lane occupancy and peak workers never count as useful work.
proposals.title: Measure opportunity capture, credited overlap, work efficiency, and false-independence waste

proposals.body: Pass prompts, DOM snapshot, layout data, server guidance, and all metadata directly into the tool result.
proposals.rationale: This preserves all diagnostics but spends context on repeated page structure and operational guidance.
proposals.title: Return complete Lavish poll output

proposals.body: Define a deterministic release-readiness command or script covering focused and end-to-end tests, plan/show/run recovery fixtures, generated-spec drift, package dry run and contents, documentation/version/changelog expectations, and clean Git status. Canonical run completion remains locally landed and verified. Push, tag, and package publication remain explicit ordinary user operations outside V1. Add remote release automation only after a concrete product request or field failure justifies it.
proposals.title: Ship a release-readiness check instead of remote release automation

proposals.body: Pass only brainstorm/review IDs and let renderer code query and select whatever it needs.
proposals.rationale: This centralizes projection logic but couples rendering to the datastore and broadens its authority/data surface.
proposals.title: Let the renderer read complete brainstorm state

proposals.body: Define a renderer-neutral `ModelReviewTurnProjection` containing project/focus identity, model revision/hash, non-authoritative Current understanding, delta/frontier summaries selected for this turn, the exact hash-bound active review points/options/dispositions, and optional agent-authored presentation blocks. The renderer receives this projection from the domain adapter and never reads `project-model/model.json` or full focus state directly.
proposals.rationale: A stable input contract lets chat and Lavish share semantic review content while the renderer owns layout and the domain owns model access.
proposals.title: Render from a narrow versioned turn projection
tradeoffs: The projection becomes a versioned API that requires fixtures.
Agents need an explicit way to attach rich presentation blocks.
Large context blocks require size limits or linked artifacts.

proposals.body: Map selected proposal IDs and comments to decisions inside renderer/adapter code and call resolution automatically.
proposals.rationale: This is efficient for simple choices but cannot safely interpret corrections, contradictions, custom context, mixed comments, or changed rationale.
proposals.title: Translate standard controls directly into semantic state

proposals.body: At wide widths, render all nine F0–F8 segments with passed, current, and pending cells distinguishable without relying only on color. At medium widths, retain a compact nine-cell bar and stage label while truncating titles/dependent labels first. At narrow widths, replace the bar with `Fcurrent passed/9`; at subminimum widths, keep only alias, primary mark, and stage. Regression simply redraws fewer passed cells.
proposals.rationale: This preserves the accepted semantic bar where space permits while never violating topology or exact-width obligations.
proposals.title: Use a segmented stage bar with deterministic compact fallbacks

proposals.body: For a single-channel Lavish authority flow, render exact review choices only through package-owned shell controls and disallow arbitrary agent-authored scripts in the same authority document. Rich scripted context must be linked as a separate artifact that cannot call the review queue. The adapter may then treat standard action prompts from its trusted generated document as review-scoped human interactions.
proposals.rationale: Constraining executable context makes the generated authority surface a trusted code boundary despite Lavish lacking prompt-origin provenance.
proposals.title: Restrict authority review surfaces to package-owned controls
tradeoffs: Reverses the accepted unrestricted-context-in-one-document direction.
Rich context and decision controls become separate browsing surfaces.
Still relies on trusted renderer and Lavish package code.

proposals.body: Do not add production renderer code. Continue using the Lavish skill and bash commands to author ad hoc review artifacts when useful; ordinary `dag_model_review` remains chat-only.
proposals.rationale: Avoids dependency and adapter complexity until more dogfood establishes recurring renderer requirements.
proposals.title: Keep Lavish as an agent skill only
tradeoffs: Repeats shell/CSS/control boilerplate and burns context.
No deterministic focus/review resume behavior.
Authority confirmation remains entirely manual.

proposals.body: Write review documents under .lavish/ and retain them after resolution for later browsing.
proposals.rationale: This aids retrospective browsing but creates a second history surface and conflicts with disposable projections.
proposals.title: Keep one .lavish artifact per review as history

proposals.body: Require every `subagent_report` to include task outcome, summary, changed files, commands/checks with outcomes, findings/evidence, conflicts or decisions needed, artifact paths, and retry recommendation. Use optional task-kind variants for implementation, review, and research while retaining a shared core.
proposals.rationale: Rich typing lets future adapters automate more behavior without parsing report prose.
proposals.title: Require rich typed changes, checks, findings, and retry fields
tradeoffs: Workers must fill irrelevant fields or select variants correctly.
The schema begins encoding workflow semantics before DAG and planning redesign.
Model tool-call errors and report-repair frequency likely increase.
Worker claims can be mistaken for observed facts unless every field preserves provenance.

proposals.body: Canonical immutable authorization sets union multiple valid partial receipts, derive dependency/effect/integration-closed scope within the plan maximum, and bind each attempt/effect to the exact set hash; later receipts do not retroactively authorize old work. Expiry/revocation creates a new set and fences affected work. A successor plan always creates a distinct run and never changes the old run's plan hash. V1 may adopt an exact candidate commit/tree through an equivalence receipt but reruns F0–F8 under the successor plan; direct cross-plan stage-evidence adoption is deferred until dogfood proves rerun cost justifies its risk and complexity.
proposals.title: Compose exact authorization sets and keep v1 successor adoption candidate-only

proposals.body: Store a mutable `DagPlanTransactionV1` snapshot under repository-local ignored planning storage, with owner epoch, revision/snapshot CAS, natural idempotency, and pointers to immutable phase facts. Progress through intake, grounding, architecture-ready, decomposition-ready, validated, review-presented, review-approved, published, and handoff-ready; cancellation and supersession are terminal. Seal one exact canonical candidate before review, publish identical bytes through exact plan-lineage CAS, and build an immutable just-in-time run-start bundle only after explicit authorization and freshness revalidation. Do not start execution automatically after approval.
proposals.title: Use a run-grade resumable planning transaction

proposals.body: Pause stops new stage/integration/effect dispatch but lets current attempts settle; their exact results and evidence may ingest normally while their generation remains current. Cancellation, replan, and successor operations atomically fence the affected generation and invalidate pointers before requesting external cancellation. Post-fence old results are immutable quarantine facts and never advance or release current leases. No automatic late-result adoption is allowed. A result proven immutable before the cancellation CAS may be explicitly adopted only through a hash-bound ordering/equivalence/authority receipt and still requires current conductor-sealed evidence.
proposals.title: Pause dispatch, fence cancellation, and quarantine late results

proposals.body: After process termination or `agent_settled`, write one immutable schema-versioned result containing completion/worker/attempt/config identities; canonical terminal status; report status; optional captured worker report; started/ended timestamps; process exit and signal; Pi/model stop reason; model and usage; bounded fallback final text; diagnostic/artifact references; and result hash. Derive status by precedence: verified cancellation → cancelled; lost/ambiguous process identity → lost or needs_attention; nonzero process exit, RPC/protocol failure, or model error → failed; settled with valid `needs_attention` report → needs_attention; settled with valid `completed` report → succeeded; settled without valid report after repair → needs_attention. A captured success claim is preserved but never overrides observed failure.
proposals.rationale: Two-axis provenance prevents a worker's self-report from rewriting process facts while preserving useful partial work and deterministic completion delivery.
proposals.title: Derive one immutable terminal envelope from report and observed runtime facts
tradeoffs: Canonical status derivation needs exhaustive precedence tests.
Usage and model metadata may be incomplete after abrupt process failure.
A result envelope can be needs-attention even though the Pi process settled normally.

proposals.body: Bind full model hash/revision for audit plus a versioned selector and closure over relevant workstreams, explicit seeds, transitive governing relationships, effective authority states, and object semantic hashes. Also bind generated-spec input/content hashes, immutable repository commit/tree identities, plan schema/canonicalization/profile hashes, and context artifact digests. Freshness classifies exact, revalidated, stale-model, stale-code, stale-schema, integration-drift, or unknown-impact. A global revision change may revalidate only when the closure is mechanically unchanged; unknown impact blocks.
proposals.title: Use selector-closure staleness with typed revalidation

proposals.body: Implement server-side TypeScript template/components for understanding, navigation, frontier, review cards, recommendations, Other/comments, queue/submit state, and turn actions. Generate a portable HTML document with package-owned inline CSS and control JavaScript; freeform context may load its own dependencies. Avoid a browser build step and avoid requiring Tailwind/DaisyUI CDN for the standard shell.
proposals.rationale: Generated boilerplate costs no model tokens, works offline, stays visually consistent, and avoids CDN/runtime failure while keeping final artifacts ordinary editable HTML.
proposals.title: Ship a self-contained package-owned shell

proposals.body: Add an optional `dag_model_present_review` tool outside the six semantic project-model tools. It accepts the active review ID and an action such as present, resume, or end; renders the renderer-neutral review projection; opens or resumes Lavish; waits through poll; marks the exact review presented only when browser feedback proves delivery; and returns bounded feedback for agent interpretation. It never resolves review state or grants authority.
proposals.rationale: This preserves the six-tool authority boundary and lets Markdown and Lavish present the same review packet without making Lavish a datastore concept.
proposals.title: Keep Lavish as a separate presentation adapter tool
tradeoffs: A seventh active tool increases surface area.
The agent performs a second tool call after creating a review.
Presentation and semantic resolution remain mechanically separable.

proposals.body: Produce a coherent implementation plan first, then transform accepted plan structure into executable nodes and dependencies in a distinct chunking phase.
proposals.title: Keep planning and DAG decomposition separate

proposals.body: Add explicit `/dag release <runId>` backed by a crash-safe release-closure store. Start only after exact plan completion and bind plan/run/completion receipt, local commit/tree, required tests/evaluation/package/spec-drift evidence, release authorization, remote/ref, and expected-old/desired-new OIDs. Persist exact push intent before dispatch; reconcile remote observation after success or crash as applied, safe retry, or conflict. Never persist credentials or let `/dag run` push. Consider the focus released only after an immutable release receipt or explicit human local-only closure.
proposals.title: Use an explicit release-closure transaction after plan completion

proposals.body: The immutable plan stores executable F0–F8 work items separately from non-executable architecture, contract, human, environment, external-precondition, and integration gates. It stores one precedence graph only for producer/consumer and feedback causality; separate phase-scoped semantic mutex groups; resource demand classes and semantic safety maxima but not machine capacity or leases; and per-repository integration trains. Gates declare whether satisfaction is immutable plan-bound authority or run-time evidence. Predicted/observed paths stay advisory. Operational overlays may restrict; semantic graph changes require a successor plan.
proposals.title: Separate executable work items, gates, and static constraint intent

proposals.body: In the same atomic `worker-session.json` mutation that ingests a terminal result, enqueue one item keyed by stable completion ID and internally bound to the immutable result hash. Queue states are `pending → delivered → acknowledged`, with needs-attention for poison/conflicting disposition, and at most one in-flight item. When Pi is idle, inject exactly one bounded custom follow-up containing completion identity and result/artifact references. The top-level agent finishes handling it by calling `dag_worker_completion_ack` with completion ID and disposition only; the tool validates the internally bound result. Only a later `agent_settled` after ack clears in-flight and schedules the next item. Settling without ack leaves the item in-flight and surfaces attention.
proposals.rationale: An explicit semantic ack proves the top-level agent dealt with each completion; `agent_settled` alone proves only that a turn ended and may include abort or partial side effects.
proposals.title: Drain one durable completion at a time with explicit agent acknowledgement
tradeoffs: Each completion turn needs one extra tool call.
A noncompliant agent can stall the queue.
The ack schema and system guidance become part of the main-agent contract.

proposals.body: Replace independent interval callbacks with one controller that owns a session generation, at most one status refresh, a dirty/coalesced successor refresh, the last fresh observation time, animation frame, stable-height render state, and idempotent disposal. Stale callbacks check generation before publishing. Semantic refresh runs near the existing one-second cadence; lightweight animation requests renders only while at least one exact live worker remains fresh.
proposals.rationale: This addresses overlapping refreshes, teardown races, false perpetual motion, and stale variable-height rows without coupling terminal behavior into canonical run state.
proposals.title: Wrap the pure renderer in a serialized disposable widget controller

proposals.body: At session start bind the exact CWD common-dir, worktree-admin identity, checked-out direct branch, HEAD/tree/index, and owner epoch. Planning may inspect or edit there, but execution starts only after the user supplies a committed clean baseline. Each node uses its own worktree. During execution the conductor does not create tracked changes in its session worktree. After exact proposal verification, hold the repository/session-worktree lock, require the bound branch and HEAD still equal expected old and the index/worktree are clean, persist landing intent, then run an ordinary worktree-aware fast-forward in the bound CWD. Reconcile exact old/new/third and post-state cleanliness. Dirty state, branch change, another live session, non-fast-forward drift, or worktree identity mismatch blocks without stash/reset/clean/switch. Launching on `main` is allowed because branch choice is explicit user context.
proposals.title: Land through the bound session worktree with ordinary fast-forward Git

proposals.body: When a blocking plan-affecting finding is recorded, atomically set the whole run to `needs_replan` before any new dispatch or integration. Let already-running workers settle and retain their branches/results. Present the finding for agent/user judgment. A confirmed semantic change creates a revised plan and new run; a dismissed or misclassified finding may be downgraded and the run resumed with an ordinary disposition note. Defer closure-wide cancellation, mandatory successor on dismissal, adoption receipts, and cross-plan evidence transfer. Prior output may be bounded seed context and is revalidated according to actual changed scope.
proposals.title: Pause the run simply when a blocking finding requires replanning

proposals.body: Persist the attached conductor's random epoch, Pi session ID, PID plus process-start identity, attach timestamp, and low-frequency heartbeat in the canonical run snapshot. A replacement Pi process may take ownership only when the prior conductor is proven dead; if it is live, identity cannot be verified, or concurrent mutation is detected, deny mutation and surface needs-decision. Detached workers and results route by repository/run/attempt identity rather than the original Pi session, so a replacement top-level session can resume delivery.
proposals.rationale: The project does not support concurrent conductors, but top-level restart must work. An explicit lease prevents two Pi sessions from advancing one DAG while avoiding pi-subagents' original-session-only result routing.
proposals.title: Allow one attached conductor per run with fail-closed takeover
tradeoffs: A stale but unverifiable conductor blocks automatic takeover.
Network filesystems and containers can weaken host process identity.
Read-only inspection may remain available while mutation is denied.

proposals.body: Replace separate user-facing plan and chunk artifacts with one versioned model-bound planning transaction and one canonical artifact. Phase A establishes outcomes, architecture decisions/gates, acceptance oracles, semantic effects, risk, and integration strategy. Phase B decomposes that same structure into nodes, fixed lifecycle applicability, typed precedence/gate/resource/integration constraints, expected evidence, and the live projection. Review both views together before execution. `/dag plan` owns the workflow; decomposition is an internal phase and deterministic projection rather than a second prose-authority handoff. A read-only decomposition/diagram command may remain for inspection.
proposals.rationale: Historical sessions show plan and chunk were usually paired in one conductor session and their separate prose/JSON outputs helped reviewability but caused translation, hydration, root-DAG drift, and authority gaps. Two cognitive phases preserve architectural coherence without maintaining two independently stale artifacts.
proposals.title: Use one canonical planning artifact with two internal phases
tradeoffs: The combined transaction is larger and needs structured intermediate validation.
Review must still expose architecture before node detail to avoid graph-first thinking.
A dedicated re-decompose operation is needed when only graph constraints change.
Historical evidence has no controlled unified-vs-separate comparison.

proposals.body: Every review rewrites one stable file and continues or reopens the same Lavish session.
proposals.rationale: This minimizes files and supports continuous reload, but ended-session state and old annotations can leak across semantically distinct reviews.
proposals.title: Use one current.html for the whole brainstorm

proposals.body: Make `/dag show` the single canonical read-only inspection namespace. It resolves only an exact session-bound run, exact active planning transaction, a sole non-superseded plan with an explicit selection label, or a user-supplied full selector; ambiguity produces a bounded choice list rather than choosing latest. Support plan architecture/decomposition/graph/all views, exact node detail, and session-bound run overlays. Automatically show architecture plus static graph after each valid `/dag plan` revision. Keep optional Lavish and exported Markdown/graph as hash-labeled non-authoritative presentations of the same pure projection. Do not repurpose legacy `dag_diagram`.
proposals.title: Use `/dag show` for static plans and exact live overlays
