proposals.body: Make the attached top-level worker manager the only process allowed to mutate one atomic versioned `worker-session.json` containing top-level session identity, owner process epoch, workers, attempts, ingested result hashes, and the serial completion queue. Detached supervisors never edit it. Each supervisor atomically replaces only its own small mailbox heartbeat/status snapshot and creates one immutable terminal result envelope. Startup and filesystem notifications feed these mailboxes into one serialized worker-session mutation queue.
proposals.rationale: Single-writer state avoids cross-process locks and lost updates while allowing detached workers to survive. Atomic mailbox files make disk growth proportional to attempts rather than streaming events.
proposals.title: Use a single-writer worker-session snapshot with per-attempt mailboxes
tradeoffs: The top-level conductor must reconstruct progress from mailboxes after absence.
A terminal result cannot advance the DAG until a top-level process reconnects.
Atomic file replacement and schema migration need disciplined implementation.

proposals.body: Order queue items by terminal result timestamp and stable attempt ID as tie-breaker. No priority lane exists in v1. On the same Pi session, reconcile custom message delivery IDs against session entries after crash. If an item was delivered but never acknowledged and the owning top-level session is replaced, redeliver it to the new compatible session with the same completion ID and a new delivery-attempt ID, explicitly marked as unacknowledged retry. Ack and result ingestion remain idempotent by completion ID/result hash.
proposals.rationale: This matches the user's one-by-one queue, preserves deterministic ordering, and avoids silently losing an item when the top-level session disappears.
proposals.title: Use stable FIFO completion order with same-ID redelivery
tradeoffs: Unacknowledged redelivery is at-least-once handling and may repeat partial agent side effects.
Strict FIFO allows a poison item to block later completions until explicitly dispositioned.
Cross-session session-entry reconciliation cannot prove semantic handling without ack.

proposals.body: Every F0–F8 attempt starts from immutable `StageAttemptInputV1` and can advance only through conductor-validated `StageEvidenceV1`; generic worker success is merely a runtime fact. Check disposition is PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED/WAIVED/NOT_APPLICABLE/BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, while stage state is separately pending/active/passed/failed/blocked/budget_exhausted/cancelled/invalidated. WAIVED and NOT_APPLICABLE apply only to catalog checks; every stage still emits evidence. Use eight semantic finding kinds—product defect, test/evidence gap, architecture issue, oracle/contract issue, infrastructure failure, capability absent, external precondition failure, equivalent/nonactionable—with separate severity, local/plan-affecting materiality, domain, fingerprint, and subject fields. Evidence binds exact plan/work-item/oracle/model closure, candidate generation, worker attempt/result, commit/tree, procedure, environment, authorization, findings, side effects, budgets, and bounded artifacts. Corrections, invalidations, finding closure, and adoption are immutable hash-linked records.
proposals.title: Use conductor-sealed stage evidence with small orthogonal enums

proposals.body: When exact evidence discovers a new runtime-narrowing incompatibility between active nodes, preserve the earlier admitted node and generation-fence the later node's conflicting attempt before cancellation. The later work item retains its sticky active-node lane while waiting for conflict release, repair, cancellation, or successor-plan disposition; it is not automatically replaced by an inactive node. Capacity reduction blocks new leases; cancel newest attempts only when continued overlap is explicitly unsafe. Structural deadlock holds only the affected active-node closure. Missing causality or semantic scope requires a successor plan.
proposals.title: Contain conflicts within sticky active-node lanes

proposals.body: Schema v1 has one executable `change` work-item kind; only it runs fixed F0–F8. Architecture declares outcomes, non-goals, components, contracts, risks, and assumptions. Global semantic subjects use typed behavior, invariant, contract, schema, decision, data, generated-source, or external-resource identities. Each work item contains stable ID/content hash, title/objective, one write repository, outcome/non-goal/model/contract/oracle refs, bounded `extraContext` plus content-addressed context refs, typed semantic reads and writes, risk tier/reasons/hardening profiles, required capability refs by phase, fixed-catalog check applicability with reasons, advisory path/symbol impact evidence with basis/confidence, and integration obligations. Read modes are observe/consume/validate; write modes are create/extend/replace/migrate/delete with compatibility compatible/breaking/unknown and mandatory migration-protocol reference for migrate/delete or breaking replace. Each pre-F1 acceptance oracle has accepted/independent source refs and typed assertions containing subject, observation method/procedure ref, expected pass condition, failure signals, tolerance, environment profile, and required evidence class. Every outcome and work item has an oracle; implementation output or a worker completion claim alone is invalid. Paths never grant or deny edits, and work items cannot define phases, flows, worker boundaries, or arbitrary commands outside bound check/procedure catalogs.
proposals.title: Use one structured change-work-item, oracle, and effect contract

proposals.body: Use a bounded structured terminal result boundary so the top-level agent never needs a duplicated transcript. Earlier proposed required fields such as changed files, checks, affected model/spec IDs, validator verdict, and retryability are now candidates rather than universal requirements because the generic runtime is DAG-agnostic. Runtime identity, termination, usage, report provenance, and result hashing belong to a supervisor-derived envelope; worker-authored fields require separate review.
proposals.rationale: A stable result boundary supports DAG automation, model reconciliation, compact context, and reliable retries.
proposals.title: Require a bounded structured terminal result envelope
tradeoffs: Workers need a finalization tool or strict output contract.
Malformed or missing envelopes require a fallback classifier.
Not every research result maps cleanly to changed files/tests.

proposals.body: Launch each DAG worker through the exact installed Pi CLI in RPC mode with an ephemeral session by default. Parse strict LF-framed protocol incrementally, retain only normalized bounded progress/result state, and never persist raw message-update streams. Use `agent_settled` as terminal completion, RPC abort for graceful cancellation followed by process-group termination, and explicit worker profiles for model, thinking, built-in tools, trusted project context, and optional extensions.
proposals.rationale: Process isolation contains worker crashes and memory leaks and reuses the exact installed Pi distribution and authentication path. RPC provides stable public lifecycle control without importing another extension's private source modules. It costs more startup/transport overhead than SDK sessions but better matches durable async worker supervision.
proposals.title: Use a minimal process-isolated Pi RPC worker kernel
tradeoffs: Cold-start and process overhead per worker.
The runtime must implement a strict bounded RPC client and child-process cleanup.
Extension/tool inheritance must be explicit to avoid recursion and compatibility surprises.

proposals.body: Make the first runtime require atomic conductor transitions, explicit worker ownership/profile/context, structured terminal results, idempotent recovery and completion receipts, and compact snapshots. Never persist `message_update`, cumulative `partial`/`message`, reasoning deltas, or raw RPC streams. Optional diagnostics may retain normalized final `message_end`, tool, lifecycle, and control records behind asynchronous bounded writing and a configurable per-run cap defaulting to 50 MiB. Treat token, cost, turn, and aggressive timeout budgets as configurable policy rather than mandatory finite v1 constraints.
proposals.rationale: This directly prevents the measured 486× quadratic amplification and multi-gigabyte failed-run logs without over-optimizing ordinary resource use or weakening conductor correctness.
proposals.title: Target write amplification and durable correctness without broad mandatory budgets
tradeoffs: A generous diagnostic cap still permits moderate disk use.
Optional budgets may allow expensive but legitimate workers unless configured.
Normalized diagnostic schemas require deliberate selection and redaction.

proposals.body: Implement one revisioned inspectable plan record with outcomes, non-goals, architecture notes, repository baseline, concise project-model/spec references, work items, checks, dependencies, optional concurrency constraints, and integration profile. `/dag plan` performs architecture then decomposition internally, validates and saves the record, derives readable Markdown and graph, and asks only about unresolved meaning. `/dag show` renders exact candidate/published plan, node, and live-run views without mtime selection. `/dag run` resolves the plan, checks whole-plan identity and baseline, derives existing runtime genesis/context internally, atomically creates or resumes one run, and hides low-level receipt/genesis vocabulary. Keep the shipped runtime as substrate; do not rewrite it before the user-facing vertical slice proves value.
proposals.title: Ship a thin plan/show/run vertical slice over the existing runtime

proposals.body: Evaluate in three strata: uncompensated conformance/safety invariants; quality-conditioned run outcomes; explanatory diagnostics. Run deterministic property/failpoint/real-Git matrices and a scripted failure scenario suite. For comparative direction, execute six valid fresh pairs (12 executions) from identical immutable baselines with fixed plan/oracle/model/profile/environment and counterbalanced serial `maxActiveNodes=1` versus selected parallel settings: two independent fan-out/fan-in, two hidden-constraint/architecture-pressure, one integration-train, and one recovery-sensitive case. Run provider/worker loss, conductor crash/resume, and target-drift/conflict drills separately from speed comparison. Publish every pair, no significance claim. Stop immediately on integrity/duplicate/stale/effect/architecture escape; otherwise review after six valid pairs and continue until blocking fixes are re-exercised and the last three valid pairs add no new blocking failure class, with a mandatory review by four weeks or twelve pairs.
proposals.title: Use uncompensated invariants, a quality scorecard, six paired runs, and separate recovery drills

proposals.body: Give each supervisor a bounded atomic control mailbox keyed by attempt identity and ownership token. A conductor writes monotonic commands such as cancel with command ID and reason; the supervisor acknowledges the command in its worker mailbox, sends RPC abort, waits a grace period, closes stdin, then terminates the child process or verified process group if needed. Repeated commands are idempotent. Steering and arbitrary follow-ups remain out of v1 unless separately reviewed.
proposals.rationale: After top-level reload there is no live child-process handle or stdin. A durable command inbox preserves cancellation without trusting PID-only signals.
proposals.title: Control detached RPC workers through a token-bound command inbox
tradeoffs: File polling adds small cancellation latency.
Supervisor failure may still require conductor-side verified process-group escalation.
The protocol needs command retention and acknowledgement cleanup.

proposals.body: The domain supplies one TurnProjection containing brainstorm/revision identity, Initial/Current understanding, active review points and stored options, selected frontier summaries, and explicitly relevant settled context. Each point chooses context kind: Markdown, semantic helper blocks, trusted raw HTML/CSS/scripts, or linked/embedded artifact. The renderer never reads full brainstorm state and the agent never authors the standard document shell.
proposals.rationale: A narrow projection preserves datastore/renderer separation and sensible context use, while explicit context kind lets the engine insert unrestricted material correctly without forcing cross-renderer compatibility.
proposals.title: Render a narrow turn projection with explicit flexible context descriptors

proposals.body: Represent producer/consumer and feedback dependencies as directed precedence; unresolved architecture and contract choices as prerequisite gate nodes; non-directional semantic write conflicts and singleton resources as mutex/capacity constraints; and merge/deployment order as a separate integration train. Launch otherwise-ready work in isolated worktrees with namespaced runtime resources. Classify speculative work as green, amber, or red based on reversibility and evidence; continuously simulate merges and run combined checks; dynamically add discovered constraints; and adapt fanout to invalidation and review capacity.
proposals.rationale: This preserves parallel implementation where integration must be ordered, avoids pretending every exclusion is a semantic dependency, and uses evidence/revalidation instead of path locks.
proposals.title: Schedule with typed precedence, gates, conflicts, resources, and integration trains
tradeoffs: Semantic effects are incomplete and require dynamic correction.
Speculative branches consume model, test, and review capacity.
Irreversible external effects still require stricter serialization.
A richer canonical graph and projection schema is required.

proposals.body: Gates are non-executable records with kind model-authority, contract, human-authorization, environment-capability, external-precondition, or integration; subject/authority/evidence refs; `plan_revision` or `run_evidence` release mode; typed predicate; and work-item phase blockers. Semantic/contract resolution requires a successor plan; operational evidence may release inside the run. Precedence contains only producer-consumer or feedback causality with subject, evidence, and release disposition. Semantic mutex groups are unordered, phase-scoped memberships with subject/reason/confidence/evidence. Resource classes declare units/namespacing/safety maxima and work items declare phase-scoped demand; actual capacity and leases remain run state. Per-repository integration trains declare members, partial integration precedence, strategy, prefix/final validation profiles, and never imply authoring precedence. Migration protocols bind subject/from/to, strategy atomic or expand-contract, typed expand/dual-support/backfill/switch/contract stages, compatibility matrix, rollback, node/gate/oracle refs; breaking persisted/external migrate/delete requires expand-contract unless an explicit accepted atomic-risk disposition proves mixed-version safety unnecessary. Every union has a content hash and cannot masquerade as another category.
proposals.title: Use disjoint phase-scoped gate, migration, and constraint unions

proposals.body: Use one model-aware decomposition pass that jointly defines outcomes, acceptance evidence, node boundaries, and dependency constraints rather than translating a prose plan into a second artifact.
proposals.title: Plan directly as an executable DAG

proposals.body: Ask Lavish to expose a machine-readable poll mode and a chrome-owned trusted-action control path that binds a user gesture to opaque action data without making the token callable or forgeable by artifact scripts. If such provenance can be audited, the adapter could create a review-scoped interaction receipt and resolve exact displayed options without a Pi confirmation round trip.
proposals.rationale: This is the only path identified so far to retain unrestricted artifact scripts and make Lavish the sole authority channel mechanically.
proposals.title: Explore an upstream trusted-action protocol for single-channel authority
tradeoffs: Depends on upstream design and release timing.
Browser gesture/provenance security needs careful threat modeling.
Not required for an initial presentation-only adapter.

proposals.body: `modelBinding` records the full project ID/schema/revision/model hash for audit, then a selector version, selected workstream IDs, explicit seed IDs, and deterministic closure. Roots are all effective, receipt-valid, non-superseded accepted intents, concepts, scenarios, decisions, and commitments whose repository scope or workstream scope intersects the selector, plus explicit accepted seeds. Repeatedly include receipt-valid current governing objects connected to the closure by inbound or outbound typed relationships, regardless of workstream, until fixed point. Store sorted entries with collection, ID, effective state, semantic hash, and acceptance content hash; hash the selector and closure independently. Explicit non-governing evidence/question/proposal inputs live in a separate sorted `contextRefs` list and do not make every new research note stale. Bind every generated-spec projection actually consumed by ID, projection contract, model-input hash, and content hash. Revalidation reruns the same selector version; a new accepted in-scope or connected authority changes the closure, while unrelated model metadata or unselected evidence may revalidate.
proposals.title: Define a reproducible governing selector and closure

proposals.body: Keep historical V1 plan, run, worker, Git, and evaluation artifacts readable and immutable. New writers should use versioned simpler schemas: one canonical plan hash plus governing-closure digest and bounded manifest artifact rather than blanket entity/schema hashes; UUID/revision authorization and review records; globally unique run/attempt/effect IDs plus generation where stale output matters; revision-CAS snapshots with optional external checksums rather than semantic hash chains; one content-address key per immutable fact/artifact without embedded self-hash duplication; direct structured repository/worktree identity plus native Git OIDs; and accumulator/index revisions rather than hash CAS. Do not automatically convert active V1 runs or reinterpret old hashes with new semantics.
proposals.title: Simplify new schema versions without rewriting historical artifacts

proposals.body: Make the compiler the only producer of executable plans. Introduce a new immutable canonical plan schema version rather than silently changing persisted V1: embed stable source/receipt bindings and entity traceability needed for execution packet closure, while placing bulky deterministic trace tables, diagnostics, packet manifests, and projection hashes in a strict content-addressed compilation manifest referenced by the plan. Compile from immutable phase facts, recompute governing closure and freshness at every authority boundary, derive constraints from an explicit semantic access matrix, generate complete node packets and deterministic projections, and permit conductor start only from a published fresh start bundle. Preserve V1 parsing for historical runs but do not allow caller-authored V1 plans through the new authoritative planning path.
proposals.title: Introduce a source-joined compiler with a trace-complete canonical plan version

proposals.body: Define global and per-run concurrency; optional provider/model lanes; FIFO fairness; idle and hard timeouts; turn/token/cost/output limits; process stdout/stderr memory caps; retry classification with bounded exponential backoff; maximum attempts; fail-fast versus continue policy; and circuit breaking after repeated provider/runtime failures. No numeric limit defaults to unlimited in production.
proposals.rationale: An owned runtime must prevent both disk amplification and uncontrolled process/provider/resource fan-out.
proposals.title: Enforce run and worker resource, timeout, and retry policy
tradeoffs: Conservative defaults may reduce throughput.
Provider-specific failures need normalization.
Budget enforcement may yield useful partial work that requires explicit status.

proposals.body: Launch each child with explicit worker-role metadata. The extension's ordinary parent entrypoint returns before attaching worker-session writer, result watcher, completion dispatcher, management UI, or parent commands. A child-specific registration exposes only the structured report surface from this extension. Normal unrelated Pi tools/extensions remain inherited according to the separate child tool policy. Nested delegation is out of v1.
proposals.rationale: Ambient extension inheritance otherwise makes the child indistinguishable from a completion-receiving top-level session and can create duplicate UI/dispatch ownership.
proposals.title: Keep top-level services inert inside RPC worker processes
tradeoffs: The subagent launch tool is visible but operationally unavailable in workers.
Explicit nested delegation would require a separately designed parent-routing contract.
Environment metadata must be validated with the RPC launch configuration.

proposals.body: Use a mandatory context core plus adaptively selected supporting sections. Every decision brief establishes the decision, why it matters, the recommendation, and the exact question. Prompts encourage relevant current behavior, change context, constraints, consequences, and model evidence whenever they help explain why the decision exists. The goal is not to render every possible section every time, but to prevent briefs from collapsing into only a description of the recommended option.
proposals.title: Use layered question briefs with decision context before recommendation

proposals.body: After resolution, report the selected option, changed object IDs, generated paths, and unresolved review points, followed by the next action. This is highly auditable but requires the user to interpret model internals.
proposals.title: Expose a concise model transaction receipt

proposals.body: Describe the desired presentation in guidance but add no deterministic checks for prompt delivery or Markdown rendering beyond existing generic behavior.
proposals.title: Rely entirely on agent formatting judgment

proposals.body: Always render Goal, Current behavior, Accepted direction, Open questions, and Boundaries in a stable order, allowing explicit none entries when a category is empty.
proposals.title: Use a fixed snapshot template for every Current understanding

proposals.body: After resolving user input, produce a short structured Markdown acknowledgement that states what was understood, what materially changed in the model or governing behavior, what remains unresolved, and what happens next. Omit sections that add no information and avoid restating the full Current understanding.
proposals.title: Acknowledge the accepted direction, semantic effect, and next frontier

proposals.body: Use Markdown and semantic coverage as scaffolding, but evaluate whether the agent selected, connected, and explained the facts that matter. Avoid fixed documentation-like forms whose completeness can mask shallow retrieval or copied model prose.
proposals.title: Prompt for contextual synthesis rather than template completeness

proposals.body: Require the synthesis to make the goal, relevant current mechanism or state, and governing accepted direction easy to find. Add open frontier, constraints, boundaries, evidence, or risks when they materially affect alignment. Let headings adapt to the subject, and leave turn-by-turn changes to the separate delta and acknowledgement surfaces.
proposals.title: Use a mandatory semantic core with adaptive Markdown headings for Current understanding

proposals.body: Lead with a compact alignment summary, then expand current behavior, governing direction, frontier, and evidence in adaptive sections. This optimizes scanning but intentionally repeats some facts at two levels.
proposals.title: Use an at-a-glance summary followed by adaptive supporting detail

proposals.body: Require a minimum Markdown shape such as headings plus multiple blocks for question context and Current understanding, rejecting writes or reviews that do not satisfy it.
proposals.title: Mechanically reject unstructured brainstorm prose

proposals.body: Current understanding should act as an agent-authored synthesis of goals, relevant current behavior, governing direction, open questions, and boundaries. It should reveal what the agent judges relevant rather than reproduce project documentation. Do not force a separate acknowledgement surface; ordinary acknowledgements may remain conversational.
proposals.title: Make Current understanding an evidence-bearing synthesis

proposals.body: Do not add a dedicated post-resolution acknowledgement. Let the next formal review's Current understanding and model delta demonstrate the result.
proposals.title: Rely on updated Current understanding and the next review

proposals.body: Strengthen mode guidance to require scannable Markdown and contextual synthesis. Deterministic tests verify that the guidance is injected, Markdown headings/lists render safely, and required source references remain fresh. Runtime tools do not reject prose based on heading counts or claim to validate comprehension.
proposals.title: Require structured synthesis in guidance and test delivery, not prose quality

proposals.body: Revise the active-focus mode guidance to cover contextual question briefs, adaptive Markdown Current understanding, selective synthesis rather than model reproduction, no mandatory acknowledgement surface, and automatic next-frontier continuation. Add deterministic tests for guidance injection and structured Markdown rendering without adding a runtime prose-shape validator or semantic quality gate.
proposals.title: Update mode guidance and targeted structural regressions

proposals.body: Superseded as a rigid cross-surface contract. Question briefs and Current understanding still require scannable Markdown and semantic coverage through agent guidance, but no fixed acknowledgement surface or runtime heading-count validator is required.
proposals.title: Define a structured Markdown contract for brainstorm surfaces

questions.body: The requirement to survive Pi reload and exit is accepted. Choose the durability mechanism between detached per-run supervisors with bounded durable reconciliation and a centralized daemon with durable scheduling/multi-session coordination.
questions.title: Must asynchronous workers survive Pi exit or extension reload?

questions.body: Codify that default plan authorization covers all reversible local implementation/evaluation work and unrestricted architecture-preserving edits inside declared repositories, with no path/symbol boundaries. Define mechanical dependency closure, when separate authorization is required for undeclared repositories, external/live effects, irreversible operations, integration/landing, deployment, credentials, and budget escalation, and how partial authorization remains visible without becoming a confused deputy.
questions.title: What exact broad coordination authorization defaults should the plan use?

questions.body: Define one atomic versioned conductor snapshot, ownership/recovery, node/stage attempt identity, immutable completion/result references, idempotent launch/ingest transitions, graph/model staleness, cancellation/lost handling, queue reconstruction, and direct-session transfer without making generic worker state the DAG authority.
questions.title: How should canonical DAG run state bind owned-worker attempts?

questions.body: Define versioned planning input, architecture/outcome view, node contracts, acceptance oracles, typed precedence/gates/resources/integration constraints, model object hashes, graph hash, staleness, review state, and execution authorization in the one-artifact/two-phase workflow.
questions.title: What exact canonical schema binds model-aware planning to execution?

questions.body: Specify closed fields, canonicalization, plan hash versus transport/provenance metadata, stable plan ID/revision, supersedes hash, per-entity hashes, set ordering, unknown-field behavior, schema migration, and the evidence-adoption rule for equivalent nodes after re-decomposition.
questions.title: What exact top-level plan, hash, and lineage envelope should schema v1 use?

questions.body: The current closed V1 bytes cannot represent exact acceptance-receipt identity, entity-level source/artifact traceability, semantic-read provenance, complete work-item architecture relevance, or a mandatory compilation manifest. Choose whether to evolve the immutable canonical schema to V2 with traceability embedded, or keep execution topology compact while requiring every published plan to bind a strict compilation manifest that supplies the missing trace closure. Persisted V1 runs must remain readable and immutable either way.
questions.title: Should compiler traceability be embedded in CanonicalDagPlanV2 or a mandatory bound manifest?

questions.body: Worktrees and recoverable integration need immutable commits, while planning often starts with user changes present. Decide whether run authorization requires a clean commit, supports a conductor-created snapshot commit, or can bind a dirty patch/tree hash without making worktree recovery unsafe.
questions.title: Must execution authorization bind a clean committed Git baseline?

questions.body: No. The trusted agent and ordinary explicit user direction are already inside the workflow trust boundary, so publication and run start do not require a complete cryptographic interaction-receipt stack. The shipped vertical slice instead source-joins concrete authoritative model/spec bytes and clean Git baselines, retains ordinary approval and authorization fields as separate decisions, records one recoverable mutable start intent, and preserves the canonical runtime's internal compatibility facts without presenting them as human-consent proofs. Add more trace detail only if field evidence demonstrates a concrete debugging or interoperability need.
questions.title: Should publication and run start require the complete closed receipt stack?

questions.body: If one top-level Pi session attaches multiple runs, independent per-run queues could trigger competing turns. A session-wide dispatcher can select the earliest pending item across owned runs while leaving each queue durably stored in its run snapshot. If v1 permits only one attached mutable run, this complexity can be deferred.
questions.title: Is one-at-a-time completion delivery scoped per run or per top-level Pi session?

questions.body: The project model is repository-scoped, but historical work sometimes spanned related repositories/worktrees and prior art supports cross-project gates. Decide whether v1 remains one repository with external contract gates, or supports multiple repository bindings and per-repository integration trains from the start.
questions.title: Does schema v1 support multiple repositories?

questions.body: Determine how Pi can show running/queued/completed workers in DAG context, whether a live ASCII diagram should be a widget or custom editor surface, how updates are throttled, and how users inspect, cancel, retry, or navigate nodes without overwhelming the main conversation.
questions.title: What DAG-centered live worker UI belongs in Pi?

questions.body: Define `RunEvaluationEnvelopeV1`, exact source hashes, metric schema/policy version, coverage flags, derivable versus lossy fields, regeneration, run/project retention, cross-run aggregates, clock quality, redaction, multi-repository partial landing, and instrumentation failure behavior without creating an event log or execution authority.
questions.title: What bounded evaluation envelope, retention, and missingness contract should v1 use?

questions.body: Define counts and intervals for human decisions/authorization/replan, autonomous spans, exact model/provider/token/reported-cost coverage, like-for-like comparisons, and the boundary that defers transcript/LLM-judge prompt quality to a later corpus exercise. No metric may become a hidden time/token/cost budget.
questions.title: How should human attention, model usage, cost, and later prompt evaluation be separated?

questions.body: Choose primary release invariants, outcome measures, prospective fixture and substantive-run coverage, comparison strategy, and a stopping/review rule. Historical audits can seed scenarios but not supply trustworthy rates. Avoid a composite score or percentage gate that lets throughput compensate for correctness.
questions.title: Which quality-conditioned outcomes and evidence portfolio should count as successful dogfooding?

questions.body: Define active-lane and operation overlap intervals, quality/integration survival, serial-work proxy, typed wait decomposition, false-independence and missing-causality rates, conflict/invalidation cost, censoring, and runs with no parallel opportunity. Higher concurrency must not become a goal independent of accepted quality.
questions.title: What exact denominators define useful parallelism and lost concurrency benefit?

questions.body: Candidate semantics include current lifecycle stage ordinal F0–F8, passed stages over the current generation, or completed operations in the current attempt. The user accepts non-monotonic movement during iteration, but the denominator and reset behavior still need an explicit product definition.
questions.title: What should the node progress bar measure?

questions.body: Choose bounded telemetry and evaluation criteria for planning rework, usable parallelism, queue/wait time, phase duration, retry/back-edge rates, provider/environment failures, codified regressions, architecture findings, hardening yield, speculative invalidation, merge conflicts, integrated verification, model cost, stale recovery, and human decision latency.
questions.title: How will dogfooding prove the redesigned DAG is better?

questions.body: The exact incident trigger is still unknown, but one concrete corruption mechanism is now identified: integration.ts widens Pi's supplied render width to at least 20 columns, violating the component contract during narrow/resize states. Remaining investigation should determine whether the preserved incident also requires variable widget height, overlapping asynchronous refreshes, teardown/re-registration, or another Pi differential-rendering transition. Reproduction should capture PI_TUI_WRITE_LOG and terminal dimensions/projection revisions.
questions.title: What exact render transition scrambles the DAG widget and editor boundary?

questions.body: An activity spotlight can stay compact and read-only, with exact full-DAG topology and diagnostics available through dag_run_diagram/inspect or a separate command/overlay. Decide whether any keyboard interaction is needed in the persistent surface.
questions.title: Should the persistent widget remain passive while detail moves elsewhere?

questions.body: Define focus anchors, immediate-neighbor closure, omitted-region summaries, stable tie-breaks, horizontal/adjacency fallbacks, label truncation, and maximum row allocation for narrow, normal, and wide terminals. The slice must preserve useful edge direction and never imply that omitted nodes or edges do not exist.
questions.title: How should the widget choose and lay out a bounded topology slice at each terminal size?

questions.body: Define an ASCII-only mandatory glyph set and deterministic precedence when a node is simultaneously active, waiting on a worker, blocked, needs attention, integrating, or has stale/quarantined facts. Color may reinforce but never carry meaning. Phase, worker, retry, finding, and integration annotations remain orthogonal.
questions.title: What exact ASCII glyph and primary-state precedence should represent each DAG node?

questions.body: Define bounded full diagram, run summary, node/phase/attempt inspection, worker tail, wait-for/blocker explanation, pause/resume, cancellation, retry/replacement, reattach, and successor-plan handoff surfaces. Controls must compile to closed reducer commands with exact expected revision/epoch and never mutate through the widget itself.
questions.title: Which exact read and control commands/tools should accompany the passive widget?

questions.body: Specify when the below-editor widget appears/clears, how it subscribes to conductor transitions and recovers after reload/resume, how projection input hashes and stale snapshots appear, how render/watch failures degrade to read-only commands, and how non-TUI modes behave. The widget must never mutate run state or infer DAG facts from generic worker files.
questions.title: What lifecycle, refresh, stale-state, and degradation behavior should the widget use?

questions.body: Answered: live motion occupies a separate activity cell and never replaces the stable primary glyph. The activity cell animates only from a fresh exact joined worker observation and disappears in the subminimum fallback.
questions.title: How should live motion coexist with the accepted primary state glyph?

questions.body: The worker observation source and separate activity cell are accepted, but production still needs numeric timing. The current semantic scan cadence is one second. The choice must balance brief scheduling jitter against stale motion claims and avoid repainting when no exact worker is freshly live.
questions.title: What exact freshness window and animation cadence should govern live motion?

questions.body: A definite contract violation is known and the replacement safety invariants cover the other plausible transition classes, but the exact historical transition has not been captured with PI_TUI_WRITE_LOG. Decide whether implementation is gated on reproduction or whether reproduction remains a nonblocking diagnostic follow-up.
questions.title: Must the historical editor-scrambling incident be reproduced before implementing the replacement?

questions.body: Answered: wide and medium widths use nine ordered F0–F8 cells; narrow width uses current stage plus passed/9; subminimum width retains alias, primary mark, and current stage only.
questions.title: How should nine-stage progress compress across terminal widths?

scenarios.action: Redeliver the same completion ID after restart. The completion instruction requires inspecting current run/repository state, recognizing already-applied actions, and acknowledging without repeating them. Never generate a new completion ID for redelivery.
scenarios.body: The completion-triggered agent turn merges or edits repository state, then Pi exits before `dag_worker_completion_ack` commits.
scenarios.context: The queue item remains delivered and unacknowledged.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Queue state remains safe and the top-level handler can avoid duplicate side effects, while the system explicitly does not claim transactional exactly-once model behavior.
scenarios.title: Top-level actions commit before the completion acknowledgement

scenarios.action: Write one token-bound cancel command, observe supervisor acknowledgement, let the supervisor send RPC abort and escalate its child locally, then ingest one cancelled terminal result. Only if the supervisor fails and its process identity still matches may the conductor signal the supervisor/process group directly.
scenarios.body: A replacement conductor attaches to a run and the user cancels a matching live detached worker.
scenarios.context: The supervisor identity is verified but the new conductor has no inherited child stdin handle.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Cancellation remains available after reload without PID-only signaling or duplicate terminal transitions.
scenarios.title: Cancel a live worker after the top-level agent reloads

scenarios.action: Queue all four, deliver only the first when idle, wait for its explicit ack and subsequent settle, then deliver the second; repeat until empty. Already-running workers continue, while newly unlocked dependent launches wait for their originating completion's disposition.
scenarios.body: Four workers finish while the top-level agent is busy or closed.
scenarios.context: All four results are atomically ingested and ordered by terminal timestamp plus attempt ID.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Every completion is handled in deterministic order with at most one completion turn in flight and no coalescing.
scenarios.title: A completion burst drains one item per settled acknowledged turn

scenarios.action: On same-session restart, scan session entries, reconcile D into the run snapshot as delivered/in-flight, and do not append another message. If durable visibility cannot be proven, retain the item as unacknowledged and require same-ID redelivery/ack rather than treating it handled.
scenarios.body: A custom follow-up containing delivery attempt D is persisted in the Pi session, then the top-level process exits before marking the queue item delivered.
scenarios.context: The queue item and custom message both carry the same completion ID, result hash, and delivery-attempt ID.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: The completion is not silently lost; duplicate semantic acknowledgement remains impossible, and duplicate presentation is bounded by stable IDs.
scenarios.title: Conductor crashes after completion message append but before run snapshot update

scenarios.action: On reconnect, wait a bounded bootstrap grace and inspect the token-scoped mailbox and process identity. If a matching worker appears, attach it. If absence cannot be proven or state conflicts, mark the attempt launch-ambiguous and the node needs-decision; do not auto-relaunch in the same worktree.
scenarios.body: The OS creates a supervisor process, but the top-level conductor exits before its returned PID is committed to the run snapshot.
scenarios.context: The attempt claim and ownership token were persisted before spawn; the supervisor may or may not have written its first mailbox.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: At most one worker edits the worktree, and uncertainty is explicit rather than converted into duplicate execution.
scenarios.title: Conductor crashes between detached spawn and persisted PID

scenarios.action: Do not infer completion from freeform files, do not advance the DAG, and do not enqueue a normal success/failure completion. Quarantine the artifact reference, mark the attempt corrupt-artifact/needs-decision in the canonical snapshot, and enqueue at most one bounded attention completion if its identity can be trusted.
scenarios.body: A detached supervisor disappears and its result file is malformed, hash-mismatched, or bound to a different ownership token.
scenarios.context: The mailbox may be stale or terminal.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Corruption is visible and cannot become an authoritative DAG transition or repeated delivery storm.
scenarios.title: A terminal result is truncated or fails identity validation

scenarios.action: Fail launch validation before claiming/spawning when possible; otherwise classify the prompt/model-selection response as launch failure. Never silently load all extensions or substitute a model unless the profile explicitly defines fallback.
scenarios.body: The parent model comes from an extension-registered provider, but its worker profile does not name the provider extension.
scenarios.context: The child launches with `--no-extensions` and explicit approved resources.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Provider compatibility failures are clear, bounded, and do not expand child authority.
scenarios.title: Selected custom provider is unavailable in the isolated child

scenarios.action: Fence every publish and render request by controller generation, coalesce successor work only within the live generation, and dispose timers/TUI references idempotently.
scenarios.body: A status refresh begins, then the session reloads, switches, or shuts down before the refresh completes.
scenarios.context: The old controller still has an in-flight promise while a new session generation owns or has cleared the widget.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: The old result cannot publish into the new widget, request through stale TUI state, restore a cleared widget, or overwrite current diagnostics.
scenarios.title: A slow widget refresh completes after reload or session replacement

scenarios.action: Render each frame from the exact supplied width, switch to a minimal fallback below the rich-layout minimum, and recompute bounded height deterministically.
scenarios.body: A DAG widget is visible while the terminal rapidly crosses wide, normal, narrow, and sub-20-column breakpoints.
scenarios.context: The editor contains text and the widget's selected activity neighborhood would normally require multiple rows.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: No line exceeds the supplied width, the editor/footer boundary remains intact, and stale rows disappear when breakpoint changes reduce widget height.
scenarios.title: Terminal resizes through a width below the widget's rich-layout minimum

scenarios.action: Freeze the spinner while preserving canonical node/lane state, stale-read-only diagnostics, progress, and the last-good topology.
scenarios.body: The widget receives an exact live-worker observation and then subsequent semantic refreshes fail or stop while the last-good projection remains visible.
scenarios.context: No new terminal worker fact or canonical DAG revision has arrived, and the controller freshness window expires.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: The UI no longer claims current motion, but it also does not invent worker death, node failure, or lost progress.
scenarios.title: A previously live worker observation becomes stale before terminal reconciliation

scenarios.action: Result ingestion is idempotent, DAG advancement is not repeated, and completion delivery checks the persisted receipt before queuing a follow-up.
scenarios.body: A worker result file is persisted, then the extension reloads before its completion notification receipt is flushed; recovery sees the same terminal result again.
scenarios.context: The worker attempt has a stable completion ID.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Exactly one semantic DAG transition and at most one main-agent completion report occur.
scenarios.title: A terminal result is observed twice around reload

scenarios.action: The worker either jams unrelated behavior into allowed files or violates its assignment to preserve architecture.
scenarios.body: A node is allowed to edit only a narrow file set even though a clean implementation requires moving or introducing responsibilities elsewhere.
scenarios.context: The scheduler treats path ownership as the primary conflict-avoidance mechanism.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: The redesigned planner treats path overlap as a warning signal, not a hard architecture boundary, and escalates shared design ownership or integration needs explicitly.
scenarios.title: A file allowlist forces implementation into the wrong architecture

scenarios.body: When the user forks or clones a Pi conversation to edit an earlier response, the exact linked focus session is validated and remains active without requiring `/dag brainstorm` reentry.
scenarios.title: Forking to correct an earlier response preserves focus

scenarios.action: The replacement proves the old conductor dead, takes a new epoch, scans results before mailboxes, ingests each exactly once, advances DAG projections, and enqueues stable FIFO completions. It injects only the first custom follow-up. The top-level agent inspects current state, handles it, calls exact ack with disposition, settles, and then receives the second. Newly unlocked dependent work launches only after its originating completion receives continue disposition.
scenarios.body: A conductor claims and launches one RPC worker, then top-level Pi closes. The detached supervisor finishes, writes a structured result, and exits. A replacement Pi session attaches while two other results are also pending.
scenarios.context: The run snapshot, token-bound mailbox/result files, and completion IDs are valid.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Worker work survives; no raw stream is persisted; no result or queue item duplicates; one completion turn is in flight; and restored DAG state matches disk/process reality.
scenarios.title: Worker completes across top-level restart and drains through acknowledgement

scenarios.action: Ground the request, develop architecture and acceptance criteria, decompose that same plan into a canonical executable graph, and present the human-readable plan with the static DAG before execution authorization.
scenarios.body: A user invokes `/dag plan` with a desired outcome and expects one coherent planning experience rather than separate planning and chunking commands.
scenarios.context: The workflow has access to current project-model authority, generated specs, repository baseline evidence, and the canonical plan schema.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: The user can review and revise both views without managing a separate chunking artifact; only one exact approved canonical plan can hand off to execution.
scenarios.title: Plan once and review prose with the executable DAG

scenarios.action: Workers independently choose incompatible designs and only discover the conflict during integration.
scenarios.body: Two nodes appear file-disjoint but both depend on the same new abstraction, interface boundary, schema, or migration ordering decision.
scenarios.context: The graph contains no explicit dependency because anticipated file edits do not overlap.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: The planner extracts the shared decision into a prerequisite node or shared accepted contract and serializes dependents only until that uncertainty is resolved.
scenarios.title: Parallel nodes unknowingly share an unresolved architecture decision

scenarios.action: Apply an explicit session-lineage ownership rule while supervisors continue writing only A-correlated mailboxes and results.
scenarios.body: Session A launches workers, then the user forks or starts session B before they finish. Pi tears down A's extension runtime and initializes B with a distinct session UUID. Detached workers continue.
scenarios.context: Session A owns live worker attempts and a durable completion queue; session B is now attached in the TUI.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Results are not delivered twice or silently attached to B; reopening or explicitly adopting A recovers its queue deterministically.
scenarios.title: A top-level Pi session forks while workers are still running

scenarios.action: Compare PID, OS start identity, token-bound config/mailbox hash, and expected executable. Treat mismatch as identity-mismatch, never signal the process, keep the worktree quarantined, and require a decision before retry.
scenarios.body: After a worker exits without a final result, the OS reuses its PID before the top-level conductor reconnects.
scenarios.context: The mailbox contains the old PID and process-start identity.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: The runtime never kills or attaches to an unrelated process and never starts a competing worker in the same worktree automatically.
scenarios.title: A persisted PID now belongs to an unrelated process

scenarios.action: Treat the valid terminal result as stronger evidence than the stale running mailbox, ingest it once, enqueue completion once, and mark the attempt terminal in `run.json`; preserve the stale mailbox for diagnostics until run cleanup.
scenarios.body: The supervisor atomically writes its terminal result and the machine or process stops before replacing its mailbox with terminal state.
scenarios.context: The immutable result validates against the attempt identity and ownership token.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Completion is not lost or delayed by write ordering, and repeated scans are harmless.
scenarios.title: Terminal result exists while worker mailbox still says running

scenarios.body: When the user answers only part of a review and unrelated model content changed, each fresh hash-matching point resolves independently while omitted, ambiguous, contradictory, or stale points remain unresolved.
scenarios.title: Sparse review resolution preserves stale and omitted points

scenarios.action: Do not send the next completion and do not launch work gated by this result. Show needs-attention status and allow the next compatible top-level turn to inspect and acknowledge or explicitly disposition the same item.
scenarios.body: The completion-triggered turn ends, but no matching acknowledgement tool call was committed.
scenarios.context: The item remains delivered and in-flight in the canonical worker-session snapshot.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: The queue never mistakes turn completion for semantic handling and never drains past an unresolved completion.
scenarios.title: Top-level agent settles without acknowledging the in-flight completion

scenarios.action: Only the matching live conductor may mutate. The second session remains read-only or receives a conflict; it cannot claim work, ingest results, deliver completions, cancel workers, or take over unless the prior process is proven dead or the user explicitly resolves the conflict.
scenarios.body: A resumed session and an older still-live Pi process both load the same repository run.
scenarios.context: The run snapshot carries a conductor epoch and process identity.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: One serialized state machine advances the DAG; no split-brain completion or worker launch occurs.
scenarios.title: Two top-level Pi sessions attempt to attach the same run

scenarios.action: The conductor persists and deduplicates each terminal result, advances all affected DAG nodes, schedules newly ready work within capacity, rerenders once, and sends one bounded follow-up completion summary after the main agent settles.
scenarios.body: Four ready DAG nodes run concurrently and finish within 200 ms of each other.
scenarios.context: The main agent is still executing an unrelated tool call.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: No result is lost or delivered twice, and the main agent receives one turn rather than four competing turns.
scenarios.title: Several independent workers finish in one burst

scenarios.action: Write the immutable structured result atomically, then mark the worker mailbox terminal. On reconnect, the conductor scans results, validates identity/schema/hash, applies the DAG transition and enqueues one completion in the same run-snapshot mutation, and deduplicates future scans by result hash.
scenarios.body: A matching detached supervisor reaches `agent_settled` and exits while no top-level Pi process is attached.
scenarios.context: The supervisor owns only its mailbox and result path.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: The work survives absence, advances once after reconnect, and produces exactly one queued completion without a raw event log.
scenarios.title: Detached worker finishes while top-level Pi is closed

scenarios.action: The conductor classifies the failure, retries or falls back within budget without cancelling unrelated siblings unless fail-fast policy says so, records all attempted models/usage, and exposes partial run status.
scenarios.body: One worker receives a retryable provider error while sibling workers continue successfully.
scenarios.context: The worker profile has bounded model fallback/retry policy and the DAG may allow independent progress.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Healthy work is preserved; failed work is explicit and reproducible; budgets and concurrency remain enforced.
scenarios.title: A worker provider fails during a parallel run

scenarios.action: Preserve the report in the immutable result, derive canonical status `failed`, and deliver a failure completion that notes a captured completed claim is available for inspection.
scenarios.body: The worker calls valid terminating `subagent_report` with `outcome: completed`; the supervisor captures its details, then the child exits nonzero or emits a terminal model/protocol error before `agent_settled`.
scenarios.context: The report is a worker claim, while process and RPC events are supervisor observations.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: No self-reported success overrides an observed runtime failure, and useful summary/artifacts remain recoverable.
scenarios.title: Worker reports completion but the RPC process fails before settlement

scenarios.action: Write canonical terminal status `needs_attention`, enqueue the bounded summary/references, and leave retry or follow-up judgment to the top-level agent.
scenarios.body: The worker cannot safely finish but has useful findings or artifacts, so it calls `subagent_report` with `outcome: needs_attention` and settles normally.
scenarios.context: There is no process or protocol failure.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Partial work is neither discarded nor mislabeled as successful or failed infrastructure.
scenarios.title: Worker settles with useful partial work and needs attention

scenarios.action: The runtime retains only bounded normalized state, triggers idle/hard or output limits, sends RPC abort, escalates process-group termination, records a retryable or final timeout envelope, and applies policy without growing a log indefinitely.
scenarios.body: A child repeatedly emits message/tool updates and remains alive without reaching a terminal response.
scenarios.context: Raw event logging is disabled and the run is at its output/idle budget.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Disk and memory remain bounded; the DAG visibly shows timeout/failure and offers policy-allowed retry.
scenarios.title: A worker emits unbounded progress and stops making useful progress

scenarios.action: Run the bounded automatic report-only repair policy. If it is exhausted, write a terminal result with report status `missing` and canonical status `needs_attention`; do not infer task success or project-model authority from freeform prose.
scenarios.body: Pi emits final assistant `message_end` and `agent_settled`, but no valid `subagent_report` envelope was captured.
scenarios.context: The supervisor retained bounded final text, usage, model, stop reason, and report-attempt diagnostics.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Useful work remains inspectable without letting unstructured prose silently become a successful structured completion.
scenarios.title: A worker settles without calling the report tool

scenarios.body: After a material decision, Current understanding uses scannable adaptive Markdown to connect the user's goal, relevant current mechanism, and governing direction. It omits unrelated model facts and does not reproduce a fixed project-documentation template.
scenarios.title: Current understanding demonstrates selective synthesis

scenarios.body: A simple focus can produce a short structured synthesis with only the headings needed for comprehension. Runtime validation accepts it when content and source references are valid; tests do not require empty sections or a minimum heading count.
scenarios.title: A concise but meaningful synthesis is not rejected for shape

scenarios.body: When asking the user to choose how existing behavior should change, the brief explains the relevant current mechanism, the insufficiency or trigger, what materially changes across options, the recommendation, and the exact requested judgment. It does not begin and end with a description of the recommended option.
scenarios.title: A modification question explains why the decision exists

tensions.body: The older accepted widget requires live DAG state and conductor transitions. The newer accepted boundary says the subagent runtime must not own or infer those concepts and that DAG integration will be redesigned separately. Both goals can survive only by splitting a generic worker activity widget now from a later DAG adapter, or by deferring all UI until that adapter exists.
tensions.title: Accepted live DAG widget versus newer DAG-agnostic worker boundary

tensions.body: An explicit agent-only ack tool adds one call but binds a durable disposition to the stable completion ID; result integrity is checked internally and no hash is echoed by the agent. Automatic ack on `agent_settled` is simpler but cannot prove the worker outcome was actually handled, especially after aborts, failures, reloads, or partial side effects.
tensions.title: Explicit completion acknowledgement versus automatic settled acknowledgement

tensions.body: A minimal terminating report is reliable across worker roles and preserves DAG independence, but the top-level agent must interpret its prose. A rich report supports future automation, but burdens generic workers and prematurely encodes implementation/review/DAG concepts. Runtime-observed facts should remain outside either worker-authored schema.
tensions.title: Minimal generic report versus rich typed workflow report

tensions.body: More parallel nodes improve throughput only when they do not duplicate or prematurely freeze shared architecture decisions. Conservative serialization preserves coherence but can erase the DAG's value by making nearly every task sequential.
tensions.title: Parallel throughput versus architecture coherence

tensions.body: A passive widget plus commands is small, durable, and portable. An interactive graph/thread surface is more discoverable and powerful but adds substantial TUI complexity and pressure to retain more live transcript detail.
tensions.title: Passive DAG widget versus interactive FleetView

tensions.body: The accepted renderer boundary allows trusted agent-authored HTML, scripts, forms, and custom controls, but human authority requires that agent code cannot manufacture an eligible acceptance interaction. Lavish currently gives artifact scripts and visible controls the same queuePrompt channel with no trusted-gesture provenance. Preserving both unrestricted scripting and direct browser-to-authority resolution is therefore unsafe without another confirmation or protocol boundary.
tensions.title: Unrestricted rich context versus mechanically trustworthy authority input

tensions.body: The accepted session topology binds the top-level conductor to the current worktree and branch, while earlier safety analysis treated the initiating user worktree as observation-only. These are compatible only if the current directory is explicitly designated as the session/conductor worktree and conductor target updates use ordinary worktree-aware fast-forward operations with exact cleanliness/HEAD guards—never raw ref movement, stash, reset, clean, forced checkout, or silent branch switching.
tensions.title: The conductor worktree is user-visible but must also be the landing surface

tensions.body: The measured incident requires eliminating cumulative streaming-event persistence and bounding diagnostics. A broader baseline additionally makes all concurrency, timeout, token, cost, turn, output, and attempt limits finite from v1. The targeted option keeps conductor correctness mandatory but allows ordinary resource budgets to remain configurable.
tensions.title: Targeted amplification safety versus broad mandatory resource budgets

tensions.body: Keeping results with the launching session is deterministic and matches the accepted queue boundary but interrupts continuity after a fork. Automatic transfer follows the user's active branch but adds hidden ownership mutation and crash/concurrency hazards. Explicit adoption is visible but requires a new transfer protocol.
tensions.title: Worker continuity across forks versus strict session-local ownership

tensions.body: A subprocess RPC worker has stronger fault/resource isolation and exact CLI compatibility but higher startup and protocol cost. An in-process SDK worker avoids raw transport and disk I/O but shares failure/resource domains and currently has a public-API gap for reusing the parent extension's exact model runtime and custom providers.
tensions.title: Worker process isolation versus in-process SDK efficiency

tensions.body: Session-scoped cancellation no longer satisfies the accepted durability requirement. Detached per-run supervisors survive reload/exit through bounded durable state without a service, but require process identity, orphan reconciliation, and reconnect delivery. A daemon adds centralized durable scheduling and cross-session coordination at the cost of authenticated IPC and a separate lifecycle.
tensions.title: Session-scoped workers versus daemon durability

tensions.body: Question briefs and Current understanding need enough Markdown structure and contextual coverage to be readable project-model windows, but a rigid or exhaustive schema can turn the output into project documentation and obscure whether the agent can synthesize what actually matters.
tensions.title: Scannable structure versus performative template compliance
